212.s:
agnir uvāca
kāmyadānāni vakṣyāmi sarvakāma pradāni te /
nityapūjāṃ māsi māsi kṛtvātho kāmyapūjanaṃ //
212.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
काम्यदानानि वक्ष्यामि सर्वकाम प्रदानि ते /
नित्यपूजां मासि मासि कृत्वाथो काम्यपूजनं //
212.m: Agni said: / I will proclaim to you the gifts for desired ends, which grant all desires: / having performed the regular worship month by month, and then worship for desired ends,

212.s:
vratārhaṇaṃ guroḥ pūjā vatsarānte mahārcanaṃ /
aśvaṃ vai mārgaśairṣe tu kamalaṃ piṣṭasambhavaṃ //
212.d:
व्रतार्हणं गुरोः पूजा वत्सरान्ते महार्चनं /
अश्वं वै मार्गशैर्षे तु कमलं पिष्टसम्भवं //
212.m: offering for a votive observance, worship of the guru, and the great worship at the end of the year. / In Mārgaśīrṣa, whoever offers an horse, or a lotus made of meal,

212.s:
śivāya pūjya yo dadyāt sūryaloke ciraṃ vaset(1) /
:n
1 svargaloke ciraṃ vasediti ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , ṭa.. ca / śivaloke ciraṃ vasediti
jha..
:p 272
gajaṃ pauṣe piṣṭamayaṃ trisaptakulamuddharet //
212.d:
शिवाय पूज्य यो दद्यात् सूर्यलोके चिरं वसेत्(1) /
:न्
1 स्वर्गलोके चिरं वसेदिति ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. , ट.. च / शिवलोके चिरं वसेदिति
झ..
:प् 272
गजं पौषे पिष्टमयं त्रिसप्तकुलमुद्धरेत् //
212.m:
to Śiva, having worshipped him, will dwell in the realm of the Sun for a long time.
[Note]
[Footnote 1: "svargaloke ciraṃ vasediti" in manuscripts ga, gha, ṅa, and ṭa; "śivaloke ciraṃ vasediti" in jha. / Page 272]
In Pauṣa, [by giving] an elephant made of meal, one delivers twenty-one generations of one's lineage.

212.s:
māghe cāśvarathaṃ paiṣṭhaṃ dattvā narakaṃ vrajet /
phālgune tu vṛṣaṃ paiṣṭaṃ svargabhuk syānmahīpatiḥ //
212.d:
माघे चाश्वरथं पैष्ठं दत्त्वा नरकं व्रजेत् /
फाल्गुने तु वृषं पैष्टं स्वर्गभुक् स्यान्महीपतिः //
212.m: In Māgha, having given a horse-drawn chariot made of meal, one goes to hell. / But in Phālguna, [giving] a bull made of meal, one becomes an earthly ruler enjoying heaven.

212.s:
caitre cekṣumayīṃ gāvandāsadāsīsamanvitāṃ /
dattvā svarge ciraṃ sthitvā tadante syānmahīpatiḥ //
212.d:
चैत्रे चेक्षुमयीं गावन्दासदासीसमन्वितां /
दत्त्वा स्वर्गे चिरं स्थित्वा तदन्ते स्यान्महीपतिः //
212.m: In Caitra, having given a cow made of sugarcane together with male and female slaves, / having dwelt long in heaven, at the end thereof he becomes an earthly ruler.

212.s:
saptavrīhīṃś ca vaiśākhe dattvā śivamayo bhavet /
balimaṇḍalakañcānnaiḥ kṛtvāṣāḍhe śivo bhavet //
212.d:
सप्तव्रीहींश् च वैशाखे दत्त्वा शिवमयो भवेत् /
बलिमण्डलकञ्चान्नैः कृत्वाषाढे शिवो भवेत् //
212.m: Having given seven kinds of grain in Vaiśākha, he becomes identified with Śiva. / Having made a circular offering of food portions in Āṣāḍha, he becomes Śiva.

212.s:
vimānaṃ śrāvaṇe pauṣpaṃ dattvā svargī tato nṛpaḥ /
śatadvayaṃ phalānāntu dattvoddhṛtya kulaṃ nṛpaḥ //
212.d:
विमानं श्रावणे पौष्पं दत्त्वा स्वर्गी ततो नृपः /
शतद्वयं फलानान्तु दत्त्वोद्धृत्य कुलं नृपः //
212.m: Having given a celestial chariot made of flowers in Śrāvaṇa, one becomes a heavenly dweller and then a king. / Having given two hundred fruits, he delivers his lineage and becomes a king.

212.s:
guggulādi dahedbhādre svargī sa syāttato nṛpaḥ /
kṣīrasarpirbhṛtaṃ pātramāśvine svargadambhavet //
212.d:
गुग्गुलादि दहेद्भाद्रे स्वर्गी स स्यात्ततो नृपः /
क्षीरसर्पिर्भृतं पात्रमाश्विने स्वर्गदम्भवेत् //
212.m: One should burn bdellium and other incenses in Bhādra; he becomes a heavenly dweller, then a king. / A vessel filled with milk and clarified butter in Āśvina bestows heaven.

212.s:
kārttike guḍakhaṇḍājyaṃ dattvā svargī tato nṛpaḥ /
merudānaṃ dvādaśakaṃ vakṣye 'haṃ bhuktimuktidaṃ //
212.d:
कार्त्तिके गुडखण्डाज्यं दत्त्वा स्वर्गी ततो नृपः /
मेरुदानं द्वादशकं वक्ष्ये ऽहं भुक्तिमुक्तिदं //
212.m: In Kārttika, having given raw sugar, sugar candy, and clarified butter, one becomes a heavenly dweller and then a king. / I shall proclaim the twelvefold gift of Meru, granting worldly enjoyment and liberation.

212.s:
meruvrate tu kārttikyāṃ ratnamerundaded dvije /
sarveṣāñcaiva merūṇāṃ pramāṇaṃ kramaśaḥ śṛṇu //
212.d:
मेरुव्रते तु कार्त्तिक्यां रत्नमेरुन्ददेद् द्विजे /
सर्वेषाञ्चैव मेरूणां प्रमाणं क्रमशः शृणु //
212.m: In the Meru votive observance on the full moon of Kārttika, one should give a jewel-Meru to a brāhmaṇa. / Hear in succession the measure of all the Merus:

212.s:
vajrapadmamahānīlanīlasphaṭikasañjñitaḥ /
puṣpaṃ marakataṃ muktā prasthamātreṇa cottamaḥ //
212.d:
वज्रपद्ममहानीलनीलस्फटिकसञ्ज्ञितः /
पुष्पं मरकतं मुक्ता प्रस्थमात्रेण चोत्तमः //
212.m: named diamond, ruby, sapphire, blue gem, and quartz crystal; / the highest is [made with] a prastha measure of topaz, emerald, and pearls;

212.s:
madhyo 'rdhaḥ syāttadardho 'dho vittaśāṭhyaṃ vivarjayet /
kārṇikāyāṃ nyasenmeruṃ brahmaviṣṇvīśadaivataṃ //
212.d:
मध्यो ऽर्धः स्यात्तदर्धो ऽधो वित्तशाठ्यं विवर्जयेत् /
कार्णिकायां न्यसेन्मेरुं ब्रह्मविष्ण्वीशदैवतं //
212.m: the middling is half of that, and the lowest is half of that; one must avoid stinginess with wealth. / One should place Meru upon the pericarp, having Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva as its deities.

212.s:
mālyavān pūrvataḥ pūjyastatpūrve bhadarasañjñitaḥ /
aśvarakṣastataḥ prokto niṣadho merudakṣiṇe //
212.d:
माल्यवान् पूर्वतः पूज्यस्तत्पूर्वे भदरसञ्ज्ञितः /
अश्वरक्षस्ततः प्रोक्तो निषधो मेरुदक्षिणे //
212.m: Mālyavat should be worshipped to the east; east of that, the mountain named Bhadra; / then Aśvarakṣas is prescribed, and Niṣadha to the south of Meru;

212.s:
hemakūṭo 'tha himavān trayaṃ saumye tathā trayaṃ /
nīlaḥ śvetaś ca śṛṅgī ca paścime gandhamādanaḥ //
:p 273
212.d:
हेमकूटो ऽथ हिमवान् त्रयं सौम्ये तथा त्रयं /
नीलः श्वेतश् च शृङ्गी च पश्चिमे गन्धमादनः //
:प् 273
212.m:
then Hemakūṭa and Himavat—three [mountains]; similarly three to the north: / Nīla, Śveta, and Śṛṅgin; and Gandhamādana to the west;
[Page 273]

212.s:
vaikaṅkaḥ ketumālaḥ syānmerurdvādaśasaṃyutaḥ /
sopavāso 'rcayedviṣṇuṃ śivaṃ vā snānapūrvakaṃ //
212.d:
वैकङ्कः केतुमालः स्यान्मेरुर्द्वादशसंयुतः /
सोपवासो ऽर्चयेद्विष्णुं शिवं वा स्नानपूर्वकं //
212.m: Vaikaṅka and Ketumāla. [Thus] Meru is endowed with twelve [subsidiary mountains]. / Observing a fast, after bathing, one should worship Viṣṇu or Śiva,

212.s:
devāgre cārcya meruñca mantrair viprāya vai dadet /
viprāyāmukagotrāya merundravyamayamparaṃ //
212.d:
देवाग्रे चार्च्य मेरुञ्च मन्त्रैर् विप्राय वै ददेत् /
विप्रायामुकगोत्राय मेरुन्द्रव्यमयम्परं //
212.m: and having worshipped Meru before the god, he should give it to a brāhmaṇa with mantras: / 'To the brāhmaṇa of such-and-such lineage, this supreme Meru made of precious materials,

212.s:
bhuktyai muktyai nirmalatve viṣṇudaivaṃ dadāmi te /
indraloke brahmaloke śivaloke hareḥ pure //
212.d:
भुक्त्यै मुक्त्यै निर्मलत्वे विष्णुदैवं ददामि ते /
इन्द्रलोके ब्रह्मलोके शिवलोके हरेः पुरे //
212.m: for worldly enjoyment, for liberation, and for purity, belonging to deity Viṣṇu, I give to you.' / In Indra's realm, in Brahmā's realm, in Śiva's realm, or in Hari's city,

212.s:
kulamuddhṛtya krīḍeta vimāne devapūjitaḥ /
anyeṣvapi ca kāleṣu saṅkrāntyādau pradāpayet //
212.d:
कुलमुद्धृत्य क्रीडेत विमाने देवपूजितः /
अन्येष्वपि च कालेषु सङ्क्रान्त्यादौ प्रदापयेत् //
212.m: having delivered his lineage, he disports in a celestial chariot, worshipped by the gods. / At other times as well, such as at a solar transit, one should give it.

212.s:
palānāntu sahasreṇa hemamerumprakalpayet /
śṛṅgatrayasamāyuktaṃ brahmaviṣṇuharānvitaṃ //
212.d:
पलानान्तु सहस्रेण हेममेरुम्प्रकल्पयेत् /
शृङ्गत्रयसमायुक्तं ब्रह्मविष्णुहरान्वितं //
212.m: One should construct a gold Meru with a thousand palas, / endowed with three peaks and accompanied by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva.

212.s:
ekaikaṃ parvatantasya śataikaikena kārayet /
meruṇā saha śailāstu khyātāstatra trayodaśa //
212.d:
एकैकं पर्वतन्तस्य शतैकैकेन कारयेत् /
मेरुणा सह शैलास्तु ख्यातास्तत्र त्रयोदश //
212.m: One should make each of its [surrounding] mountains with a single hundred [palas]; / together with Meru, thirteen mountains are celebrated there.

212.s:
ayane grahaṇādau ca viṣṇvagre harimarcya ca /
svarṇameruṃ dvijāyārpya viṣṇuloke ciraṃ vaset //
212.d:
अयने ग्रहणादौ च विष्ण्वग्रे हरिमर्च्य च /
स्वर्णमेरुं द्विजायार्प्य विष्णुलोके चिरं वसेत् //
212.m: At a solstice, an eclipse, and other occasions, having worshipped Hari before Viṣṇu / and having presented the golden Meru to a brāhmaṇa, he dwells in the realm of Viṣṇu for a long time.

212.s:
paramāṇavo yāvanta iha rājā bhavecciraṃ /
raupyameruṃ dvādaśādriyutaṃ saṅkalpato dadet(1) //
212.d:
परमाणवो यावन्त इह राजा भवेच्चिरं /
रौप्यमेरुं द्वादशाद्रियुतं सङ्कल्पतो ददेत्(1) //
212.m: As many atoms as there are, for that long he becomes a king here. / With formal vow one should give a silver Meru accompanied by twelve mountains;

212.s:
prāguktaṃ ca phalaṃ tasya viṣṇuṃ vipraṃprapūjya ca /
bhūmimeruñca viṣayaṃ maṇḍalaṃ grāmameva ca(2) //
212.d:
प्रागुक्तं च फलं तस्य विष्णुं विप्रंप्रपूज्य च /
भूमिमेरुञ्च विषयं मण्डलं ग्राममेव च(2) //
212.m: and the fruit of that is as stated before. Having worshipped Viṣṇu and a brāhmaṇa, / [one may give] an earth-Meru: a district, a province, or a village,

212.s:
parikalpyāṣṭamāṃśena śeṣāṃśāḥ(3) pūrvavat phalaṃ /
dvādaśādrisamāyuktaṃ hastimerusvarūpiṇaṃ //
:n
1 saṅkalpya taddadediti ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , ña.. ca
2 maṇḍalaṃ grāmameveti ga.. , jha.. , ṭa.. ca
3 śeṣāṅgā iti kha..
:p 274
212.d:
परिकल्प्याष्टमांशेन शेषांशाः(3) पूर्ववत् फलं /
द्वादशाद्रिसमायुक्तं हस्तिमेरुस्वरूपिणं //
:न्
1 सङ्कल्प्य तद्ददेदिति ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. , ञ.. च
2 मण्डलं ग्राममेवेति ग.. , झ.. , ट.. च
3 शेषाङ्गा इति ख..
:प् 274
212.m:
having fashioned it, with an eighth part [for Meru] and the remaining parts [for the mountains]; the fruit is as before. / [Or one may give] the form of an elephant-Meru accompanied by twelve mountains;
[Note]
[Footnote 1: "saṅkalpya taddadediti" in manuscripts ga, gha, ṅa, and ña.]
[Footnote 2: "maṇḍalaṃ grāmameveti" in ga, jha, and ṭa.]
[Footnote 3: "śeṣāṅgā iti" in kha. / Page 274]

212.s:
dadettripuruṣair yuktaṃ dattvānantaṃ phalaṃ labhet /
tripañcāśvair aśvameruṃ hayayadvādaśasaṃyutaṃ //
212.d:
ददेत्त्रिपुरुषैर् युक्तं दत्त्वानन्तं फलं लभेत् /
त्रिपञ्चाश्वैर् अश्वमेरुं हययद्वादशसंयुतं //
212.m: one should give it accompanied by three persons; having given it, one obtains endless reward. / [Or] a horse-Meru with three and five horses, accompanied by twelve horses;

212.s:
viṣṇvādīn pūjya taṃ dattvā bhuktabhogo nṛpo bhavet /
aśvasaṅkhyāpramāṇena gomeruṃ pūrvavaddadet //
212.d:
विष्ण्वादीन् पूज्य तं दत्त्वा भुक्तभोगो नृपो भवेत् /
अश्वसङ्ख्याप्रमाणेन गोमेरुं पूर्ववद्ददेत् //
212.m: having worshipped Viṣṇu and the others and having given that, he becomes a king who has enjoyed pleasures. / One should give a cow-Meru as before, with the same measure as the number of horses.

212.s:
paṭṭavastrair bhāramātrair vastrameruś ca madhyataḥ /
śailair dvādaśavastraiś ca dattvā tañcākṣayaṃ phalaṃ //
212.d:
पट्टवस्त्रैर् भारमात्रैर् वस्त्रमेरुश् च मध्यतः /
शैलैर् द्वादशवस्त्रैश् च दत्त्वा तञ्चाक्षयं फलं //
212.m: And a cloth-Meru in the centre with silk clothes measuring a bhāra, / and mountains of twelve garments; having given that, [one obtains] imperishable reward.

212.s:
ghṛtapañcasahasraiś ca palānāmājyaparvataḥ /
śataiḥ pañcabhirekaikaḥ pārvate 'smin hariṃ yajet //
212.d:
घृतपञ्चसहस्रैश् च पलानामाज्यपर्वतः /
शतैः पञ्चभिरेकैकः पार्वते ऽस्मिन् हरिं यजेत् //
212.m: A clarified-butter mountain is made with five thousand palas of clarified butter; / each [surrounding mountain] is five hundred. On this mountain, one should worship Hari.

212.s:
viṣṇvagre brāhmaṇāyārpya sarvaṃ prāpya hariṃ vrajet /
evaṃ ca khaṇḍameruñca kṛtvā dattvāpnuyāt phalaṃ //
212.d:
विष्ण्वग्रे ब्राह्मणायार्प्य सर्वं प्राप्य हरिं व्रजेत् /
एवं च खण्डमेरुञ्च कृत्वा दत्त्वाप्नुयात् फलं //
212.m: Having offered it to a brāhmaṇa before Viṣṇu, having attained everything, he goes to Hari. / Having fashioned and given a sugar-candy Meru in this manner, one obtains the reward.

212.s:
dhānyameruḥ pañcakhāro 'para ekaikakhārakāḥ /
svarṇatriśṛṅgakāḥ sarve brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarān //
212.d:
धान्यमेरुः पञ्चखारो ऽपर एकैकखारकाः /
स्वर्णत्रिशृङ्गकाः सर्वे ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वरान् //
212.m: A grain-Meru is five khārīs, and the others are one khārī each, / all having three peaks of gold. Having worshipped Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara

212.s:
sarveṣu pūjya viṣṇuṃ vā viśeṣādakṣayaṃ phalaṃ /
evaṃ daśāṃśamānena tilameruṃ prakalpayet //
212.d:
सर्वेषु पूज्य विष्णुं वा विशेषादक्षयं फलं /
एवं दशांशमानेन तिलमेरुं प्रकल्पयेत् //
212.m: on all of them, or especially Viṣṇu, [the reward is] imperishable. / In this way, with a tenth part as the measure, one should fashion a sesame-seed Meru.

212.s:
śṛṅgāṇi pūrvavattasya tathaivānyanageṣu ca /
tilameruṃ pradāyātha bandhubhirviṣṇulokabhāk(1) //
212.d:
शृङ्गाणि पूर्ववत्तस्य तथैवान्यनगेषु च /
तिलमेरुं प्रदायाथ बन्धुभिर्विष्णुलोकभाक्(1) //
212.m: Its peaks are as before, and likewise on the other mountains. / Having given the sesame-seed Meru, he shares the realm of Viṣṇu together with his kinsmen.

212.s:
namo viṣṇusvarūpāya dharādharāya vai namaḥ /
brahmaviṣṇvīśaśṛṅgāya dharānābhisthitāya ca //
212.d:
नमो विष्णुस्वरूपाय धराधराय वै नमः /
ब्रह्मविष्ण्वीशशृङ्गाय धरानाभिस्थिताय च //
212.m: 'Obeisance to the support of the earth, whose form is Viṣṇu; indeed obeisance! / To him whose peaks are Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva, and who is situated at the navel of the earth,

212.s:
nagadvādaśanāthāya sarvapāpāpahāriṇe /
viṣṇubhaktāya śāntāya trāṇaṃ me kuru sarvathā //
212.d:
नगद्वादशनाथाय सर्वपापापहारिणे /
विष्णुभक्ताय शान्ताय त्राणं मे कुरु सर्वथा //
212.m: to the lord of the twelve mountains, who removes all sins, / devoted to Viṣṇu, peaceful: grant me protection in every way!

212.s:
niṣpāpaḥ pitṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ viṣṇuṃ gacchāmi oṃ namaḥ /
:n
1 bandhubhirbrahmalokabhāgiti jha..
:p 275
tvaṃ haristu hareragre ahaṃ viṣṇuś ca viṣṇave //
212.d:
निष्पापः पितृभिः सार्धं विष्णुं गच्छामि ओं नमः /
:न्
1 बन्धुभिर्ब्रह्मलोकभागिति झ..
:प् 275
त्वं हरिस्तु हरेरग्रे अहं विष्णुश् च विष्णवे //
212.m:
Free of sin, together with my ancestors, I go to Viṣṇu. Oṃ namaḥ!
[Note]
[Footnote 1: "bandhubhirbrahmalokabhāgiti" in manuscript jha. / Page 275]
You are Hari before Hari; I am Viṣṇu, and to Viṣṇu

212.s:
nivedayāmi bhaktyā tu bhuktimuktyarthahetave /
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe merudānāni nāma
dvādaśādhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha trayodaśādhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
pṛthvīdānāni
212.d:
निवेदयामि भक्त्या तु भुक्तिमुक्त्यर्थहेतवे /
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे मेरुदानानि नाम
द्वादशाधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ त्रयोदशाधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
पृथ्वीदानानि
212.m:
I offer [this] with devotion, for the sake of worldly enjoyment and liberation.'
Thus ends the two hundred and twelfth chapter, entitled "Gifts of Mount Meru", in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the two hundred and thirteenth chapter.
Gifts of the Earth

213.s:
agnir uvāca
pṛthvīdānaṃ pravakṣyāmi pṛthivī trividhā matā /
śatakoṭiryojanānāṃ saptadvīpā sasāgarā //
213.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
पृथ्वीदानं प्रवक्ष्यामि पृथिवी त्रिविधा मता /
शतकोटिर्योजनानां सप्तद्वीपा ससागरा //
213.m: Agni said: / I shall explain the gift of the earth; the earth is considered to be threefold: / a hundred crore yojanas in extent, having seven continents and oceans,

213.s:
jambudvīpāvadhiḥ sā ca uttamā medinīritā /
uttamāṃ pañcabhirbhāraiḥ kāñcanaiś ca prakalpayet //
213.d:
जम्बुद्वीपावधिः सा च उत्तमा मेदिनीरिता /
उत्तमां पञ्चभिर्भारैः काञ्चनैश् च प्रकल्पयेत् //
213.m: and extending to Jambūdvīpa—that is called the highest earth. / One should fashion the highest one with five bhāras of gold;

213.s:
tadardhāntarajaṃ kūrmaṃ tathā padmaṃ samādiśet /
uttamā kathitā pṛthvī dvyaṃśenaiva tu madhyamā //
213.d:
तदर्धान्तरजं कूर्मं तथा पद्मं समादिशेत् /
उत्तमा कथिता पृथ्वी द्व्यंशेनैव तु मध्यमा //
213.m: one should prescribe the tortoise and lotus inside it with half of that. / The highest earth has been declared; the middling one is with two parts.

213.s:
kanyasā ca tribhāgena(1) trihānyā kūrmapaṅkaje /
palānāntu sahasreṇa kalpayet kalpapādapaṃ //
213.d:
कन्यसा च त्रिभागेन(1) त्रिहान्या कूर्मपङ्कजे /
पलानान्तु सहस्रेण कल्पयेत् कल्पपादपं //
213.m: And the least [earth should be made] with a third part, reducing the tortoise and lotus by three. / One should fashion the wish-fulfilling tree with a thousand palas,

213.s:
mūladaṇḍaṃ sapatrañca phalapuṣpasamanvitaṃ /
:n
1 svalpā sā tu tribhāgeneti ṅa.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 276
pañcaskandhantu saṅkalpya pañcānāndāpayet sudhīḥ //
213.d:
मूलदण्डं सपत्रञ्च फलपुष्पसमन्वितं /
:न्
1 स्वल्पा सा तु त्रिभागेनेति ङ.. , ट.. च
:प् 276
पञ्चस्कन्धन्तु सङ्कल्प्य पञ्चानान्दापयेत् सुधीः //
213.m:
having a base, trunk, and leaves, and furnished with fruits and flowers.
[Note]
[Apparatus note on line 1]
Having fashioned it with five branches, the wise person should cause it to be given to five [brāhmaṇas].

213.s:
etaddātā brahmaloke pitṛbhirmodate ciraṃ /
viṣṇvagre kāmadhenuntu palānāṃ pañcabhiḥ śataiḥ //
213.d:
एतद्दाता ब्रह्मलोके पितृभिर्मोदते चिरं /
विष्ण्वग्रे कामधेनुन्तु पलानां पञ्चभिः शतैः //
213.m: The giver of this rejoices for a long time with his ancestors in the world of Brahmā. / In the presence of Viṣṇu, [one should give] a wish-granting cow [fashioned] with five hundred palas.

213.s:
brahmaviṣṇumaheśādyā devā dhenau vyavasthitāḥ /
dhenudānaṃ sarvadānaṃ sarvada brahmalokadaṃ //
213.d:
ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेशाद्या देवा धेनौ व्यवस्थिताः /
धेनुदानं सर्वदानं सर्वद ब्रह्मलोकदं //
213.m: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the other deities are situated within the cow. / The gift of a cow is [equal to] all gifts, granting all things, and granting the world of Brahmā.

213.s:
viṣṇvagre kapilāṃ dattvā tārayet sakalaṃ kulaṃ /
alaṅkṛtya striyaṃ dadyādaśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet(1) //
213.d:
विष्ण्वग्रे कपिलां दत्त्वा तारयेत् सकलं कुलं /
अलङ्कृत्य स्त्रियं दद्यादश्वमेधफलं लभेत्(1) //
213.m: Having given a brown cow before Viṣṇu, one delivers one's entire family. / Having adorned a maiden, one should give her; one obtains the fruit of an aśvamedha sacrifice.

213.s:
bhūmiṃ dattvā sarvabhāk syāt sarvaśasyaprarohiṇīm /
grāmaṃ vātha puraṃ vāpi(2) kheṭakañca dadt sukhī //
213.d:
भूमिं दत्त्वा सर्वभाक् स्यात् सर्वशस्यप्ररोहिणीम् /
ग्रामं वाथ पुरं वापि(2) खेटकञ्च दद्त् सुखी //
213.m: Having given land producing all crops, one enjoys all things. / Giving a village or even a city, or a market town, one becomes happy.

213.s:
kārttikyādau(3) vṛṣotsargaṃ kurvaṃstārayate kulaṃ(4) //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe pṛthvīdānāni nāma
trayodaśādhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha caturdaśādhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
mantramāhatmyakathanaṃ
213.d:
कार्त्तिक्यादौ(3) वृषोत्सर्गं कुर्वंस्तारयते कुलं(4) //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे पृथ्वीदानानि नाम
त्रयोदशाधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ चतुर्दशाधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
मन्त्रमाहत्म्यकथनं
213.m:
Performing the liberation of a bull on the full-moon day of Kārttika and other [times], one delivers one's family.
Thus ends the two hundred and thirteenth chapter, entitled 'Gifts of the Earth', in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the two hundred and fourteenth chapter:
Discourse on the Greatness of Mantras.

214.s:
agnir uvāca
nāḍīcakraṃ pravakṣyāmi yajjñānāj jñāyate hariḥ /
nābheradhastādyat kandamaṅkurāstatra nirgatāḥ //
:n
1 naramedhaphalaṃ labhediti ga.. , ṅa.. , ña.. ca
2 purīṃ vāpīti kha..
3 kārttikādāviti kha.. , ṭa.. ca
4 kurvan santārayet kulamiti ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 277
214.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
नाडीचक्रं प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञानाज् ज्ञायते हरिः /
नाभेरधस्ताद्यत् कन्दमङ्कुरास्तत्र निर्गताः //
:न्
1 नरमेधफलं लभेदिति ग.. , ङ.. , ञ.. च
2 पुरीं वापीति ख..
3 कार्त्तिकादाविति ख.. , ट.. च
4 कुर्वन् सन्तारयेत् कुलमिति ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. , ट.. च
:प् 277
214.m:
Agni said: / I shall declare the system of subtle channels, by the knowledge of which Hari is known. / Below the navel is a bulb from which sprouts emerge.
[Note]
[Apparatus note on verse 8]
[Apparatus note on verse 9]
[Apparatus notes on verse 10]

214.s:
dvāsaptatisahasrāṇi nābhimadhye vyavasthitāḥ /
tiryagūrdhvamadhaś caiva vyāptantābhiḥ samantataḥ //
214.d:
द्वासप्ततिसहस्राणि नाभिमध्ये व्यवस्थिताः /
तिर्यगूर्ध्वमधश् चैव व्याप्तन्ताभिः समन्ततः //
214.m: Seventy-two thousand [channels] are situated in the center of the navel. / The whole [body] is pervaded by them horizontally, upward, and downward on all sides.

214.s:
cakravatsaṃsthitā hy etāḥ pradhānā daśanāḍayaḥ /
iḍā ca piṅgalā caiva susumṇā ca tathaiva ca //
214.d:
चक्रवत्संस्थिता ह्य् एताः प्रधाना दशनाडयः /
इडा च पिङ्गला चैव सुसुम्णा च तथैव च //
214.m: Arranged like a wheel, ten of these channels are primary: / Iḍā, Piṅgalā, and likewise Suṣumnā,

214.s:
gāndhārī hastijihvā ca pṛthā caiva yathā tathā /
alambuṣā huhuś caiva śaṅkhinī daśamī smṛtā //
214.d:
गान्धारी हस्तिजिह्वा च पृथा चैव यथा तथा /
अलम्बुषा हुहुश् चैव शङ्खिनी दशमी स्मृता //
214.m: Gāndhārī, Hastijihvā, and likewise Pṛthā as well, / Alambuṣā, Huhū, and Śaṅkhinī is remembered as the tenth.

214.s:
daśa prāṇavahā hy etā nāḍayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ /
prāṇo 'pānaḥ samānaś ca udāno vyāna eva ca //
214.d:
दश प्राणवहा ह्य् एता नाडयः परिकीर्तिताः /
प्राणो ऽपानः समानश् च उदानो व्यान एव च //
214.m: These channels are proclaimed as carrying the ten vital breaths: / prāṇa, apāna, samāna, udāna, and vyāna,

214.s:
nāgaḥ kūrmo 'tha kṛkaro devadatto dhanañjayaḥ /
prāṇastu prathamo vāyurdaśānāmapi sa prabhuḥ //
214.d:
नागः कूर्मो ऽथ कृकरो देवदत्तो धनञ्जयः /
प्राणस्तु प्रथमो वायुर्दशानामपि स प्रभुः //
214.m: nāga, kūrma, kṛkara, devadatta, and dhanañjaya. / Prāṇa is the first wind, and he is the lord of all ten.

214.s:
prāṇaḥ prāṇayate prāṇaṃ visargāt pūraṇaṃ prati /
nityamāpūrayatyeṣa prāṇināmurasi sthitaḥ //
214.d:
प्राणः प्राणयते प्राणं विसर्गात् पूरणं प्रति /
नित्यमापूरयत्येष प्राणिनामुरसि स्थितः //
214.m: Prāṇa animates the breath from expiration to inspiration. / Situated in the chest of living beings, it constantly fills [them].

214.s:
niḥśvāsocchvāsakāsaistu prāṇo jīvasamāśritaḥ /
prayāṇaṃ kurute yasmāttasmāt prāṇaḥ prakīrtitaḥ //
214.d:
निःश्वासोच्छ्वासकासैस्तु प्राणो जीवसमाश्रितः /
प्रयाणं कुरुते यस्मात्तस्मात् प्राणः प्रकीर्तितः //
214.m: Prāṇa depends upon the individual soul through exhalations, inhalations, and coughing. / Because it makes departure (prayāṇa), it is called prāṇa.

214.s:
adho nayatyapānastu āhārañca nṛṇāmadhaḥ /
mūtraśukravaho vāyurapānastena kīrtitaḥ //
214.d:
अधो नयत्यपानस्तु आहारञ्च नृणामधः /
मूत्रशुक्रवहो वायुरपानस्तेन कीर्तितः //
214.m: Apāna carries downward; it carries the food of men down. / Because it is the wind carrying urine and semen, it is called apāna.

214.s:
pītabhakṣitamāghrātaṃ raktapittakaphānilaṃ /
samannayati gātreṣu samāno nāma mārutaḥ //
214.d:
पीतभक्षितमाघ्रातं रक्तपित्तकफानिलं /
समन्नयति गात्रेषु समानो नाम मारुतः //
214.m: The wind named samāna brings what is drunk, eaten, and smelled / to equilibrium in the limbs, along with blood, bile, phlegm, and wind.

214.s:
spandayatyadharaṃ vaktraṃ netrarāgaprakopanaṃ /
udvejayati marmāṇi udāno nāma mārutaḥ //
214.d:
स्पन्दयत्यधरं वक्त्रं नेत्ररागप्रकोपनं /
उद्वेजयति मर्माणि उदानो नाम मारुतः //
214.m: The wind named udāna causes the lower lip and mouth to quiver, / excites the redness of the eyes, and agitates the vital points.

214.s:
vyāno vināmayatyaṅgaṃ vyāno vyādhiprakopanaḥ /
pratidānaṃ tathā kaṇṭhādvyāpānādvyāna ucyate //
214.d:
व्यानो विनामयत्यङ्गं व्यानो व्याधिप्रकोपनः /
प्रतिदानं तथा कण्ठाद्व्यापानाद्व्यान उच्यते //
214.m: Vyāna bends the body; vyāna provokes disease. / From throat and from pervading (vyāpāna) it is called vyāna, [distributing] returns.

214.s:
udgāre nāga ity uktaḥ kūrmaśconmīlane sthitaḥ /
:p 278
kṛkaro bhakṣaṇe caiva devadatto vijṛmbhite //
214.d:
उद्गारे नाग इत्य् उक्तः कूर्मश्चोन्मीलने स्थितः /
:प् 278
कृकरो भक्षणे चैव देवदत्तो विजृम्भिते //

214.s:
dhanañjayaḥ sthito ghoṣe mṛtasyāpi na muñcati /
jīvaḥ prayāti daśadhā nāḍīcakraṃ hi tena tat //
214.d:
धनञ्जयः स्थितो घोषे मृतस्यापि न मुञ्चति /
जीवः प्रयाति दशधा नाडीचक्रं हि तेन तत् //
214.m: Dhanañjaya is situated in sound, and does not abandon even a dead person. / The individual soul moves in ten ways; therefore, it is indeed that system of channels.

214.s:
saṅkrāntirviṣuvañcaiva ahorātrāyanāni ca /
adhimāsa ṛṇañcaiva ūnarātra dhanantathā(1) //
214.d:
सङ्क्रान्तिर्विषुवञ्चैव अहोरात्रायनानि च /
अधिमास ऋणञ्चैव ऊनरात्र धनन्तथा(1) //
214.m: The planetary transit, the equinox, day and night, the solstices, / the intercalary month, the waning day, the subtracted day, and wealth:

214.s:
ūnarātraṃ bhaveddhikkā adhimāso vijṛmbhikā /
ṛṇañcātra bhavet kāso niśvāso dhanamucyate(2) //
214.d:
ऊनरात्रं भवेद्धिक्का अधिमासो विजृम्भिका /
ऋणञ्चात्र भवेत् कासो निश्वासो धनमुच्यते(2) //
214.m: The subtracted day is hiccup, the intercalary month is yawning, / the waning day is cough, and inhalation is called wealth.

214.s:
uttaraṃ dakṣiṇaṃ jñeyaṃ vāmaṃ dakṣiṇasañjñitaṃ /
madhye tu viṣuvaṃ proktaṃ puṭadvayaviniḥsmṛtaṃ //
214.d:
उत्तरं दक्षिणं ज्ञेयं वामं दक्षिणसञ्ज्ञितं /
मध्ये तु विषुवं प्रोक्तं पुटद्वयविनिःस्मृतं //
214.m: North and south are to be known, designated as left and right. / The equinox is declared to be in the center, emerging from both nostrils.

214.s:
saṅkrāntiḥ punarasyaiva svasthānāt sthānayogataḥ /
susumṇā madhyame hy aṅge iḍā vāme pratiṣṭhitā //
214.d:
सङ्क्रान्तिः पुनरस्यैव स्वस्थानात् स्थानयोगतः /
सुसुम्णा मध्यमे ह्य् अङ्गे इडा वामे प्रतिष्ठिता //
214.m: And the transit of this [breath occurs] from its own place by the conjunction of places. / Suṣumnā is fixed in the central limb, and Iḍā in the left,

214.s:
piṅgalā dakṣiṇe vipra ūrdhvaṃ prāṇo hy ahaḥ smṛtaṃ /
apāno rātrirevaṃ syādeko vāyurdaśātmakaḥ //
214.d:
पिङ्गला दक्षिणे विप्र ऊर्ध्वं प्राणो ह्य् अहः स्मृतं /
अपानो रात्रिरेवं स्यादेको वायुर्दशात्मकः //
214.m: Piṅgalā in the right, O brāhmaṇa. The upward prāṇa is known as day; / apāna is night in this way. The single wind consists of ten forms.

214.s:
āyāmo dehamadhyasthaḥ somagrahaṇamiṣyate /
dehātitattvamāyāmaṃ ādityagrahaṇaṃ viduḥ //
214.d:
आयामो देहमध्यस्थः सोमग्रहणमिष्यते /
देहातितत्त्वमायामं आदित्यग्रहणं विदुः //
214.m: Restraint stationed in the middle of the body is considered a lunar eclipse; / the restraint that transcends the elements of the body, they know as a solar eclipse.

214.s:
udaraṃ pūrayettāvadvāyunā yāvadīpsitaṃ /
prāṇāyāmī bhavedeṣa pūrakā dehapūrakaḥ //
214.d:
उदरं पूरयेत्तावद्वायुना यावदीप्सितं /
प्राणायामी भवेदेष पूरका देहपूरकः //
214.m: One should fill the abdomen with wind as long as desired. / This breath-control, the filler of the body, is the inhalation (pūraka).

214.s:
pidhāya sarvadvārāṇi niśvāsocchvāsavarjitaḥ /
sampūraṇakumbhavattiṣṭhet prāṇāyāmaḥ sa kumbhakaḥ //
214.d:
पिधाय सर्वद्वाराणि निश्वासोच्छ्वासवर्जितः /
सम्पूरणकुम्भवत्तिष्ठेत् प्राणायामः स कुम्भकः //
214.m: Having closed all the apertures, free from exhalation and inhalation, / one should remain like a filled jar; that breath-control is the retention (kumbhaka).

214.s:
muñcedvāyuṃ tatastūrdhvaṃ śvāsenaikena mantravit /
ucchvāsayogayuktaś ca vāyumūrdvaṃ virecayet //
:n
1 balantatheti ña..
2 balamucyate iti ña.. , jha.. ca
:p 279
214.d:
मुञ्चेद्वायुं ततस्तूर्ध्वं श्वासेनैकेन मन्त्रवित् /
उच्छ्वासयोगयुक्तश् च वायुमूर्द्वं विरेचयेत् //
:न्
1 बलन्तथेति ञ..
2 बलमुच्यते इति ञ.. , झ.. च
:प् 279
214.m:
Then the knower of mantras should release the wind upward in a single breath. / Connected with the application of exhalation, he should expel the wind upward.
[Note]
[Apparatus note on verse 35]
[Apparatus note on verse 36]

214.s:
uccarati svayaṃ yasmāt svadehāvasthitaḥ śivaḥ /
tasmāt tattvavidāñcaiva sa eva japa uccyate //
214.d:
उच्चरति स्वयं यस्मात् स्वदेहावस्थितः शिवः /
तस्मात् तत्त्वविदाञ्चैव स एव जप उच्च्यते //
214.m: Because Śiva, residing in one's own body, sounds forth spontaneously, / therefore that alone is called recitation by knowers of the truth.

214.s:
ayute dve sahasraikaṃ ṣaṭśatāni tathaiva ca /
ahorātreṇa yogīndro japasaṅkhyāṃ karoti saḥ //
214.d:
अयुते द्वे सहस्रैकं षट्शतानि तथैव च /
अहोरात्रेण योगीन्द्रो जपसङ्ख्यां करोति सः //
214.m: Twenty-one thousand and six hundred [times]: / that is the number of recitations the lord of yogins performs in a day and night.

214.s:
ajapā nāma gāyatrī brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarī /
ajapāṃ japate yastāṃ punarjanma na vidyate //
214.d:
अजपा नाम गायत्री ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वरी /
अजपां जपते यस्तां पुनर्जन्म न विद्यते //
214.m: The Gāyatrī named Ajapā is the sovereign of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva. / For one who recites that Ajapā, rebirth does not occur.

214.s:
candrāgniravisaṃyuktā ādyā kuṇḍalinī matā /
hṛtpradeśe tu sā jñeyā aṅkurākārasaṃsthitā //
214.d:
चन्द्राग्निरविसंयुक्ता आद्या कुण्डलिनी मता /
हृत्प्रदेशे तु सा ज्ञेया अङ्कुराकारसंस्थिता //
214.m: The primordial Kuṇḍalinī is considered to be joined with moon, fire, and sun. / She should be known in the heart region, situated in the form of a sprout.

214.s:
sṛṣṭinyāso bhavettatra sa vai sargāvalambanāt /
sravantaṃ cintayettasminnamṛtaṃ sāttvikottamaḥ //
214.d:
सृष्टिन्यासो भवेत्तत्र स वै सर्गावलम्बनात् /
स्रवन्तं चिन्तयेत्तस्मिन्नमृतं सात्त्विकोत्तमः //
214.m: Deposition of creation occurs there, resting indeed upon creation. / The best sattvic person should contemplate nectar flowing within it.

214.s:
dehasthaḥ sakalo jñeyo niṣphalo dehavarjitaḥ(1) /
haṃsahaṃseti yo brūyāddhaṃso devaḥ sadāśivaḥ //
214.d:
देहस्थः सकलो ज्ञेयो निष्फलो देहवर्जितः(1) /
हंसहंसेति यो ब्रूयाद्धंसो देवः सदाशिवः //
214.m: Dwelling in the body, it is known as qualified (sakala); free from the body, it is partless (niṣkala). / He who utters 'haṃsa haṃsa'—that Haṃsa is the god Sadāśiva.

214.s:
tileṣu ca yathā tailaṃ puṣpe gandhaḥ samaśritaḥ /
puruṣasya tathā dehe sa vāhyābhyantarāṃ sthitaḥ //
214.d:
तिलेषु च यथा तैलं पुष्पे गन्धः समश्रितः /
पुरुषस्य तथा देहे स वाह्याभ्यन्तरां स्थितः //
214.m: Just as oil resides in sesame seeds and fragrance in a flower, / so does he dwell outside and inside the body of the person.

214.s:
brahmaṇo hṛdaye sthānaṃ kaṇṭhe viṣṇuḥ samāśritaḥ /
tālumadhye(2) sthito rudro lalāṭe tu maheśvaraḥ //
214.d:
ब्रह्मणो हृदये स्थानं कण्ठे विष्णुः समाश्रितः /
तालुमध्ये(2) स्थितो रुद्रो ललाटे तु महेश्वरः //
214.m: Brahmā's place is in the heart; Viṣṇu rests in the throat; / Rudra is situated in the palate; and Maheśvara in the forehead.

214.s:
prāṇāgrantu śivaṃ vidyāttasyānte tu parāparaṃ /
pañcadhā sakalaḥ prokto viparītastu niṣphalaḥ //
214.d:
प्राणाग्रन्तु शिवं विद्यात्तस्यान्ते तु परापरं /
पञ्चधा सकलः प्रोक्तो विपरीतस्तु निष्फलः //
214.m: One should know Śiva at the tip of the breath, and at its end the supreme and non-supreme. / The qualified is declared to be fivefold; its reverse is the partless.

214.s:
prāsādaṃ nādamutthāpya śatatantu japedyadi /
ṣaṇmāsātsiddhimāpnoti yogayukto na saṃśayaḥ //
214.d:
प्रासादं नादमुत्थाप्य शततन्तु जपेद्यदि /
षण्मासात्सिद्धिमाप्नोति योगयुक्तो न संशयः //
214.m: Raising the prāsāda [mantra] and the sound (nāda), if one should recite it a hundred times, / joined with yoga, one attains perfection in six months without doubt.

214.s:
gamāgamasya jñānena sarvapāpakṣayo bhavet /
:n
1 dehapūjita iti kha.. , gha.. , cha.. ca
2 tālumūle iti kha..
:p 280
aṇimādiguṇaiśvaryaṃ ṣaḍbhirmāsair avāpnuyāt //
214.d:
गमागमस्य ज्ञानेन सर्वपापक्षयो भवेत् /
:न्
1 देहपूजित इति ख.. , घ.. , छ.. च
2 तालुमूले इति ख..
:प् 280
अणिमादिगुणैश्वर्यं षड्भिर्मासैर् अवाप्नुयात् //
214.m:
Through knowledge of the coming and going [of the breath], destruction of all sins takes place.
[Note]
[Apparatus note on verse 52]
[Apparatus note on verse 54]
In six months he obtains lordship endowed with qualities such as miniaturisation.

214.s:
sthūlaḥ sūkṣmaḥ paraśceti prāsādaḥ kathito mayā /
hrasvo dīrghaḥ plutaśceti prāsādaṃ lakṣayettridhā //
214.d:
स्थूलः सूक्ष्मः परश्चेति प्रासादः कथितो मया /
ह्रस्वो दीर्घः प्लुतश्चेति प्रासादं लक्षयेत्त्रिधा //
214.m: The prāsāda-mantra has been declared by me as gross, subtle, and supreme. / One should discern the prāsāda-mantra in three ways: short, long, and prolated.

214.s:
hrasvo dahati pāpāni dīrgho mokṣaprado bhavet /
āpyāyane plutaśceti mūrdhni vinduvibhūṣitaḥ //
214.d:
ह्रस्वो दहति पापानि दीर्घो मोक्षप्रदो भवेत् /
आप्यायने प्लुतश्चेति मूर्ध्नि विन्दुविभूषितः //
214.m: The short burns sins; the long bestows liberation; / and the prolated, adorned with a bindu on its crest, is for nourishment.

214.s:
ādāvante ca hrasvasya phaṭkāro māraṇe hitaḥ /
ādāvante ca hṛdayamākṛṣṭau samprakīrtitam //
214.d:
आदावन्ते च ह्रस्वस्य फट्कारो मारणे हितः /
आदावन्ते च हृदयमाकृष्टौ सम्प्रकीर्तितम् //
214.m: The sound 'phaṭ' at the beginning and the end of the short [syllable] is beneficial for slaying. / The heart-mantra at the beginning and the end is proclaimed for attraction.

214.s:
devasya dakṣiṇāṃ mūrtiṃ pañcalakṣaṃ sthito japet /
japānte ghṛtahomastu daśasāhasriko bhavet //
214.d:
देवस्य दक्षिणां मूर्तिं पञ्चलक्षं स्थितो जपेत् /
जपान्ते घृतहोमस्तु दशसाहस्रिको भवेत् //
214.m: Remaining steady, one should recite five hundred thousand times facing the southern icon of the god. / At the end of the recitation, a fire oblation of clarified butter should consist of ten thousand [offerings].

214.s:
evamāpyāyito mantro vaśyoccāṭādi kārayet /
ūrdhve śūnyamadhaḥ śūnyaṃ madhye śūnyaṃ nirāmayaṃ //
214.d:
एवमाप्यायितो मन्त्रो वश्योच्चाटादि कारयेत् /
ऊर्ध्वे शून्यमधः शून्यं मध्ये शून्यं निरामयं //
214.m: The mantra thus invigorated may effect subjugation, eradication, and the like. / Void above, void below, void in the middle, free from affliction—

214.s:
triśūnyaṃ yo vijānāti mucyate 'sau dhruvaṃ dvijaḥ /
prāsādaṃ yo na jānāti pañcamantramahātanuṃ //
214.d:
त्रिशून्यं यो विजानाति मुच्यते ऽसौ ध्रुवं द्विजः /
प्रासादं यो न जानाति पञ्चमन्त्रमहातनुं //
214.m: that twice-born man who knows the threefold void is surely liberated. / He who does not know the prāsāda-mantra, the great body consisting of five mantras,

214.s:
aṣṭatriṃśatkalāyuktaṃ na sa ācārya ucyate /
tathoṅkārañca gāyatrīṃ rudrādīn vettya.asau guruḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe mantramāhātmyaṃ nāma
caturdaśādhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:p 281
:ś atha pañcadaśādhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
sandhyāvidhiḥ
214.d:
अष्टत्रिंशत्कलायुक्तं न स आचार्य उच्यते /
तथोङ्कारञ्च गायत्रीं रुद्रादीन् वेत्त्य.असौ गुरुः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे मन्त्रमाहात्म्यं नाम
चतुर्दशाधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:प् 281
:श् अथ पञ्चदशाधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
सन्ध्याविधिः
214.m:
endowed with thirty-eight kalās, is not called an ācārya. / Likewise, he who knows the sound Oṃ, the Gāyatrī, and Rudra and the others, is a guru.
Thus in the great Purāṇa composed by Agni, the two hundred and fourteenth chapter, named 'The Greatness of the Mantra.'
[Page 281]
Now, the two hundred and fifteenth chapter:
The Rule for Twilight Devotions.

215.s:
agnir uvāca
oṅkāraṃ yo vijānāti sa yogī sa hariḥ pumān /
oṅkāramabhyasettasmānmṛnmantrasārantu sarvadaṃ //
215.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
ओङ्कारं यो विजानाति स योगी स हरिः पुमान् /
ओङ्कारमभ्यसेत्तस्मान्मृन्मन्त्रसारन्तु सर्वदं //
215.m: Agni said: / That man who knows the syllable Oṃ is a yogin; he is Hari. / Therefore, one should practice the syllable Oṃ, the essence of all mantras, all-bestowing.

215.s:
sarvamantraprayogeṣu praṇavaḥ prathamaḥ smṛtaḥ /
tena samparipūrṇaṃ yattat pūrṇaṃ karma netarat //
215.d:
सर्वमन्त्रप्रयोगेषु प्रणवः प्रथमः स्मृतः /
तेन सम्परिपूर्णं यत्तत् पूर्णं कर्म नेतरत् //
215.m: In all ritual applications of mantras, the praṇava is remembered as the first. / That rite which is completed by it is complete; no other is.

215.s:
oṅkārapūrvikāstisro mahāvyāhṛtayo 'vyayāḥ /
tripadā caiva sāvitrī vijñeyaṃ brahmaṇī mukhaṃ //
215.d:
ओङ्कारपूर्विकास्तिस्रो महाव्याहृतयो ऽव्ययाः /
त्रिपदा चैव सावित्री विज्ञेयं ब्रह्मणी मुखं //
215.m: The three immutable Great Utterances preceded by the syllable Oṃ / and the three-footed Sāvitrī are to be known as the mouth of the Veda.

215.s:
yo 'dhīte 'hanyahanyetāstrīṇi varṣāṇyatantritaḥ /
sa brahmaparamabhyeti vāyubhūtaḥ khamūrtimān //
215.d:
यो ऽधीते ऽहन्यहन्येतास्त्रीणि वर्षाण्यतन्त्रितः /
स ब्रह्मपरमभ्येति वायुभूतः खमूर्तिमान् //
215.m: He who recites these day after day for three years without slackening, / becomes of the nature of wind, embodied as space, and attains the supreme Brahman.

215.s:
ekākṣaraṃ paraṃ brahma prāṇāyāmaparantapaḥ /
sāvitryāstu parannāsti maunāt satyaṃ viśiṣyate //
215.d:
एकाक्षरं परं ब्रह्म प्राणायामपरन्तपः /
सावित्र्यास्तु परन्नास्ति मौनात् सत्यं विशिष्यते //
215.m: The single syllable is the supreme Brahman; prāṇāyāma is the supreme austerity. / There is nothing higher than the Sāvitrī; truth excels silence.

215.s:
saptāvartā pāpaharā daśabhiḥ prāpayeddivaṃ /
viṃśāvartā tu sā devī nayate hīśvarālayaṃ //
215.d:
सप्तावर्ता पापहरा दशभिः प्रापयेद्दिवं /
विंशावर्ता तु सा देवी नयते हीश्वरालयं //
215.m: Repeated seven times, she destroys sin; with ten, she causes one to reach heaven; / repeated twenty times, that goddess leads indeed to the abode of the Lord.

215.s:
aṣṭottaraśataṃ japtvā tīrṇaḥ saṃsārasāgarāt /
rudrakuṣmāṇḍajapyebhyo gāyatrī tu viśiṣyate //
215.d:
अष्टोत्तरशतं जप्त्वा तीर्णः संसारसागरात् /
रुद्रकुष्माण्डजप्येभ्यो गायत्री तु विशिष्यते //
215.m: Having recited it one hundred and eight times, one is carried across the ocean of worldly existence. / The Gāyatrī is superior even to recitations of the Rudra and the Kūṣmāṇḍa hymns.

215.s:
na gāyatryāḥ parañjapyaṃ na vyāhṛtisamaṃ hutaṃ /
gāyatryāḥ pādamapyardhamṛgardhamṛcameva vā //
215.d:
न गायत्र्याः परञ्जप्यं न व्याहृतिसमं हुतं /
गायत्र्याः पादमप्यर्धमृगर्धमृचमेव वा //
215.m: There is no recitation higher than the Gāyatrī; no fire oblation equal to the Utterances. / Even a single quarter of the Gāyatrī, or half, or half a verse, or a whole verse,

215.s:
brahmahatyā surāpānaṃ suvarṇasteyameva ca /
gurudārāgamaś caiva japyenaiva punāti sā //
:p 282
215.d:
ब्रह्महत्या सुरापानं सुवर्णस्तेयमेव च /
गुरुदारागमश् चैव जप्येनैव पुनाति सा //
:प् 282
215.m:
purifies by recitation alone [even from] the slaying of a brāhmaṇa, the drinking of liquor, / theft of gold, and violation of the guru's bed.
[Page 282]

215.s:
pāpe kṛte tilair homo gāyatrījapa īritaḥ /
japtvā sahasraṃ gāyatryā upavāsī sa pāpahā(1) //
215.d:
पापे कृते तिलैर् होमो गायत्रीजप ईरितः /
जप्त्वा सहस्रं गायत्र्या उपवासी स पापहा(1) //
215.m: When a sin is committed, a fire oblation with sesame seeds and recitation of the Gāyatrī are prescribed. / Fasting and having recited a thousand times the Gāyatrī, one destroys sin.

215.s:
goghnaḥ pitṛghno mātṛghno brahmahā gurutalpagaḥ /
brahmaghnaḥ svarṇahārī ca surāpo lakṣajapyataḥ //
215.d:
गोघ्नः पितृघ्नो मातृघ्नो ब्रह्महा गुरुतल्पगः /
ब्रह्मघ्नः स्वर्णहारी च सुरापो लक्षजप्यतः //
215.m: A cow-slayer, a father-slayer, a mother-slayer, a slayer of a brāhmaṇa, a violator of the guru's bed, / a murderer of a brāhmaṇa, a stealer of gold, and a drinker of liquor, through a recitation of a hundred thousand [times],

215.s:
śudhyate vātha vā snātvā śatamantarjale japet /
apaḥ śatena pītvā tu gāyatryāḥ pāpahā bhavet //
215.d:
शुध्यते वाथ वा स्नात्वा शतमन्तर्जले जपेत् /
अपः शतेन पीत्वा तु गायत्र्याः पापहा भवेत् //
215.m: is purified; or having bathed, one should recite a hundred times under water. / Drinking water with a hundred [recitations] of the Gāyatrī, one becomes a destroyer of sin.

215.s:
śataṃ japtā tu gāyatrī pāpopaśamanī smṛtā /
sahasraṃ śaptā sā devī upapātakanāśinī //
215.d:
शतं जप्ता तु गायत्री पापोपशमनी स्मृता /
सहस्रं शप्ता सा देवी उपपातकनाशिनी //
215.m: Recited a hundred times, the Gāyatrī is declared to appease sin; / recited a thousand times, that goddess destroys minor sins.

215.s:
abhīṣṭadā koṭijapyā devatvaṃ rājatāmiyāt /
oṅkāraṃ pūrvamuccārya bhūrbhuvaḥ svastathaiva ca //
215.d:
अभीष्टदा कोटिजप्या देवत्वं राजतामियात् /
ओङ्कारं पूर्वमुच्चार्य भूर्भुवः स्वस्तथैव च //
215.m: Recited ten million times, she grants desired wishes; one attains divinity or kingship. / Uttering the syllable Oṃ first, and likewise 'bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ',

215.s:
gāyatrī praṇavaścānte jape caivamudāhṛtaṃ /
viśvāmitra ṛṣicchando gāyatraṃ savitā tathā //
215.d:
गायत्री प्रणवश्चान्ते जपे चैवमुदाहृतं /
विश्वामित्र ऋषिच्छन्दो गायत्रं सविता तथा //
215.m: then the Gāyatrī, and the praṇava at the end: thus it is declared for recitation. / The seer is Viśvāmitra; the metre is Gāyatrī; the deity is Savitṛ;

215.s:
devatopanaye japye viniyogo hute tathā /
agnirvāyū ravirvidyut yamo jalapatirguruḥ //
215.d:
देवतोपनये जप्ये विनियोगो हुते तथा /
अग्निर्वायू रविर्विद्युत् यमो जलपतिर्गुरुः //
215.m: its ritual application is in initiation, recitation, and in fire oblation. / Agni, Vāyu, the Sun, Lightning, Yama, the Lord of Waters, Bṛhaspati,

215.s:
parjanya indro gandharvaḥ pūṣā ca tadanantaraṃ /
mitro 'tha varuṇastvaṣṭā vasavo marutaḥ śaśī //
215.d:
पर्जन्य इन्द्रो गन्धर्वः पूषा च तदनन्तरं /
मित्रो ऽथ वरुणस्त्वष्टा वसवो मरुतः शशी //
215.m: Parjanya, Indra, the Gandharva, and then Pūṣan, / Mitra, then Varuṇa, Tvaṣṭṛ, the Vasus, the Maruts, the Moon,

215.s:
aṅgirā viśvanāsatyau kas tathā sarvadevatāḥ /
rudro brahmā ca viṣṇuś ca kramaśo 'kṣaradevatāḥ //
215.d:
अङ्गिरा विश्वनासत्यौ कस् तथा सर्वदेवताः /
रुद्रो ब्रह्मा च विष्णुश् च क्रमशो ऽक्षरदेवताः //
215.m: Aṅgiras, the Viśvedevas, the two Nāsatyas, Ka, and all the gods, / Rudra, Brahmā, and Viṣṇu, are in sequence the deities of the syllables.

215.s:
gayatryā japakāle tu kathitāḥ pāpanāśanāḥ /
pādāṅguṣṭhau ca gulphau ca nalakau jānunī tathā //
215.d:
गयत्र्या जपकाले तु कथिताः पापनाशनाः /
पादाङ्गुष्ठौ च गुल्फौ च नलकौ जानुनी तथा //
215.m: At the time of recitation of the Gāyatrī, they are declared to destroy sin: / the two big toes, the ankles, the shins, and the two knees,

215.s:
jaṅghe śiśraś ca vṛṣaṇau kaṭir nābhistathodaraṃ /
:n
1 upapātakapāpaheti ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. ca
:p 283
stanau ca hṛdayaṃ grīvā mukhantālu ca nāsike //
215.d:
जङ्घे शिश्रश् च वृषणौ कटिर् नाभिस्तथोदरं /
:न्
1 उपपातकपापहेति ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. च
:प् 283
स्तनौ च हृदयं ग्रीवा मुखन्तालु च नासिके //
215.m:
the thighs, the penis, the testicles, the hips, the navel, and the abdomen,
[Note]
[Page 283]
the breasts, the heart, the neck, the mouth, the palate, and the two nostrils,

215.s:
cakṣuṣī ca bhruvormadhyaṃ lalāṭaṃ pūrvamānanaṃ /
dakṣiṇottarapārśve dve śira āsyamanukramāt //
215.d:
चक्षुषी च भ्रुवोर्मध्यं ललाटं पूर्वमाननं /
दक्षिणोत्तरपार्श्वे द्वे शिर आस्यमनुक्रमात् //
215.m: the two eyes, the space between the brows, the forehead, the east face, / the two flanks, south and north, the head, and the mouth in sequence.

215.s:
pītaḥ śyāmaś ca kapilo marakato 'gnisannibhaḥ /
rukmavidyuddhūmrakṛṣṇaraktagaurendranīlabhāḥ //
215.d:
पीतः श्यामश् च कपिलो मरकतो ऽग्निसन्निभः /
रुक्मविद्युद्धूम्रकृष्णरक्तगौरेन्द्रनीलभाः //
215.m: Yellow, dark, tawny, emerald-green, resembling fire; / having the luster of gold, lightning, smoke, black, red, pale white, and sapphire;

215.s:
sphāṭikasvarṇapāṇḍvābhāḥ padmarāgo 'khiladyutiḥ(1) /
hemadhūmraraktanīlaraktakṛṣṇasuvarṇabhāḥ //
215.d:
स्फाटिकस्वर्णपाण्ड्वाभाः पद्मरागो ऽखिलद्युतिः(1) /
हेमधूम्ररक्तनीलरक्तकृष्णसुवर्णभाः //
215.m: having the hues of crystal, gold, and pale white; ruby, of all-encompassing brilliance; / having the luster of gold, smoke, red, blue, reddish-black, and fine gold;

215.s:
śuklakṛṣṇapālāśābhā(2) gāyatryā varṇakāḥ kramāt /
dhyānakāle pāpaharā hutaiṣā sarvakāmadā //
215.d:
शुक्लकृष्णपालाशाभा(2) गायत्र्या वर्णकाः क्रमात् /
ध्यानकाले पापहरा हुतैषा सर्वकामदा //
215.m: and resembling white, black, and palāśa: these are the colors of the Gāyatrī in sequence. / At the time of meditation, she destroys sin; when offered as fire oblation, she grants all desires.

215.s:
gāyatryā tu tilair homaḥ sarvapāpapraṇāśanaḥ /
śāntikāmo yavaiḥ kuryādāyuṣkāmo ghṛtena ca //
215.d:
गायत्र्या तु तिलैर् होमः सर्वपापप्रणाशनः /
शान्तिकामो यवैः कुर्यादायुष्कामो घृतेन च //
215.m: A fire oblation with sesame seeds using the Gāyatrī destroys all sins. / One desiring pacification should offer with barley; one desiring longevity, with clarified butter;

215.s:
siddhārthakaiḥ karmasiddhyai payasā brahmavarcase /
putrakāmas tathā dadhnā dhānyakāmastu śālibhiḥ //
215.d:
सिद्धार्थकैः कर्मसिद्ध्यै पयसा ब्रह्मवर्चसे /
पुत्रकामस् तथा दध्ना धान्यकामस्तु शालिभिः //
215.m: with white mustard seeds for success in rites; with milk for Vedic splendour; / one desiring a son, with curds; one desiring grain, with rice paddy;

215.s:
kṣīravṛkṣasamiddhistu grahapīḍopaśāntaye /
dhanakāmas tathā bilvaiḥ śrīkāmaḥ kamalais tathā //
215.d:
क्षीरवृक्षसमिद्धिस्तु ग्रहपीडोपशान्तये /
धनकामस् तथा बिल्वैः श्रीकामः कमलैस् तथा //
215.m: with kindling sticks from milky trees for the pacification of planetary afflictions; / one desiring wealth, with bilva fruits; one desiring prosperity, with lotuses;

215.s:
ārogyakāmo dūrvābhirgurūtpāte sa eva hi /
saubhāgyecchurguggulunā vidyārthī pāyasena ca //
215.d:
आरोग्यकामो दूर्वाभिर्गुरूत्पाते स एव हि /
सौभाग्येच्छुर्गुग्गुलुना विद्यार्थी पायसेन च //
215.m: one desiring health, with dūrvā grass—the same during grave portents; / one wishing good fortune, with bdellium; and one seeking learning, with milk-rice.

215.s:
ayutenoktasiddhiḥ syāllakṣeṇa manasepsitaṃ /
koṭyā brahmabadhān muktaḥ kuloddhārī harirbhavet //
215.d:
अयुतेनोक्तसिद्धिः स्याल्लक्षेण मनसेप्सितं /
कोट्या ब्रह्मबधान् मुक्तः कुलोद्धारी हरिर्भवेत् //
215.m: With ten thousand, the stated attainment occurs; with a hundred thousand, that which is desired by the mind; / with ten million, freed from the slaughter of a brāhmaṇa, he elevates his lineage and becomes Hari.

215.s:
grahayajñamukho vāpi homo 'yutamukho 'rthakṛt /
:n
1 padmarāgo 'maladyutiriti kha.. , cha.. , ja.. , ṭa.. ca
2 śuklapadmapalāśābheti ṅa.. , ña.. ca
:p 284
āvāhanañca gāyatryāstata oṅkāramabhyaset //
215.d:
ग्रहयज्ञमुखो वापि होमो ऽयुतमुखो ऽर्थकृत् /
:न्
1 पद्मरागो ऽमलद्युतिरिति ख.. , छ.. , ज.. , ट.. च
2 शुक्लपद्मपलाशाभेति ङ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 284
आवाहनञ्च गायत्र्यास्तत ओङ्कारमभ्यसेत् //
215.m:
Either beginning with a sacrifice to the planets, or a fire oblation beginning with ten thousand [offerings], accomplishes one's purpose.
[Note]
1. Manuscripts kha, cha, ja, and ṭa read: "the ruby is of spotless lustre".
[Page 284]
And after invoking the Gāyatrī, one should practice the syllable Oṃ.

215.s:
smṛtvauṅkārantu gāyatryā nibadhnīyācchikhāntataḥ /
punarācamya hṛḍayaṃ nābhiṃ skandhau ca saṃspṛśet //
215.d:
स्मृत्वौङ्कारन्तु गायत्र्या निबध्नीयाच्छिखान्ततः /
पुनराचम्य हृडयं नाभिं स्कन्धौ च संस्पृशेत् //
215.m: Remembering the syllable Oṃ, one should tie one's topknot with the Gāyatrī; / sipping water again, one should touch the heart, the navel, and the two shoulders.

215.s:
praṇavasya ṛṣirbrahmā gāyatrīcchanda eva ca /
devo 'gniḥ paramātmā syādyogo vai sarvakarmasu //
215.d:
प्रणवस्य ऋषिर्ब्रह्मा गायत्रीच्छन्द एव च /
देवो ऽग्निः परमात्मा स्याद्योगो वै सर्वकर्मसु //
215.m: Of the praṇava, the seer is Brahmā, the metre is Gāyatrī, / the deity is Agni, the Supreme Self, and its application is in all rites.

215.s:
śuklā cāgnimukhī devyā kātyāyanasagotrajā /
trailokyavaraṇā divyā pṛthivyādhārasaṃyutā //
215.d:
शुक्ला चाग्निमुखी देव्या कात्यायनसगोत्रजा /
त्रैलोक्यवरणा दिव्या पृथिव्याधारसंयुता //
215.m: She is white, fire-faced, born of the lineage of Kātyāyana, / chosen by the three worlds, divine, having the earth as her support,

215.s:
akṣarasūtradharā devī padmāsanagatā śubhā /
oṃ tejo 'si maho 'si balamasi bhrājo 'si devānāndhāmanāmāsi / viśvamasi
viśvāyuḥ sarvamasi sarvāyuḥ oṃ abhi bhūḥ
āgaccha varade devi japye me sannidhau bhava //
215.d:
अक्षरसूत्रधरा देवी पद्मासनगता शुभा /
ओं तेजो ऽसि महो ऽसि बलमसि भ्राजो ऽसि देवानान्धामनामासि / विश्वमसि
विश्वायुः सर्वमसि सर्वायुः ओं अभि भूः
आगच्छ वरदे देवि जप्ये मे सन्निधौ भव //
215.m:
holding an akṣasūtra rosary, auspicious, seated upon a lotus seat:
'Oṃ, you are brilliance, you are majesty, you are strength, you are splendor, you are the abode and the name of the gods. You are all, all-life; you are everything, the lifespan of all. Oṃ, become manifest!'
'Come, O boon-granting goddess; be present at my recitation!'

215.s:
vyāhṛtīnāntu sarvāsāmṛṣireva prajāpatiḥ /
vyastāś caiva samastāś ca brāhmamakṣaramomiti //
215.d:
व्याहृतीनान्तु सर्वासामृषिरेव प्रजापतिः /
व्यस्ताश् चैव समस्ताश् च ब्राह्ममक्षरमोमिति //
215.m: Of all the Utterances, the seer is indeed Prajāpati, / whether separated or united, and of the syllable 'Oṃ', the immutable Brahman.

215.s:
viśvāmitro yamadagnirbharadvājo 'tha gotamaḥ /
ṛṣiratrirvaśiṣṭhaś ca kāśyapaś ca yathākramaṃ //
215.d:
विश्वामित्रो यमदग्निर्भरद्वाजो ऽथ गोतमः /
ऋषिरत्रिर्वशिष्ठश् च काश्यपश् च यथाक्रमं //
215.m:
Viśvāmitra, Jamadagni, Bharadvāja, Gotama,
Atri as the seer, Vasiṣṭha, and Kāśyapa, in order.

215.s:
agnirvāyū raviś caiva vākpatirvaruṇas tathā /
indro viṣṇurvyāhṛtīnāṃ daivatāni yathākramaṃ //
215.d:
अग्निर्वायू रविश् चैव वाक्पतिर्वरुणस् तथा /
इन्द्रो विष्णुर्व्याहृतीनां दैवतानि यथाक्रमं //
215.m:
Agni, Vāyu, Ravi, Vākpati, Varuṇa,
Indra, and Viṣṇu are the deities of the [seven] vyāhṛtis, in order.

215.s:
gāyatryaṣṭiganuṣṭup ca vṛhatī paṅktireva ca /
triṣṭup ca jagatī ceti chandāṃsyāhuranuktāmāt //
215.d:
गायत्र्यष्टिगनुष्टुप् च वृहती पङ्क्तिरेव च /
त्रिष्टुप् च जगती चेति छन्दांस्याहुरनुक्तामात् //
215.m:
Gāyatrī, Uṣṇih, Anuṣṭubh, Bṛhatī, Paṅkti,
Triṣṭubh, and Jagatī are declared to be the meters in the same order.

215.s:
viniyoge vyāhṛtīnāṃ prāṇāyāme ca homake /
āpohiṣṭhetyṛcā cāpāndrupadādīti vā smṛtā(1) //
:n
1 drupadādīni vāpyṛcā iti ṅa.. , ja.. , ña.. ca
:p 285
215.d:
विनियोगे व्याहृतीनां प्राणायामे च होमके /
आपोहिष्ठेत्यृचा चापान्द्रुपदादीति वा स्मृता(1) //
:न्
1 द्रुपदादीनि वाप्यृचा इति ङ.. , ज.. , ञ.. च
:प् 285
215.m:
In the application of the vyāhṛtis, in breath-control, and in fire oblation,
and with the water hymn beginning "āpo hi ṣṭhā", or that beginning with "drupadād iva",
[Note]
[Footnote 1: "or with the verse drupadādīni" in manuscripts ṅa, ja, and ña. Page 285.]

215.s:
tathā hiraṇyavarṇābhiḥ pāvamānībhirantataḥ /
vipruṣo 'ṣṭau kṣipedūrdhvamājanmakṛtapāpajit //
215.d:
तथा हिरण्यवर्णाभिः पावमानीभिरन्ततः /
विप्रुषो ऽष्टौ क्षिपेदूर्ध्वमाजन्मकृतपापजित् //
215.m:
likewise with the verses beginning "hiraṇyavarṇāḥ" and with the purifying pāvamānī verses at the end,
one should sprinkle eight drops upward, conquering sin committed from birth.

215.s:
antarjale ṛtañceti upettriraghamarṣaṇaṃ /
āpohiṣṭhetyṛco 'syāś ca sindhudvīpa ṛṣiḥ smṛtaḥ //
215.d:
अन्तर्जले ऋतञ्चेति उपेत्त्रिरघमर्षणं /
आपोहिष्ठेत्यृचो ऽस्याश् च सिन्धुद्वीप ऋषिः स्मृतः //
215.m:
Underwater, [reciting] the verse "ṛtañ ca", one should perform the Aghamarṣaṇa rite.
And for this verse beginning "āpo hi ṣṭhā", Sindhudvīpa is taught as the seer.

215.s:
brahmasnānāya chando 'sya gāyatrī devatā jalaṃ /
mārjane viniyogasya hayāvabhṛthake kratoḥ //
215.d:
ब्रह्मस्नानाय छन्दो ऽस्य गायत्री देवता जलं /
मार्जने विनियोगस्य हयावभृथके क्रतोः //
215.m:
For the Brahma-ablution, its meter is Gāyatrī, the deity is water,
and its application is in sprinkling at the concluding ablution of the horse sacrifice.

215.s:
aghamarṣaṇasūktasya ṛṣirevāghamarṣaṇaṃ /
anuṣṭup ca bhavecchando bhāvavṛttastu daivataṃ //
215.d:
अघमर्षणसूक्तस्य ऋषिरेवाघमर्षणं /
अनुष्टुप् च भवेच्छन्दो भाववृत्तस्तु दैवतं //
215.m:
Of the Aghamarṣaṇa hymn, Aghamarṣaṇa himself is the seer,
the meter is Anuṣṭubh, and Bhāvavṛtta is the deity.

215.s:
āpījyorīrasa iti gāyatryāstu śiraḥ smṛtaṃ /
ṛṣiḥ prajāpatistasya chandohīnaṃ yajuryataḥ //
215.d:
आपीज्योरीरस इति गायत्र्यास्तु शिरः स्मृतं /
ऋषिः प्रजापतिस्तस्य छन्दोहीनं यजुर्यतः //
215.m:
"āpo jyotī raso 'mṛtam" is taught as the head of the Gāyatrī.
Its seer is Prajāpati; it is devoid of meter because it is a Yajus formula.

215.s:
brahmāgnivāyusūryāś ca devatāḥ parikīrtitāḥ /
prāṇarodhāttu vāyuḥ syādvāyoragniś ca jāyate //
215.d:
ब्रह्माग्निवायुसूर्याश् च देवताः परिकीर्तिताः /
प्राणरोधात्तु वायुः स्याद्वायोरग्निश् च जायते //
215.m:
Brahmā, Agni, Vāyu, and Sūrya are declared to be its deities.
From breath-retention, wind arises; from wind, fire is produced;

215.s:
agnerāpastataḥ śuddhistataścācamanañcaret /
antaś carati bhūteṣu guhāyāṃ viśvamūrtiṣu //
215.d:
अग्नेरापस्ततः शुद्धिस्ततश्चाचमनञ्चरेत् /
अन्तश् चरति भूतेषु गुहायां विश्वमूर्तिषु //
215.m:
from fire, waters, and thence purity; therefore one should perform sipping of water.
It moves within beings, in the cave of the heart, in all forms,

215.s:
tapoyajñavaṣaṭkāra āpo jyotī raso 'mṛtaṃ /
udutyaṃ jātavedasamṛṣiḥ praṣkanna ucyate //
215.d:
तपोयज्ञवषट्कार आपो ज्योती रसो ऽमृतं /
उदुत्यं जातवेदसमृषिः प्रष्कन्न उच्यते //
215.m:
ascetic austerity, sacrifice, the vaṣaṭ-call: "waters, light, essence, nectar."
For the hymn "ud u tyaṃ jātavedasam", Praṣkaṇva is declared the seer;

215.s:
gāyatrīcchanda ākhyātaṃ sūryaś caiva tu daivatam /
atirātre niyogaḥ syādagnīṣomo niyogakaḥ //
215.d:
गायत्रीच्छन्द आख्यातं सूर्यश् चैव तु दैवतम् /
अतिरात्रे नियोगः स्यादग्नीषोमो नियोगकः //
215.m:
the meter is proclaimed as Gāyatrī, and Sūrya is the deity.
Its application is in the Atirātra sacrifice, and Agnīṣoma is the presiding divinity.

215.s:
citraṃ deveti ṛcake ṛṣiḥ kautsa udāhṛtaḥ /
triṣṭup chando daivatañca sūryo 'syāḥ parikīrtitaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe sandhyāvidhirnāma
pañcadaśādhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:p 286
:ś atha ṣoḍaśādhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
gāyatrīnirvāṇaṃ
215.d:
चित्रं देवेति ऋचके ऋषिः कौत्स उदाहृतः /
त्रिष्टुप् छन्दो दैवतञ्च सूर्यो ऽस्याः परिकीर्तितं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे सन्ध्याविधिर्नाम
पञ्चदशाधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:प् 286
:श् अथ षोडशाधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
गायत्रीनिर्वाणं
215.m:
In the verse "citraṃ devānām", Kautsa is cited as the seer;
Triṣṭubh is the meter, and Sūrya is proclaimed as its deity.
Thus ends the two hundred and fifteenth chapter, named 'The Rule of Twilight Worship', in the great Agni Purāṇa.
[Page 286]
Now begins the two hundred and sixteenth chapter.
The Ultimate Essence of the Gāyatrī.

216.s:
agnir uvāca
evaṃ sandhyāvidhiṃ kṛtvā gāyatrīñca japet smaret /
gāyañcchiṣyān yatastrāyet bhāryāṃ prāṇāṃstathaiva ca(1) //
216.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
एवं सन्ध्याविधिं कृत्वा गायत्रीञ्च जपेत् स्मरेत् /
गायञ्च्छिष्यान् यतस्त्रायेत् भार्यां प्राणांस्तथैव च(1) //

216.s:
tataḥ smṛteyaṃ gāyatrī sāvitrīya tato yataḥ /
prakāśanātsā saviturvāgrūpatvāt sarasvatī //
216.d:
ततः स्मृतेयं गायत्री सावित्रीय ततो यतः /
प्रकाशनात्सा सवितुर्वाग्रूपत्वात् सरस्वती //
216.m:
it is therefore remembered as Gāyatrī; and it is remembered as Sāvitrī because it proceeds
from the illumination of Savitṛ; and as Sarasvatī because it consists of speech.

216.s:
taj jyotiḥ paramaṃ brahma bhargastejo yataḥ smṛtaṃ /
bhā dīptāviti rūpaṃ hi bhrasjaḥ pāke 'tha tat smṛtaṃ //
216.d:
तज् ज्योतिः परमं ब्रह्म भर्गस्तेजो यतः स्मृतं /
भा दीप्ताविति रूपं हि भ्रस्जः पाके ऽथ तत् स्मृतं //
216.m:
That light is the supreme Brahman, since bhargas is remembered as radiance;
for it has the form derived from the verbal root bhā, 'to shine', or it is remembered from the root bhrasj, 'to cook [or ripen]'.

216.s:
oṣadhyādikaṃ pacati bhrājṛ dīptau tathā bhavet /
bhargaḥ syād bhrājata iti bahulaṃ chanda īritaṃ //
216.d:
ओषध्यादिकं पचति भ्राजृ दीप्तौ तथा भवेत् /
भर्गः स्याद् भ्राजत इति बहुलं छन्द ईरितं //
216.m:
It ripens herbs and the like; it can likewise be from bhrāj, 'to shine'.
'Bhargas' is derived as 'that which shines'; the Vedic usage is diverse.

216.s:
vareṇyaṃ sarvatejobhyaḥ śreṣṭhaṃ vai paramaṃ padaṃ /
svargāpavargakāmair vā varaṇīyaṃ sadaiva hi //
216.d:
वरेण्यं सर्वतेजोभ्यः श्रेष्ठं वै परमं पदं /
स्वर्गापवर्गकामैर् वा वरणीयं सदैव हि //
216.m:
'Vareṇya' [means] superior to all lights, indeed the highest state,
or that which is ever to be chosen by those desiring heaven and liberation.

Because the root vṛ means 'to choose', [it is that which is] devoid of waking, dreaming, and the rest;
eternal, pure, conscious, one, and true: upon that Lord we meditate ('dhīmahi').

216.s:
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotirdhyayemahi vimuktaye /
taj jyotirbhagavān viṣṇurjagajjanmādikāraṇaṃ //
216.d:
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिर्ध्ययेमहि विमुक्तये /
तज् ज्योतिर्भगवान् विष्णुर्जगज्जन्मादिकारणं //
216.m:
'I am Brahman, the supreme light'—we should meditate for final liberation.
That light is the Blessed Lord Viṣṇu, the cause of the creation and other states of the universe.

216.s:
śivaṃ kecit paṭhanti sma śaktirūpaṃ paṭhanti ca /
kecit sūryaṅkecidagniṃ vedagā agnihotriṇaḥ //
:n
1 kāyān prāṇāṃstathaiva ceti ña..
:p 287
216.d:
शिवं केचित् पठन्ति स्म शक्तिरूपं पठन्ति च /
केचित् सूर्यङ्केचिदग्निं वेदगा अग्निहोत्रिणः //
:न्
1 कायान् प्राणांस्तथैव चेति ञ..
:प् 287
216.m:
Some recite it as Śiva, and some recite it as the embodiment of Śakti;
some as the Sun, and some as Agni, being knowers of the Veda and keepers of the sacrificial fire.
[Note]
[Page 287]

216.s:
agnyādirūpo viṣṇurhi vedādau brahma gīyate /
tat padaṃ paramaṃ viṣṇordevasya savituḥ smṛtaṃ //
216.d:
अग्न्यादिरूपो विष्णुर्हि वेदादौ ब्रह्म गीयते /
तत् पदं परमं विष्णोर्देवस्य सवितुः स्मृतं //
216.m:
Viṣṇu, possessing the forms of Agni and the rest, is sung as Brahman at the beginning of the Vedas.
That supreme abode of Viṣṇu is commemorated as belonging to the divine Savitṛ.

216.s:
mahadājyaṃ sūyate hi svayaṃ jyotirhariḥ prabhuḥ /
parjanyo vāyurādityaḥ śītoṣṇādyaiś ca pācayet //
216.d:
महदाज्यं सूयते हि स्वयं ज्योतिर्हरिः प्रभुः /
पर्जन्यो वायुरादित्यः शीतोष्णाद्यैश् च पाचयेत् //
216.m:
Indeed, the great oblation is produced; Lord Hari is self-luminous.
Becoming Parjanya, Vāyu, and the Sun, he ripens [all things] through cold, heat, and the rest.

216.s:
agnau prāstāhutiḥ samyagādityamupatiṣṭhate /
ādityājjāyate vṛṣṭirvṛṣṭerannantataḥ prajāḥ //
216.d:
अग्नौ प्रास्ताहुतिः सम्यगादित्यमुपतिष्ठते /
आदित्याज्जायते वृष्टिर्वृष्टेरन्नन्ततः प्रजाः //
216.m:
An offering cast properly into the fire approaches the sun;
from the sun rain is born, from rain food, and thence living beings.

216.s:
dadhātervā dhīmahīti manasā dhārayemahi /
no 'smākaṃ yaś ca bhargaś ca sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ dhiyaḥ //
216.d:
दधातेर्वा धीमहीति मनसा धारयेमहि /
नो ऽस्माकं यश् च भर्गश् च सर्वेषां प्राणिनां धियः //
216.m:
Or 'dhīmahi' is from the root dhā, 'to place'—we hold [it] with the mind.
'Nah' means 'our'; and whichever radiance [directs] the intellects of all living beings,

216.s:
codayāt prerayed buddhīrbhoktṝṇāṃ sarvakarmasu /
dṛṣṭādṛṣṭavipākeṣu viṣṇusūryāgnirūpavān //
216.d:
चोदयात् प्रेरयेद् बुद्धीर्भोक्तॄणां सर्वकर्मसु /
दृष्टादृष्टविपाकेषु विष्णुसूर्याग्निरूपवान् //
216.m:
may he impel ('pracodayāt')—may he direct the intellects of the experiencers in all activities
involving seen and unseen karmic fruitions, having the form of Viṣṇu, the Sun, and Agni.

216.s:
īśvaraprerito gacchet svargaṃ vāśvabhrameva vā /
īśāvāsyamidaṃ sarvaṃ mahadādijagaddhariḥ //
216.d:
ईश्वरप्रेरितो गच्छेत् स्वर्गं वाश्वभ्रमेव वा /
ईशावास्यमिदं सर्वं महदादिजगद्धरिः //
216.m:
Impelled by the Lord, one goes to heaven or indeed to the pit [of hell].
All this is enveloped by the Lord; the universe, beginning with the cosmic intellect, is Hari.

216.s:
svargādyaiḥ krīḍate devo yo 'haṃ sa puruṣaḥ prabhuḥ /
ādityāntargataṃ yacca bhargākhyaṃ vai mumukṣubhiḥ //
216.d:
स्वर्गाद्यैः क्रीडते देवो यो ऽहं स पुरुषः प्रभुः /
आदित्यान्तर्गतं यच्च भर्गाख्यं वै मुमुक्षुभिः //
216.m:
The God plays by means of heaven and the rest; that Person, the Lord, is I.
And that which is within the sun, called 'bhargas', by seekers of liberation,

216.s:
janmamṛtyuvināśāya duḥkhasya trividhasya ca /
dhyānena puruṣo 'yañca draṣṭavyaḥ sūryamaṇḍale //
216.d:
जन्ममृत्युविनाशाय दुःखस्य त्रिविधस्य च /
ध्यानेन पुरुषो ऽयञ्च द्रष्टव्यः सूर्यमण्डले //
216.m:
for the destruction of birth and death, and of the threefold suffering,
this Person is to be seen in the solar disc through meditation.

216.s:
tattvaṃ sadasi cidbrahma viṣṇoryat paramaṃ padaṃ /
devasya saviturbhargo vareṇyaṃ hi turīyakaṃ //
216.d:
तत्त्वं सदसि चिद्ब्रह्म विष्णोर्यत् परमं पदं /
देवस्य सवितुर्भर्गो वरेण्यं हि तुरीयकं //
216.m:
'Thou art That, the real, consciousness-Brahman, which is the supreme abode of Viṣṇu,
the radiance of the divine Savitṛ, the supreme, the fourth state.'

216.s:
dehādijāgradābrahma ahaṃ brahmeti dhīmahi /
yo 'sāvādityapuruṣaḥ so 'sāvahamananta oṃ //
216.d:
देहादिजाग्रदाब्रह्म अहं ब्रह्मेति धीमहि /
यो ऽसावादित्यपुरुषः सो ऽसावहमनन्त ओं //
216.m:
From the body up to the waking state and up to Brahman, we meditate: 'I am Brahman.'
He who is that Person in the sun, that am I, the infinite, Om.

216.s:
jñānāni śubhakarmādīn pravartayati yaḥ sadā //19//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe gāyatrīnirvāṇaṃ nāma
ṣoḍaśādhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:p 288
:ś atha saptadaśādhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
gāyatrīnirvāṇaṃ
216.d:
ज्ञानानि शुभकर्मादीन् प्रवर्तयति यः सदा //19//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे गायत्रीनिर्वाणं नाम
षोडशाधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:प् 288
:श् अथ सप्तदशाधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
गायत्रीनिर्वाणं
216.m:
He who ever stimulates kinds of knowledge, auspicious deeds, and the like. // 19
Thus ends the two hundred and sixteenth chapter, named 'The Ultimate Essence of the Gāyatrī', in the great Agni Purāṇa.
[Page 288]
Now begins the two hundred and seventeenth chapter.
The Ultimate Essence of the Gāyatrī.

217.s:
agnir uvāca
liṅgamūrtiṃ śivaṃ stutvā gāyatryā yogamāptavān /
nirvāṇaṃ(1) paramaṃ brahma vasiṣṭho 'nyaś ca śaṅkarāt(2) //
217.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
लिङ्गमूर्तिं शिवं स्तुत्वा गायत्र्या योगमाप्तवान् /
निर्वाणं(1) परमं ब्रह्म वसिष्ठो ऽन्यश् च शङ्करात्(2) //
217.m:
Agni said:
Having praised Śiva in the form of a liṅga by means of the Gāyatrī, Vasiṣṭha
and others obtained yoga, the supreme Brahman, liberation, from Śaṅkara.

217.s:
namaḥ kanakaliṅgāya(3) vedaliṅgāya vai namaḥ /
namaḥ paramaliṅgāya(4) vyomaliṅgāya vai namaḥ //
217.d:
नमः कनकलिङ्गाय(3) वेदलिङ्गाय वै नमः /
नमः परमलिङ्गाय(4) व्योमलिङ्गाय वै नमः //
217.m:
Homage to the golden liṅga! Homage indeed to the Vedic liṅga!
Homage to the supreme liṅga! Homage indeed to the sky liṅga!

217.s:
namaḥ sahasraliṅgāya vahniliṅgāya vai namaḥ /
namaḥ purāṇaliṅgāya śrutiliṅgāya vai namaḥ //
217.d:
नमः सहस्रलिङ्गाय वह्निलिङ्गाय वै नमः /
नमः पुराणलिङ्गाय श्रुतिलिङ्गाय वै नमः //
217.m:
Homage to the thousandfold liṅga! Homage indeed to the fire liṅga!
Homage to the Purāṇic liṅga! Homage indeed to the liṅga of revelation!

217.s:
namaḥ pātālaliṅgāya brahmaliṅgāya vai namaḥ /
namo rahasyaliṅgāya saptadvīpordhaliṅgine //
217.d:
नमः पाताललिङ्गाय ब्रह्मलिङ्गाय वै नमः /
नमो रहस्यलिङ्गाय सप्तद्वीपोर्धलिङ्गिने //
217.m:
Homage to the netherworld liṅga! Homage indeed to the Brahman liṅga!
Homage to the secret liṅga, to the one who has the liṅga above the seven continents!

217.s:
namaḥ sarvātmaliṅgāya sarvalokāṅgaliṅgine /
namastvavyaktaliṅgāya buddhiliṅgāya vai namaḥ //
217.d:
नमः सर्वात्मलिङ्गाय सर्वलोकाङ्गलिङ्गिने /
नमस्त्वव्यक्तलिङ्गाय बुद्धिलिङ्गाय वै नमः //
217.m:
Homage to the liṅga that is the Self of all, to the one whose liṅga is the limbs of all worlds!
Homage to you who are the unmanifest liṅga! Homage indeed to the intellect liṅga!

217.s:
namo 'haṅkārakiṅgāya bhūtaliṅgāya vai namaḥ /
nama indriyaliṅgāya namastanmātraliṅgine //
217.d:
नमो ऽहङ्कारकिङ्गाय भूतलिङ्गाय वै नमः /
नम इन्द्रियलिङ्गाय नमस्तन्मात्रलिङ्गिने //
217.m:
Homage to the ego-sense liṅga! Homage indeed to the element liṅga!
Homage to the sense-organ liṅga! Homage to the one who is the liṅga of subtle elements!

217.s:
namaḥ puruṣaliṅgāya bhāvaliṅgāya vai namaḥ /
:n
1 nirmalamiti kha..
2 vaśiṣtopyeva śaṅkarāditi kha.. , gha.. ca
3 kamalaliṅgāyeti ṭa..
4 namaḥ pavanaliṅgāyeti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 289
namo rajordhaliṅgāya sattvaliṅgāya(1) vai namaḥ(2) //
217.d:
नमः पुरुषलिङ्गाय भावलिङ्गाय वै नमः /
:न्
1 निर्मलमिति ख..
2 वशिष्तोप्येव शङ्करादिति ख.. , घ.. च
3 कमललिङ्गायेति ट..
4 नमः पवनलिङ्गायेति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. , ट.. च
:प् 289
नमो रजोर्धलिङ्गाय सत्त्वलिङ्गाय(1) वै नमः(2) //
217.m:
Homage to the Person liṅga! Homage indeed to the liṅga of existence!
[Note]
[Footnote 1: "nirmalam" in manuscript kha.]
[Footnote 2: "vaśiṣṭho 'py eva śaṅkarāt" in manuscripts kha and gha.]
[Footnote 3: "kamalaliṅgāya" in manuscript ṭa.]
[Page 289]
Homage to the liṅga above passion! Homage indeed to the purity liṅga!

217.s:
namstebhavaliṅgāya namastraiguṇyaliṅgine /
namo 'nāgataliṅgāya tejoliṅgāya vai namaḥ //
217.d:
नम्स्तेभवलिङ्गाय नमस्त्रैगुण्यलिङ्गिने /
नमो ऽनागतलिङ्गाय तेजोलिङ्गाय वै नमः //
217.m:
Homage to you who are the liṅga of worldly existence! Homage to the one whose liṅga consists of the three qualities!
Homage to the liṅga of what has not yet come! Homage indeed to the fiery liṅga!

217.s:
namo vāyūrdhvaliṅgāya(3) śrutiliṅgāya vai namaḥ /
namaste 'tharvaliṅgāya sāmaliṅgāya(4) vai namaḥ //
217.d:
नमो वायूर्ध्वलिङ्गाय(3) श्रुतिलिङ्गाय वै नमः /
नमस्ते ऽथर्वलिङ्गाय सामलिङ्गाय(4) वै नमः //
217.m:
Homage to the liṅga above the wind! Homage indeed to the liṅga of revelation!
Homage to you who are the Atharvan liṅga! Homage indeed to the Sāman liṅga!

217.s:
namo yajñāṅgaliṅgāya yajñaliṅgāya vai namaḥ /
namaste tattvaliṅgāya devānugataliṅgine(5) //
217.d:
नमो यज्ञाङ्गलिङ्गाय यज्ञलिङ्गाय वै नमः /
नमस्ते तत्त्वलिङ्गाय देवानुगतलिङ्गिने(5) //
217.m:
Homage to the liṅga consisting of the limbs of sacrifice! Homage indeed to the sacrifice liṅga!
Homage to you who are the reality liṅga, whose liṅga is attended by the gods!

217.s:
diśa naḥ paramaṃ yogamapatyaṃ matsamantathā /
brahma caivākṣayaṃ deva śamañcaiva paraṃ vibho(6) //
217.d:
दिश नः परमं योगमपत्यं मत्समन्तथा /
ब्रह्म चैवाक्षयं देव शमञ्चैव परं विभो(6) //
217.m:
Bestow upon us supreme yoga, and an offspring equal to myself,
as well as imperishable Brahman, O God, and supreme peace, O all-pervading Lord,

217.s:
akṣayantvañca vaṃśasya dharme ca matimakṣayāṃ /
agnir uvāca
vasiṣṭhena stutaḥ śambhustuṣṭaḥ śrīparvate purā //
217.d:
अक्षयन्त्वञ्च वंशस्य धर्मे च मतिमक्षयां /
अग्निर् उवाच
वसिष्ठेन स्तुतः शम्भुस्तुष्टः श्रीपर्वते पुरा //

217.s:
vasiṣṭhāya varaṃ dattvā tatraivāntaradhīyata //13//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe gāyatrīnirvāṇaṃ nāma
saptadaśādhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 tattvaliṅgāyeti kha.. , cha.. ca
2 nama indriyaliṅgāyetyādiḥ sattvaliṅgāya vai nama ity antaḥ
pāṭhaḥ ja.. pustake nāsti
3 namo vāgūrdhvaliṅgāyeti gha..
4 namaste sarvaliṅgāya nāmaliṅgāyeti kha.. , cha.. ca
5 namo 'nāgataliṅgāyetyādiḥ devānugataliṅgine ity antaḥ
pāṭhaḥ ja.. pustake nāsti
6 paramātmā paraṃvibho iti ja..
:p 290
:ś athāṣṭādaśādhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
rājābhiṣekakathanaṃ
217.d:
वसिष्ठाय वरं दत्त्वा तत्रैवान्तरधीयत //13//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे गायत्रीनिर्वाणं नाम
सप्तदशाधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 तत्त्वलिङ्गायेति ख.. , छ.. च
2 नम इन्द्रियलिङ्गायेत्यादिः सत्त्वलिङ्गाय वै नम इत्य् अन्तः
पाठः ज.. पुस्तके नास्ति
3 नमो वागूर्ध्वलिङ्गायेति घ..
4 नमस्ते सर्वलिङ्गाय नामलिङ्गायेति ख.. , छ.. च
5 नमो ऽनागतलिङ्गायेत्यादिः देवानुगतलिङ्गिने इत्य् अन्तः
पाठः ज.. पुस्तके नास्ति
6 परमात्मा परंविभो इति ज..
:प् 290
:श् अथाष्टादशाधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
राजाभिषेककथनं
217.m:
having granted a boon to Vasiṣṭha, he disappeared right there. // 13
Thus ends the two hundred and seventeenth chapter, named 'The Ultimate Essence of the Gāyatrī', in the great Agni Purāṇa.
[Note]
[Footnote 1: "tattvaliṅgāya" in manuscripts kha and cha.]
[Footnote 2: The passage beginning "nama indriyaliṅgāya" up to "sattvaliṅgāya vai namaḥ" is absent in manuscript ja.]
[Footnote 3: "namo vāgūrdhvaliṅgāya" in manuscript gha.]
[Footnote 4: "namas te sarvaliṅgāya nāmaliṅgāya" in manuscripts kha and cha.]
[Footnote 5: The passage beginning "namo 'nāgataliṅgāya" up to "devānugataliṅgine" is absent in manuscript ja.]
[Page 290]
Now begins the two hundred and eighteenth chapter.
The Exposition of Royal Consecration by Aspersion

218.s:
agnir uvāca
puṣkareṇa ca rāmāya rājadharmaṃ hi pṛcchate /
yathādau kathitaṃ tadvadvaśiṣṭa kathayāmi te //
218.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
पुष्करेण च रामाय राजधर्मं हि पृच्छते /
यथादौ कथितं तद्वद्वशिष्ट कथयामि ते //
218.m:
Agni said:
As it was formerly told by Puṣkara to Rāma who questioned him about royal duty,
even so, O Vasiṣṭha, I shall relate it to you.

218.s:
puṣkara uvāca
rājadharmaṃ pravakṣyāmi sarvasmāt rājadharmataḥ /
rājā bhavet(1) śatruhantā prajāpālaḥ sudaṇḍavān //
218.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
राजधर्मं प्रवक्ष्यामि सर्वस्मात् राजधर्मतः /
राजा भवेत्(1) शत्रुहन्ता प्रजापालः सुदण्डवान् //
218.m:
Puṣkara said:
I shall declare royal duty, the foremost of all royal duties.
The king should be a slayer of enemies, a protector of subjects, and one who wields the rod of justice firmly.

218.s:
pālayiṣyati vaḥ sarvān dharmasthān vratamācaret /
saṃvatsaraṃ sa vṛṇuyāt purohitamatha dvijaṃ(2) //
218.d:
पालयिष्यति वः सर्वान् धर्मस्थान् व्रतमाचरेत् /
संवत्सरं स वृणुयात् पुरोहितमथ द्विजं(2) //
218.m:
He will protect all of you who stand in righteousness; he should observe a votive observance.
For a year he should appoint an astrologer and a twice-born royal priest,

218.s:
mantriṇaścākhilātmajñānmahiṣīṃ dharmalakṣaṇāṃ /
saṃvatsaraṃ nṛpaḥ kāle sasambhāro 'bhiṣecanaṃ //
218.d:
मन्त्रिणश्चाखिलात्मज्ञान्महिषीं धर्मलक्षणां /
संवत्सरं नृपः काले ससम्भारो ऽभिषेचनं //
218.m:
ministers knowing all self-matters, and a queen endowed with righteous marks.
After a year, at an auspicious time, the king, fully equipped with provisions, should perform consecration by aspersion.

218.s:
kuryānmṛte nṛpe nātra kālasya niyamaḥ smṛtaḥ /
tilaiḥ siddhārthakaiḥ snānaṃ sāṃvatsarapurohitau //
218.d:
कुर्यान्मृते नृपे नात्र कालस्य नियमः स्मृतः /
तिलैः सिद्धार्थकैः स्नानं सांवत्सरपुरोहितौ //
218.m:
When a king dies, no restriction of time is observed in this rite.
A bath with sesame seeds and white mustard seeds is to be administered; the astrologer and the royal priest,

218.s:
ghoṣayitvā jayaṃ rājño rājā bhadrāsane sthitaḥ /
abhayaṃ ghoṣayed durgānmocayedrājyapālake //
218.d:
घोषयित्वा जयं राज्ञो राजा भद्रासने स्थितः /
अभयं घोषयेद् दुर्गान्मोचयेद्राज्यपालके //
218.m:
having proclaimed the king's victory, while the king sits upon the auspicious throne,
should proclaim fearlessness, and he should release prisoners from fortresses, while protecting the realm.

218.s:
purodhasābhiṣekāt prāk kāryaindrī śāntireva ca /
upavāsyabhiṣekāhe vedyagnau juhuyānmanūn(3) //
:n
1 rājā hariti cha.. , kha.. , gha.. , ja.. , ña.. , ṭa.. ca
2 purohitamathartvijamiti kha.. , gha.. , cha.. , ja.. , ṭa.. ca
3 juhuyādamūniti ṅa..
:p 291
218.d:
पुरोधसाभिषेकात् प्राक् कार्यैन्द्री शान्तिरेव च /
उपवास्यभिषेकाहे वेद्यग्नौ जुहुयान्मनून्(3) //
:न्
1 राजा हरिति छ.. , ख.. , घ.. , ज.. , ञ.. , ट.. च
2 पुरोहितमथर्त्विजमिति ख.. , घ.. , छ.. , ज.. , ट.. च
3 जुहुयादमूनिति ङ..
:प् 291
218.m:
Before the consecration by aspersion, the royal priest must perform the propitiatory rite for Indra.
Fasting on the day of the consecration by aspersion, one should offer mantras into the fire upon the altar:
[Note]
[Footnote 1: "rājā hariḥ" in manuscripts cha, kha, gha, ja, ña, and ṭa.]
[Footnote 2: "purohitam athartvijam" in manuscripts kha, gha, cha, ja, and ṭa.]
[Footnote 3: "juhuyād amūn" in manuscript ṅa. Page 291.]

218.s:
vaiṣṇavānaindramantrāṃstu sāvitrīn vaiśvadaivatān /
saumyān svastyayanaṃ śarmāyuṣyābhayadānmanūn //
218.d:
वैष्णवानैन्द्रमन्त्रांस्तु सावित्रीन् वैश्वदैवतान् /
सौम्यान् स्वस्त्ययनं शर्मायुष्याभयदान्मनून् //
218.m:
Vaiṣṇava mantras, Indra mantras, Sāvitrī mantras, mantras to all the gods,
Saumya mantras, benedictory mantras, and mantras conferring welfare, longevity, and fearlessness.

218.s:
aparājitāñca kalasaṃ vahnerdakṣiṇapārśvagaṃ /
sampātavantaṃ haimañca pūjayedgandhapuṣpakaiḥ //
218.d:
अपराजिताञ्च कलसं वह्नेर्दक्षिणपार्श्वगं /
सम्पातवन्तं हैमञ्च पूजयेद्गन्धपुष्पकैः //
218.m:
And one should worship the Aparājitā vessel situated on the southern side of the fire,
containing sacrificial drippings and made of gold, with fragrant scents and flowers.

218.s:
pradakṣiṇāvartaśikhastaptajāmbūnadaprabhaḥ /
rathaughameghanirghoṣo vidhūmaś ca hutāśanaḥ //
218.d:
प्रदक्षिणावर्तशिखस्तप्तजाम्बूनदप्रभः /
रथौघमेघनिर्घोषो विधूमश् च हुताशनः //
218.m:
With flames turning clockwise, resembling molten gold in radiance,
roaring like a host of chariots and clouds, and smokeless, the fire

218.s:
anulomaḥ sugandhaś ca svastikākārasannibhaḥ /
prasannārcirmahājvālaḥ sphuliṅgarahito hitaḥ //
218.d:
अनुलोमः सुगन्धश् च स्वस्तिकाकारसन्निभः /
प्रसन्नार्चिर्महाज्वालः स्फुलिङ्गरहितो हितः //
218.m:
flowing favourably, fragrant, resembling the shape of a svastika,
with clear light, large flames, and devoid of sparks, is auspicious.

218.s:
na vrajeyuś ca madhyena mārjāramṛgapakṣiṇaḥ /
parvatāgramṛdā tāvanmūrdhānaṃ śodhayennṛpaḥ //
218.d:
न व्रजेयुश् च मध्येन मार्जारमृगपक्षिणः /
पर्वताग्रमृदा तावन्मूर्धानं शोधयेन्नृपः //
218.m:
Cats, deer, and birds should not cross through the middle.
The king should then purify his head with earth from a mountain peak;

218.s:
valmīkāgramṛdā karṇau vadanaṃ keśavālayāt /
indrālayamṛdā(1) grīvāṃ hṛdayantu nṛpājirāt //
218.d:
वल्मीकाग्रमृदा कर्णौ वदनं केशवालयात् /
इन्द्रालयमृदा(1) ग्रीवां हृदयन्तु नृपाजिरात् //
218.m:
the two ears with earth from the top of an anthill; the face with earth from a temple of Keśava;
the neck with earth from a temple of Indra; and the chest with earth from the king's courtyard;

218.s:
karidantoddhṛtamṛdā dakṣiṇantu tathā bhujaṃ /
vṛṣaśṛṅgoddhṛtamṛdā vāmañcaiva tathā bhujaṃ //
218.d:
करिदन्तोद्धृतमृदा दक्षिणन्तु तथा भुजं /
वृषशृङ्गोद्धृतमृदा वामञ्चैव तथा भुजं //
218.m:
the right arm with earth uprooted by an elephant's tusk;
and likewise the left arm with earth uprooted by a bull's horn;

218.s:
saromṛdā tathā pṛṣṭhamudaraṃ saṅgamān mṛdā /
nadītaṭadvayamṛdā pārśve saṃśodhayettathā(2) //
218.d:
सरोमृदा तथा पृष्ठमुदरं सङ्गमान् मृदा /
नदीतटद्वयमृदा पार्श्वे संशोधयेत्तथा(2) //
218.m:
the back with lake-mud, the belly with earth from a river confluence;
and likewise one should purify the two sides with earth from both banks of a river.

218.s:
veśyādvāramṛdā rājñaḥ kaṭiśaucaṃ vidhīyate /
yajñasthānāttathaivorū gosthānājjānunī tathā //
218.d:
वेश्याद्वारमृदा राज्ञः कटिशौचं विधीयते /
यज्ञस्थानात्तथैवोरू गोस्थानाज्जानुनी तथा //
218.m:
Purification of the king's waist is prescribed with earth from a courtesan's doorway;
likewise the thighs with earth from a sacrificial site; and the knees with earth from a cow-pen;

218.s:
aśvasthānāttathā jaṅghe rathacakramṛdāṅghrike /
mūrdhānaṃ pañcagavyena bhadrāsanagataṃ nṛpaṃ //
218.d:
अश्वस्थानात्तथा जङ्घे रथचक्रमृदाङ्घ्रिके /
मूर्धानं पञ्चगव्येन भद्रासनगतं नृपं //
218.m:
the shanks with earth from a stable for horses; the two feet with earth from a chariot wheel.
With the five products of the cow, [he should purify] the king seated on the auspicious throne.

218.s:
abhiṣiñcedamātyānāṃ catuṣṭayamatho ghaṭaiḥ /
:n
1 candrālayamṛdeti ja..
2 saromṛdetyādiḥ saṃśodhayettathetyantaḥ pāṭhaḥ ja.. pustake
nāsti
:p 292
pūrvato hemakumbhena ghṛtapūrṇena brāhaṇaḥ //
218.d:
अभिषिञ्चेदमात्यानां चतुष्टयमथो घटैः /
:न्
1 चन्द्रालयमृदेति ज..
2 सरोमृदेत्यादिः संशोधयेत्तथेत्यन्तः पाठः ज.. पुस्तके
नास्ति
:प् 292
पूर्वतो हेमकुम्भेन घृतपूर्णेन ब्राहणः //
218.m:
Then four ministers should sprinkle the king with pitchers:
[Note]
[Footnote 1: "candrālayamṛdā" in manuscript ja.]
[Footnote 2: The passage beginning "saromṛdā" up to "saṃśodhayet tathā" is absent in manuscript ja. Page 292.]
from the east, a brāhmaṇa with a golden vessel filled with clarified butter;

218.s:
rūpyakumbhena yāmye ca kṣīrapūrṇena kṣatriyaḥ /
dadhnā ca tāmrakumbhena vaiśyaḥ paścimagena ca //
218.d:
रूप्यकुम्भेन याम्ये च क्षीरपूर्णेन क्षत्रियः /
दध्ना च ताम्रकुम्भेन वैश्यः पश्चिमगेन च //
218.m:
and in the south, a kṣatriya with a silver vessel filled with milk;
a vaiśya in the west with a copper vessel filled with curds;

218.s:
mṛṇmayena jalenodak śūdrāmātyo 'bhiṣicayet /
tato 'bhiṣekaṃ nṛpaterbahvṛcapravaro dvijaḥ //
218.d:
मृण्मयेन जलेनोदक् शूद्रामात्यो ऽभिषिचयेत् /
ततो ऽभिषेकं नृपतेर्बह्वृचप्रवरो द्विजः //
218.m:
and from the north, a śūdra minister should sprinkle him with water from an earthen vessel.
Then an eminent twice-born Ṛgvedic priest should perform consecration by aspersion of the ruler

218.s:
kurvīta madhunā vipraśchandogaś ca kuśodakaiḥ /
sampātavantaṃ kalaśaṃ tathā gatvā purohitaḥ //
218.d:
कुर्वीत मधुना विप्रश्छन्दोगश् च कुशोदकैः /
सम्पातवन्तं कलशं तथा गत्वा पुरोहितः //
218.m:
with honey, and a Sāmavedic priest with kuśa grass water.
Having thus approached the pitcher containing the sacrificial drippings, the royal priest,

218.s:
vidhāya vahnirakṣāntu sadasyeṣu yathāvidhi /
rājaśriyābhiṣeke ca ye mantrāḥ parikīrtitāḥ //
218.d:
विधाय वह्निरक्षान्तु सदस्येषु यथाविधि /
राजश्रियाभिषेके च ये मन्त्राः परिकीर्तिताः //
218.m:
having performed the fire-protection over the assembly members according to rule,
should sprinkle him with those mantras which are proclaimed for royal splendour at consecration by aspersion,

218.s:
taistu dadyānmahābhāga brāhmaṇānāṃ svanais tathā /
tataḥ purohito gacchedvedimūlantadeva tu(1) //
218.d:
तैस्तु दद्यान्महाभाग ब्राह्मणानां स्वनैस् तथा /
ततः पुरोहितो गच्छेद्वेदिमूलन्तदेव तु(1) //
218.m:
O highly fortunate one, accompanied by the chants of the brāhmaṇas.
Then the royal priest should proceed to that very base of the altar,

218.s:
śatacchidreṇa pātreṇa sauvarṇenābhiṣecayet /
yā oṣadhītyoṣadhībhīrathetyuktveti gandhakaiḥ //
218.d:
शतच्छिद्रेण पात्रेण सौवर्णेनाभिषेचयेत् /
या ओषधीत्योषधीभीरथेत्युक्त्वेति गन्धकैः //
218.m:
and sprinkle him by means of a golden vessel with a hundred holes,
with medicinal herbs saying "yā oṣadhīḥ", and then saying "atha" with perfumes.

218.s:
puṣpaiḥ puṣpavatītyeva brāhmaṇeti ca vījakaiḥ(2) /
ratnair āśuḥ śiśānaś ca ye devāś ca kuśodakaiḥ //
218.d:
पुष्पैः पुष्पवतीत्येव ब्राह्मणेति च वीजकैः(2) /
रत्नैर् आशुः शिशानश् च ये देवाश् च कुशोदकैः //
218.m: with flowers [saying] "Possessed of flowers!", and with seeds [saying] "The brāhmaṇa!"; / with jewels [saying] "Quickly whetting!", and with kusa-grass water [saying] "Which gods!".

218.s:
yajurvedyatharvavedī(3) gandhadvāreti saṃspṛśet /
śiraḥ kaṇṭhaṃ rocanayā sarvatīrthodakair dvijāḥ //
218.d:
यजुर्वेद्यथर्ववेदी(3) गन्धद्वारेति संस्पृशेत् /
शिरः कण्ठं रोचनया सर्वतीर्थोदकैर् द्विजाः //
218.m: A reciter of the Yajurveda and Atharvaveda should touch [the king] saying, "Having the fragrance door!"; / the twice-born should touch his head and neck with yellow orpiment, [sprinkling him] with water from all sacred fords,

218.s:
gītavādyādinirghoṣaiścāmaravyajanādibhiḥ /
sarvauṣadhimayaṃ kumbhaṃ dhārayeyurnṛpāgrataḥ //
218.d:
गीतवाद्यादिनिर्घोषैश्चामरव्यजनादिभिः /
सर्वौषधिमयं कुम्भं धारयेयुर्नृपाग्रतः //
218.m: amid sounds of singing, musical instruments and the like, and with flywhisks, fans and the like. / They should hold before the king a jar containing all medicinal herbs.

218.s:
taṃ paśyeddarpaṇaṃ rājā ghṛtaṃ vai maṅgalādikaṃ /
abhyarcya viṣṇuṃ brahmāṇamindrādīṃś ca graheśvarān(4) //
:n
1 vedimūlantathaiva tu iri kha..
2 dīpakair iti ṅa..
3 yajurvedyatha ṛgvedī iti ṅa..
4 grahādikāniti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. ca
:p 293
218.d:
तं पश्येद्दर्पणं राजा घृतं वै मङ्गलादिकं /
अभ्यर्च्य विष्णुं ब्रह्माणमिन्द्रादींश् च ग्रहेश्वरान्(4) //
:न्
1 वेदिमूलन्तथैव तु इरि ख..
2 दीपकैर् इति ङ..
3 यजुर्वेद्यथ ऋग्वेदी इति ङ..
4 ग्रहादिकानिति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. च
:प् 293
218.m:
The king should look at that, at a mirror, at ghee, and at auspicious objects, / having worshipped Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Indra and the other lords of the planets.
[Note]
1 [Variant reading] "vedimūlantathaiva tu" in [manuscript] kha..
2 [Variant reading] "dīpakair" in [manuscript] ṅa..
3 [Variant reading] "yajurvedyatha ṛgvedī" in [manuscript] ṅa..
4 [Variant reading] "grahādikān" in [manuscripts] kha.., ga.., and gha..

218.s:
vyāghracarmottarāṃ śayyāmupaviṣṭaḥ purohitaḥ /
madhuparkādikaṃ dattvā paṭṭabandhaṃ prakārayet //
218.d:
व्याघ्रचर्मोत्तरां शय्यामुपविष्टः पुरोहितः /
मधुपर्कादिकं दत्त्वा पट्टबन्धं प्रकारयेत् //
218.m: The royal priest, seated on a couch covered with a tiger skin, / having offered the madhuparka offering and the like, should perform the binding of the royal headband.

218.s:
rājñomukuṭabandhañca pañcacarmottaraṃ dadet /
dhruvādyair iti ca viśed vṛṣajaṃ vṛṣadaṃśajaṃ //
218.d:
राज्ञोमुकुटबन्धञ्च पञ्चचर्मोत्तरं ददेत् /
ध्रुवाद्यैर् इति च विशेद् वृषजं वृषदंशजं //
218.m: He should perform the binding of the crown for the king, and provide a cover of five skins. / Reciting "With the firm ones!" and the like, he should enter [the seat covered with] skin from a bull, skin from a cat,

218.s:
dvīpijaṃ siṃhajaṃ vyāghrajātañcarma tadāsane /
amātyasacivādīṃś ca pratīhāraḥ pradarśayet //
218.d:
द्वीपिजं सिंहजं व्याघ्रजातञ्चर्म तदासने /
अमात्यसचिवादींश् च प्रतीहारः प्रदर्शयेत् //
218.m: skin from a leopard, from a lion, and skin born of a tiger, upon that throne. / The door-keeper should introduce the ministers, counselors, and other officials.

218.s:
