gojāvigṛhadānādyaiḥ sāṃvatsarapurohitau /
pūjayitvā dvijān prārcya hy anyabhūgonnamukhyakaiḥ //
218.d:
गोजाविगृहदानाद्यैः सांवत्सरपुरोहितौ /
पूजयित्वा द्विजान् प्रार्च्य ह्य् अन्यभूगोन्नमुख्यकैः //
218.m: Having honoured the astrologer and the royal priest with gifts of cattle, goats, sheep, and houses, / and having honoured the twice-born, primarily with other lands, cattle, and food,

218.s:
vahniṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya guruṃ natvātha pṛṣṭhataḥ /
vṛṣamālabhya gāṃ vatsāṃ pūjayitvātha mantritaṃ //
218.d:
वह्निं प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य गुरुं नत्वाथ पृष्ठतः /
वृषमालभ्य गां वत्सां पूजयित्वाथ मन्त्रितं //
218.m: having circumambulated the fire from left to right, bowed to the guru behind it, / touched a bull, and worshipped a cow with her calf, then [a horse] consecrated with mantras,

218.s:
aśvamāruhya nāgañca pūjayettaṃ samāruhet /
paribhramedrājamārge balayuktaḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ //
218.d:
अश्वमारुह्य नागञ्च पूजयेत्तं समारुहेत् /
परिभ्रमेद्राजमार्गे बलयुक्तः प्रदक्षिणं //
218.m: having mounted the horse, he should worship an elephant and mount it. / Surrounded by his army, he should circumambulate the royal highway from left to right.

218.s:
puraṃ viśecca dānādyaiḥ prārcya sarvān visarjayet //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe rājābhiṣeko nāma
aṣṭādaśādhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś athonaviṃśādhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
abhiṣekamantrāḥ
218.d:
पुरं विशेच्च दानाद्यैः प्रार्च्य सर्वान् विसर्जयेत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे राजाभिषेको नाम
अष्टादशाधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथोनविंशाधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
अभिषेकमन्त्राः
218.m:
He should enter the city, and having honoured all with gifts and the like, he should dismiss them.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the two hundred and eighteenth chapter, named "The Consecration by Aspersion of a King."
Now, the two hundred and nineteenth chapter.
Mantras for Consecration by Aspersion.

219.s:
puṣkara uvāca
rājadevādyabhiṣekamantrānvakṣye 'ghamardanān /
kumbhāt kuśodakaiḥ siñcettena sarvaṃ hi siddhyati //
:p 294
219.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
राजदेवाद्यभिषेकमन्त्रान्वक्ष्ये ऽघमर्दनान् /
कुम्भात् कुशोदकैः सिञ्चेत्तेन सर्वं हि सिद्ध्यति //
:प् 294
219.m:
Puṣkara said: / I shall declare the mantras for the consecration by aspersion of kings, deities, and others, which destroy sins. / One should sprinkle [the king] with kusa-grass water from the jar; thereby indeed everything is accomplished.
[Page 294]

219.s:
surāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ /
vāsudevaḥ saṅkarṣaṇaḥ pradyumnaścāniruddhakaḥ //
219.d:
सुरास्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वराः /
वासुदेवः सङ्कर्षणः प्रद्युम्नश्चानिरुद्धकः //
219.m: May the gods consecrate you: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara; / Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, and Aniruddha!

219.s:
bhavantu vijayāyaite indrādyā daśadiggatāḥ /
rudro dharmo manurdakṣo ruciḥ śraddhā ca sarvadā //
219.d:
भवन्तु विजयायैते इन्द्राद्या दशदिग्गताः /
रुद्रो धर्मो मनुर्दक्षो रुचिः श्रद्धा च सर्वदा //
219.m: May these, led by Indra, residing in the ten directions, be for your victory! / May Rudra, Dharma, Manu, Dakṣa, Ruci, and Śraddhā always [protect you]!

219.s:
bhṛguratrirvasiṣṭhaś ca sanakaś ca sanandanaḥ /
sanatkumāro 'ṅgirāś ca pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ //
219.d:
भृगुरत्रिर्वसिष्ठश् च सनकश् च सनन्दनः /
सनत्कुमारो ऽङ्गिराश् च पुलस्त्यः पुलहः क्रतुः //
219.m: May Bhṛgu, Atri, Vasiṣṭha, Sanaka, Sanandana, / Sanatkumāra, Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu,

219.s:
marīciḥ kaśyapaḥ pāntu prajeśāḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ /
prabhāsurā vahirṣada agniṣvāttāś ca pāntu te //
219.d:
मरीचिः कश्यपः पान्तु प्रजेशाः पृथिवीपतिः /
प्रभासुरा वहिर्षद अग्निष्वात्ताश् च पान्तु ते //
219.m: Marīci, and Kaśyapa, the lords of creatures, protect the lord of the earth! / May the Prabhāsuras, the Barhiṣads, and the Agniṣvāttas protect you!

219.s:
kravyādāścopahūtāś ca ājyapāś ca sukālinaḥ /
agnibhiścābhiṣiñcantu lakṣmyādyā dharmavallabhāḥ //
219.d:
क्रव्यादाश्चोपहूताश् च आज्यपाश् च सुकालिनः /
अग्निभिश्चाभिषिञ्चन्तु लक्ष्म्याद्या धर्मवल्लभाः //
219.m: May the Kravyādas, the Upahūtas, the Ājyapas, and the Sukālins, / and the beloved wives of Dharma led by Lakṣmī, consecrate [you] with fires!

219.s:
ādityādyāḥ kaśyapasya bahuputrasya(1) vallabhāḥ /
kṛśāśvasyāgniputrasya bhāryāścāriṣṭhaneminaḥ //
219.d:
आदित्याद्याः कश्यपस्य बहुपुत्रस्य(1) वल्लभाः /
कृशाश्वस्याग्निपुत्रस्य भार्याश्चारिष्ठनेमिनः //
219.m: Aditi and the others, the beloved wives of Kaśyapa, of Bahuputra, / and of Kṛśāśva the son of Agni, and the wives of Ariṣṭanemi;

219.s:
aśvinyādyāś ca candrasya pulahasya(2) tathā priyāḥ /
bhūtā ca kapiśā daṃṣṭrī surasā saramā danuḥ //
219.d:
अश्विन्याद्याश् च चन्द्रस्य पुलहस्य(2) तथा प्रियाः /
भूता च कपिशा दंष्ट्री सुरसा सरमा दनुः //
219.m: and Aśvinī and the others, wives of the Moon, and likewise the beloved wives of Pulaha: / Bhūtā, Kapiśā, Daṃṣṭrī, Surasā, Saramā, Danu,

219.s:
śyenī bhāsī tathā krauñcī dhṛtarāṣṭrī śukī tathā /
patnyastvāmabhiṣiñcantu aruṇaścārkasārathiḥ //
219.d:
श्येनी भासी तथा क्रौञ्ची धृतराष्ट्री शुकी तथा /
पत्न्यस्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु अरुणश्चार्कसारथिः //
219.m: Śyenī, Bhāsī, as well as Krauñcī, Dhṛtarāṣṭrī, and Śukī; / may these wives consecrate you by aspersion, as well as Aruṇa the charioteer of the Sun.

219.s:
āyatir niyatīrātrir nidrā lokasthitau sthitāḥ /
umā menā śacī pāntu dhūmor nānirṛtirjaye //
219.d:
आयतिर् नियतीरात्रिर् निद्रा लोकस्थितौ स्थिताः /
उमा मेना शची पान्तु धूमोर् नानिरृतिर्जये //
219.m: Āyati, Niyati, Rātri, and Nidrā, who are established in the order of the worlds; / may Umā, Menā, and Śacī protect you, and Dhūmorṇā and Nirṛti grant victory.

219.s:
gaurī śivā ca ṛddhiś ca velā caiva naḍvalā /
aśiknī ca(3) tathā jyotsnā devapatnyo vanaspatiḥ //
219.d:
गौरी शिवा च ऋद्धिश् च वेला चैव नड्वला /
अशिक्नी च(3) तथा ज्योत्स्ना देवपत्न्यो वनस्पतिः //
219.m: Gaurī, Śivā, Ṛddhi, Velā, and Naḍvalā, / Aśiknī, and also Jyotsnā, the wives of the gods, and Vanaspati;

219.s:
mahākalpaś ca kalpaś ca manvantarayugāni ca /
:n
1 devaputrasyeti ja..
2 pulastyasyeti ga.. , gha.. , ja.. ca
3 asitā ceti ṅa..
:p 295
saṃvatsarāṇi varṣāṇi pāntu tvāmayanadvayaṃ //
219.d:
महाकल्पश् च कल्पश् च मन्वन्तरयुगानि च /
:न्
1 देवपुत्रस्येति ज..
2 पुलस्त्यस्येति ग.. , घ.. , ज.. च
3 असिता चेति ङ..
:प् 295
संवत्सराणि वर्षाणि पान्तु त्वामयनद्वयं //
219.m:
the great cosmic age and the cosmic age, and the cosmic eras of the Manus and the world-ages,
[Note]
1. devaputrasya in ms. ja.
2. pulastyasya in mss. ga., gha., and ja.
3. asitā ca in ms. ṅa.
[p. 295]
the solar cycles, the years, and the two solstitial half-years—may they protect you.

219.s:
ṛtavaś ca tathā māsā pakṣā rātryahanī tathā /
sandhyātithimuhūrtācca kālasyāvayavākṛtiḥ //
219.d:
ऋतवश् च तथा मासा पक्षा रात्र्यहनी तथा /
सन्ध्यातिथिमुहूर्ताच्च कालस्यावयवाकृतिः //
219.m: The seasons, and likewise the months, the fortnights, night and day, / the twilights, lunar days, and muhūrtas, which form the body of Time;

219.s:
sūryādyāś ca grahāḥ pāntu manuḥ svāyambhuvādikaḥ /
svāyambhuvaḥ svārociṣa auttamistāmaso manuḥ //
219.d:
सूर्याद्याश् च ग्रहाः पान्तु मनुः स्वायम्भुवादिकः /
स्वायम्भुवः स्वारोचिष औत्तमिस्तामसो मनुः //
219.m: and may the planets beginning with the Sun protect you, and the Manus beginning with Svāyambhuva: / Svāyambhuva, Svārociṣa, Auttami, the Manu Tāmasa,

219.s:
raivataścākṣuṣaḥ ṣaṣṭho vaivasvata iheritaḥ /
sāvarṇo brahmaputraś ca dharmaputraś ca rudrajaḥ //
219.d:
रैवतश्चाक्षुषः षष्ठो वैवस्वत इहेरितः /
सावर्णो ब्रह्मपुत्रश् च धर्मपुत्रश् च रुद्रजः //
219.m: Raivata, and Cākṣuṣa the sixth; Vaivasvata is declared here; / Sāvarṇa, the son of Brahmā, the son of Dharma, and the son of Rudra,

219.s:
dakṣajo raucyabhautyau ca manavastu caturdaśa /
viśvabhuk ca vipaścicca sucittiś ca śikhī vibhuḥ //
219.d:
दक्षजो रौच्यभौत्यौ च मनवस्तु चतुर्दश /
विश्वभुक् च विपश्चिच्च सुचित्तिश् च शिखी विभुः //
219.m: the son of Dakṣa, and Raucya and Bhautya—the fourteen Manus; / and Viśvabhuk, Vipaścit, Sucitti, Śikhī, Vibhu,

219.s:
manojavastathaujasvī baliradbhutaśāntayaḥ /
vṛṣaś ca ṛtadhāmā ca divaspṛk kavirindrakaḥ //
219.d:
मनोजवस्तथौजस्वी बलिरद्भुतशान्तयः /
वृषश् च ऋतधामा च दिवस्पृक् कविरिन्द्रकः //
219.m: Manojava, and likewise Ojasvī, Bali, Adbhuta, Śānti, / Vṛṣa, Ṛtadhāman, Divaspṛś, Kavi, Indraka,

219.s:
revantaś ca kumāraś ca tathā vatsavināyakaḥ /
vīrabhadraś ca nandī ca viśvakarmā purojavaḥ //
219.d:
रेवन्तश् च कुमारश् च तथा वत्सविनायकः /
वीरभद्रश् च नन्दी च विश्वकर्मा पुरोजवः //
219.m: Revanta, Kumāra, and likewise Vatsavināyaka, / Vīrabhadra, Nandī, Viśvakarman, and Purojava—

219.s:
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu suramukhyāḥ samāgatāḥ /
nāsatyau devabhiṣajau dhruvādyā vasavo 'ṣṭa ca //
219.d:
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु सुरमुख्याः समागताः /
नासत्यौ देवभिषजौ ध्रुवाद्या वसवो ऽष्ट च //
219.m: assembled together, may these chiefs of the gods consecrate you by aspersion; / the two Nāsatyas, the physicians of the gods, and the eight Vasus headed by Dhruva;

219.s:
daśa cāṅgiraso vedāstvābhiṣiñcantu siddhaye /
ātmā hy āyurmano dakṣo madaḥ prāṇastathaiva ca //
219.d:
दश चाङ्गिरसो वेदास्त्वाभिषिञ्चन्तु सिद्धये /
आत्मा ह्य् आयुर्मनो दक्षो मदः प्राणस्तथैव च //
219.m: and may the ten Aṅgirases and the Vedas consecrate you by aspersion for success: / Ātman, Āyus, Manas, Dakṣa, Mada, and likewise Prāṇa,

219.s:
haviṣmāṃś ca gariṣṭhaś ca ṛtaḥ satyaś ca pāntu vaḥ /
kraturdakṣo vasuḥ satyaḥ kālakāmo dhurirjaye //
219.d:
हविष्मांश् च गरिष्ठश् च ऋतः सत्यश् च पान्तु वः /
क्रतुर्दक्षो वसुः सत्यः कालकामो धुरिर्जये //
219.m: Haviṣmant, Gariṣṭha, Ṛta, and Satya—may they protect you! / Kratu, Dakṣa, Vasu, Satya, Kālakāma, Dhuri for victory,

219.s:
purūravā mādravāś ca viśvedevāś ca rocanaḥ /
aṅgārakādyāḥ sūryastvānnirṛtiś ca tathā yamaḥ //
219.d:
पुरूरवा माद्रवाश् च विश्वेदेवाश् च रोचनः /
अङ्गारकाद्याः सूर्यस्त्वान्निरृतिश् च तथा यमः //
219.m: Purūravas, Mādravas, the Viśvedevas, Rocana, / the planets beginning with Mars, the Sun, Nirṛti, and Yama;

219.s:
ajaikapādahirvradhro dhūmaketuś ca rudrajāḥ(1) /
:n
1 rudrakā iti ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , ña.. ca
:p 296
bharataś ca tathā mṛtyuḥ kāpāliratha kiṅkiṇiḥ //
219.d:
अजैकपादहिर्व्रध्रो धूमकेतुश् च रुद्रजाः(1) /
:न्
1 रुद्रका इति ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 296
भरतश् च तथा मृत्युः कापालिरथ किङ्किणिः //
219.m:
Ajaikapād, Ahirbudhnya, and Dhūmaketu—the Rudras,
[Note]
1. rudrakāḥ in mss. ga., gha., ṅa., and ña.
[p. 296]
Bharata, and likewise Mṛtyu, Kāpālin, and Kiṅkiṇi;

219.s:
bhavano bhāvanaḥ pāntu svajanyaḥ svajanas tathā(1) /
kratuśravāś ca mūrdhā ca yājano 'bhyuśanās tathā //
219.d:
भवनो भावनः पान्तु स्वजन्यः स्वजनस् तथा(1) /
क्रतुश्रवाश् च मूर्धा च याजनो ऽभ्युशनास् तथा //
219.m: may Bhavana and Bhāvana protect you, Svajanya and likewise Svajana, / Kratuśravas, Mūrdhan, Yājana, and Abhyuśanas,

219.s:
prasavaścāvyayaś caiva dakṣaś ca bhṛgavaḥ surāḥ /
mano 'numantā prāṇaś ca navopānaś ca vīryavān //
219.d:
प्रसवश्चाव्ययश् चैव दक्षश् च भृगवः सुराः /
मनो ऽनुमन्ता प्राणश् च नवोपानश् च वीर्यवान् //
219.m: Prasava, Avyaya, and Dakṣa—the Bhrgu gods; / Manas, Anumantṛ, Prāṇa, the nine Upānas, and Vīryavant,

219.s:
vītihotro nayaḥ sādhyo haṃso nārāyaṇo 'vatu /
vibhuś caiva prabhuś caiva devaśreṣṭhā jagaddhitāḥ //
219.d:
वीतिहोत्रो नयः साध्यो हंसो नारायणो ऽवतु /
विभुश् चैव प्रभुश् चैव देवश्रेष्ठा जगद्धिताः //
219.m: Vītihotra, Naya, Sādhya, Haṃsa—may Nārāyaṇa protect! / Vibhu and Prabhu—the foremost among the gods, benefactors of the world;

219.s:
dhātā mitro 'ryamā pūṣā śakro 'tha varuṇo bhagaḥ /
tvaṣṭā vivasvān savitā viṣṇurdvādaśa bhāskarāḥ //
219.d:
धाता मित्रो ऽर्यमा पूषा शक्रो ऽथ वरुणो भगः /
त्वष्टा विवस्वान् सविता विष्णुर्द्वादश भास्कराः //
219.m: Dhātṛ, Mitra, Aryaman, Pūṣan, Śakra, Varuṇa, Bhaga, / Tvaṣṭṛ, Vivasvant, Savitṛ, and Viṣṇu—the twelve suns;

219.s:
ekajyotiś ca dvijyotistriś caturjyotireva ca /
ekaśakro dviśakraś ca triśakraś ca mahābalaḥ //
219.d:
एकज्योतिश् च द्विज्योतिस्त्रिश् चतुर्ज्योतिरेव च /
एकशक्रो द्विशक्रश् च त्रिशक्रश् च महाबलः //
219.m: Ekajyotis, Dvijyotis, Trijyotis, and Caturjyotis, / Ekaśakra, Dviśakra, and Triśakra of great might,

219.s:
indraś ca metyādiśatu tataḥ pratimakṛttathā /
mitaś ca sammitaś caiva amitaś ca mahābalaḥ //
219.d:
इन्द्रश् च मेत्यादिशतु ततः प्रतिमकृत्तथा /
मितश् च सम्मितश् चैव अमितश् च महाबलः //
219.m: Indra, and let Mita command, and then Pratimakṛt, / Mita, Sammita, and Amita of great might,

219.s:
ṛtajit satyajiccaiva suṣeṇaḥ senajittathā /
atimitro 'numitraś ca purumitro 'parājitaḥ //
219.d:
ऋतजित् सत्यजिच्चैव सुषेणः सेनजित्तथा /
अतिमित्रो ऽनुमित्रश् च पुरुमित्रो ऽपराजितः //
219.m: Ṛtajit, Satyajit, Suṣeṇa, Senajit, / Atimitra, Anumitra, Purumitra, Aparājita,

219.s:
ṛtaś ca ṛtavāg dhātā vidhātā(2) dhāraṇo dhruvaḥ /
vidhāraṇo mahātejā vāsavasya paraḥ sakhā //
219.d:
ऋतश् च ऋतवाग् धाता विधाता(2) धारणो ध्रुवः /
विधारणो महातेजा वासवस्य परः सखा //
219.m: Ṛta, Ṛtavāc, Dhātṛ, Vidhātṛ, Dhāraṇa, Dhruva, / Vidhāraṇa of great splendour, the supreme friend of Indra,

219.s:
īdṛkṣaścāpyadṛkṣaś ca(3) etādṛgamitāśanaḥ /
krīḍitaś ca sadṛkṣaś ca sarabhaś ca mahātapāḥ //
:n
1 sujanastatheti kha.. , gha.. ca
2 viśvātmeti ṅa..
3 īdṛkṣaścānyadṛkṣaśceti cha..
:p 297
219.d:
ईदृक्षश्चाप्यदृक्षश् च(3) एतादृगमिताशनः /
क्रीडितश् च सदृक्षश् च सरभश् च महातपाः //
:न्
1 सुजनस्तथेति ख.. , घ.. च
2 विश्वात्मेति ङ..
3 ईदृक्षश्चान्यदृक्षश्चेति छ..
:प् 297
219.m:
Īdṛkṣa, Adṛkṣa, Etādṛś, Amitāśana, / Krīḍita, Sadṛkṣa, Sarabha of great austerity,
[Note]
1. sujanas tathā in mss. kha. and gha.
2. viśvātmā in ms. ṅa.
3. īdṛkṣaś cānyadṛkṣaś ca in ms. cha.
[p. 297]

219.s:
dhartā dhuryo dhurirbhīma abhimuktaḥ kṣapātsaha(1) /
dhṛtirvasuranādhṛṣyo(2) rāmaḥ kāmo jayo virāṭ //
219.d:
धर्ता धुर्यो धुरिर्भीम अभिमुक्तः क्षपात्सह(1) /
धृतिर्वसुरनाधृष्यो(2) रामः कामो जयो विराट् //
219.m: Dhartṛ, Dhurya, Dhuri, Bhīma, Abhimukta, Kṣapātsaha, / Dhṛti, Vasu, Anādhṛṣya, Rāma, Kāma, Jaya, Virāj—

219.s:
devā ekonapañcāśanmarutastvāmavantu te /
citrāṅgadaścitrarathaḥ citrasenaś ca vai kaliḥ //
219.d:
देवा एकोनपञ्चाशन्मरुतस्त्वामवन्तु ते /
चित्राङ्गदश्चित्ररथः चित्रसेनश् च वै कलिः //
219.m: may these gods, the forty-nine Maruts, protect you; / Citrāṅgada, Citraratha, Citrasena, and Kali,

219.s:
urṇāyurugrasenaś ca dhṛtarāṣṭraś ca nandakaḥ /
hāhā hūhūrnāradaś ca viśvāvasuś ca tumburuḥ //
219.d:
उर्णायुरुग्रसेनश् च धृतराष्ट्रश् च नन्दकः /
हाहा हूहूर्नारदश् च विश्वावसुश् च तुम्बुरुः //
219.m: Ūrṇāyu, Ugrasena, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Nandaka, / Hāhā, Hūhū, Nārada, Viśvāvasu, and Tumburu—

219.s:
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu gandharvā vijayāya te /
pāntu te kurupā mukhyā divyāścāpsarasāṅgaṇāḥ //
219.d:
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु गन्धर्वा विजयाय ते /
पान्तु ते कुरुपा मुख्या दिव्याश्चाप्सरसाङ्गणाः //
219.m: may these Gandharvas consecrate you by aspersion for your victory; / may the chief Kurupas protect you, and the celestial hosts of Apsarases:

219.s:
anavadyā sukeśī ca menakāḥ saha janyayā(3) /
kratusthalā ghṛtācī ca viśvācī puñjikasthalā //
219.d:
अनवद्या सुकेशी च मेनकाः सह जन्यया(3) /
क्रतुस्थला घृताची च विश्वाची पुञ्जिकस्थला //
219.m: Anavadyā, Sukeśī, Menakā together with Janyā, / Kratusthalā, Ghṛtācī, Viśvācī, Puñjikasthalā,

219.s:
pramlocā corvaśī rambhā pañcacūḍā tilottamā /
citralekhā lakṣmaṇā ca puṇḍarīkā ca vāruṇī //
219.d:
प्रम्लोचा चोर्वशी रम्भा पञ्चचूडा तिलोत्तमा /
चित्रलेखा लक्ष्मणा च पुण्डरीका च वारुणी //
219.m: Pramlocā, Urvaśī, Rambhā, Pañcacūḍā, Tilottamā, / Citralekhā, Lakṣmaṇā, Puṇḍarīkā, and Vāruṇī;

219.s:
prahlādo virocano 'tha balirvāṇo 'tha tatsutāḥ /
ete cānye 'bhiṣiñcantu dānavā rākṣasās tathā //
219.d:
प्रह्लादो विरोचनो ऽथ बलिर्वाणो ऽथ तत्सुताः /
एते चान्ये ऽभिषिञ्चन्तु दानवा राक्षसास् तथा //
219.m: Prahlāda, Virocana, Bali, Bāṇa, and their sons— / may these and other Dānavas and Rākṣasas consecrate you by aspersion;

219.s:
hetiś caiva prahetiś ca vidyutsphurjathuragrakāḥ /
yakṣaḥ siddhārmakaḥ pātu māṇibhadraś ca nandanaḥ //
219.d:
हेतिश् चैव प्रहेतिश् च विद्युत्स्फुर्जथुरग्रकाः /
यक्षः सिद्धार्मकः पातु माणिभद्रश् च नन्दनः //
219.m: Heti, Praheti, Vidyutsphūrjathuragraka; / may the Yakṣa Siddhārmaka protect you, and Māṇibhadra and Nandana,

219.s:
piṅgākṣo dyutimāṃś caiva puṣpavanto jayāvahaḥ /
śaṅkhaḥ padmaś ca makaraḥ kacchapaś ca nidhirjaye //
219.d:
पिङ्गाक्षो द्युतिमांश् चैव पुष्पवन्तो जयावहः /
शङ्खः पद्मश् च मकरः कच्छपश् च निधिर्जये //
219.m: Piṅgākṣa, Dyutimant, the Puṣpavants bringing victory; / Śaṅkha, Padma, Makara, and Kacchapa—the treasures for victory;

219.s:
piśācā ūrdhvakeśādyā bhūtā bhūmyādivāsinaḥ /
mahākālaṃ puraskṛtya narasiṃhañca mātaraḥ //
:n
1 abhimuktaḥ kṣamāsaheti ṅa..
2 anādhṛṣta iti ga.. , gha.. ,ña.. ca
3 saha kanyayeti ja..
:p 298
219.d:
पिशाचा ऊर्ध्वकेशाद्या भूता भूम्यादिवासिनः /
महाकालं पुरस्कृत्य नरसिंहञ्च मातरः //
:न्
1 अभिमुक्तः क्षमासहेति ङ..
2 अनाधृष्त इति ग.. , घ.. ,ञ.. च
3 सह कन्ययेति ज..
:प् 298
219.m:
the Piśācas headed by Ūrdhvakeśa, the Bhūtas residing on the earth and elsewhere; / placing Mahākāla and Narasiṃha at the head, the Mothers,
[…]
1. abhimuktaḥ kṣamāsahaḥ in ms. ṅa.
2. anādhṛṣṭaḥ in mss. ga., gha., and ña.
3. saha kanyayā in ms. ja.
[p. 298]

219.s:
guhaḥ skando viśākhastvānnaigameyo 'bhiṣiñcatu /
ḍākinyo yāś ca yoginyaḥ khecarā bhūcarāś ca yāḥ //
219.d:
गुहः स्कन्दो विशाखस्त्वान्नैगमेयो ऽभिषिञ्चतु /
डाकिन्यो याश् च योगिन्यः खेचरा भूचराश् च याः //
219.m: Guha, Skanda, Viśākha, and Naigameya—may they consecrate you by aspersion; / the ḍākinīs and the yoginīs that move in the sky and on earth;

219.s:
garuḍaścāruṇaḥ pāntu sampātipramukhāḥ khagāḥ /
anantādyā mahānāgāḥ śeṣavāsukitakṣakāḥ //
219.d:
गरुडश्चारुणः पान्तु सम्पातिप्रमुखाः खगाः /
अनन्ताद्या महानागाः शेषवासुकितक्षकाः //
219.m: and may Garuḍa and Aruṇa, and the birds headed by Sampāti protect you; / the great serpents headed by Ananta: Śeṣa, Vāsuki, and Takṣaka,

219.s:
airāvato mahāpadmaḥ kambalāśvatarāvubhau /
śaṅkhaḥ karkoṭakaś caiva dhṛtarāṣṭro dhanañjayaḥ //
219.d:
ऐरावतो महापद्मः कम्बलाश्वतरावुभौ /
शङ्खः कर्कोटकश् चैव धृतराष्ट्रो धनञ्जयः //
219.m: Airāvata, Mahāpadma, both Kambala and Aśvatara, / Śaṅkha, Karkoṭaka, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and Dhanañjaya;

219.s:
kumudair āvaṇau padmaḥ puṣpadanto 'tha vāmanaḥ /
supratīko 'ñjano nāgāḥ pāntu tvāṃ sarvataḥ sadā //
219.d:
कुमुदैर् आवणौ पद्मः पुष्पदन्तो ऽथ वामनः /
सुप्रतीको ऽञ्जनो नागाः पान्तु त्वां सर्वतः सदा //
219.m: Kumuda, Airāvaṇa, Padma, Puṣpadanta, Vāmana, / Supratīka, and Añjana—may the [world-elephant] serpents protect you everywhere and always;

219.s:
paitāmahas tathā haṃso vṛṣabhaḥ śaṅkarasya ca /
durgāsiṃhaś ca pāntu tvāṃ yamasya mahiṣas tathā //
219.d:
पैतामहस् तथा हंसो वृषभः शङ्करस्य च /
दुर्गासिंहश् च पान्तु त्वां यमस्य महिषस् तथा //
219.m: and the swan of Brahmā, and the bull of Śaṅkara, / and the lion of Durgā—may they protect you, and the buffalo of Yama;

219.s:
uccaiḥśravāścāśvapatis tathā dhanvantariḥ sadā /
kaustubhaḥ śaṅkarājaś ca vajraṃ śūlañca cakrakaṃ //
219.d:
उच्चैःश्रवाश्चाश्वपतिस् तथा धन्वन्तरिः सदा /
कौस्तुभः शङ्कराजश् च वज्रं शूलञ्च चक्रकं //
219.m: and Uccaiḥśravas the king of horses, and always Dhanvantari; / the Kaustubha jewel, the king of conches, the thunderbolt, trident, and discus,

219.s:
nandako 'strāṇi rakṣantu dharmaś ca vyavasāyakaḥ /
citraguptaś ca daṇḍaś ca piṅgalo mṛtyukālakau //
219.d:
नन्दको ऽस्त्राणि रक्षन्तु धर्मश् च व्यवसायकः /
चित्रगुप्तश् च दण्डश् च पिङ्गलो मृत्युकालकौ //
219.m: the sword Nandaka—may the weapons protect you, and Dharma and Vyavasāyaka, / Citragupta, the staff of punishment, Piṅgala, Mṛtyu, and Kālaka.

219.s:
bālakhilyādimunayo vyāsavālmīkimukhyakāḥ /
pṛthurdilīpo bharato duṣyantaḥ śakrajidvalī(1) //
219.d:
बालखिल्यादिमुनयो व्यासवाल्मीकिमुख्यकाः /
पृथुर्दिलीपो भरतो दुष्यन्तः शक्रजिद्वली(1) //
219.m: The sages beginning with the Bālakhilyas, headed by Vyāsa and Vālmīki; / Pṛthu, Dilīpa, Bharata, Duṣyanta, Śakrajit, and Valī;

219.s:
mallaḥ kakutsthaścānena yuvanāśvo jayadrathaḥ /
māndhātā mucukundaś ca pāntu tvāñca purūravāḥ //
219.d:
मल्लः ककुत्स्थश्चानेन युवनाश्वो जयद्रथः /
मान्धाता मुचुकुन्दश् च पान्तु त्वाञ्च पुरूरवाः //
219.m: Malla, Kakutstha, Anenas, Yuvanāśva, Jayadratha, / Māndhātṛ, Mucukunda, and Purūravas—may they protect you!

219.s:
vāstudevāḥ pañcaviṃśattattvāni vijayāya te /
rukmabhaumaḥ śilābhaumaḥ patālo nīlamūrtikaḥ(2) //
:n
1 śatrujidvalo iti ka.. , kha.. ca
2 nīlamṛttika iti kha.. , gha.. , cha.. , ja.. , ña.. , ṭa.. ca / nīlamūrdhaja iti
ṅa..
:p 299
219.d:
वास्तुदेवाः पञ्चविंशत्तत्त्वानि विजयाय ते /
रुक्मभौमः शिलाभौमः पतालो नीलमूर्तिकः(2) //
:न्
1 शत्रुजिद्वलो इति क.. , ख.. च
2 नीलमृत्तिक इति ख.. , घ.. , छ.. , ज.. , ञ.. , ट.. च / नीलमूर्धज इति
ङ..
:प् 299
219.m:
May the deities of site architecture and the twenty-five principles [grant] you victory: / Rukmabhauma, Śilābhauma, Pātāla, Nīlamūrtika,
[…]
1 "śatrujidvalo" thus in [manuscripts] ka and kha
2 "nīlamṛttika" thus in kha, gha, cha, ja, ña, and ṭa; "nīlamūrdhaja" thus in ṅa. / [Page] 299

219.s:
pītaraktaḥ kṣitiś caiva śvetabhaumo rasātalaṃ /
bhūlloko 'tha bhuvarmukhyā jamvūdvīpādayaḥ śriye //
219.d:
पीतरक्तः क्षितिश् चैव श्वेतभौमो रसातलं /
भूल्लोको ऽथ भुवर्मुख्या जम्वूद्वीपादयः श्रिये //
219.m: Pītarakta, Kṣiti, Śvetabhauma, Rasātala, / the Bhūrloka, the Bhuvarloka above all, and [the continents] beginning with Jambūdvīpa, [serve] for prosperity!

219.s:
uttarāḥ kuravaḥ pāntu ramyā hiraṇyakas tathā(1) /
bhadrāśvaḥ ketumālaś ca varṣaś caiva valāhakaḥ //
219.d:
उत्तराः कुरवः पान्तु रम्या हिरण्यकस् तथा(1) /
भद्राश्वः केतुमालश् च वर्षश् चैव वलाहकः //
219.m: May the northern Kurus protect [you], as well as Ramyaka, Hiraṇyaka, / Bhadrāśva, Ketumāla, and the Valāhaka realm;

219.s:
harivarṣaḥ kimpuruṣa indradvīpaḥ kaśerumān /
tāmravarṇo gabhastimān nāgadvīpaś ca saumyakaḥ //
219.d:
हरिवर्षः किम्पुरुष इन्द्रद्वीपः कशेरुमान् /
ताम्रवर्णो गभस्तिमान् नागद्वीपश् च सौम्यकः //
219.m: Harivarṣa, Kimpuruṣa, Indradvīpa, Kaśerumān, / Tāmravarṇa, Gabhastimān, Nāgadvīpa, Saumyaka,

219.s:
gandharvo varuṇo yaś ca navamaḥ pāntu rājyadāḥ /
himavān hemakūṭaś ca niṣadho nīla eva ca //
219.d:
गन्धर्वो वरुणो यश् च नवमः पान्तु राज्यदाः /
हिमवान् हेमकूटश् च निषधो नील एव च //
219.m: Gandharva, and Varuṇa which is the ninth—givers of kingdoms, may they protect [you]! / The Himavat, Hemakūṭa, Niṣadha, and Nīla;

219.s:
śvetaś ca śṛṅavān merurmālyavān gandhamādanaḥ /
mahendro malayaḥ sahyaḥ śaktimānṛkṣavān giriḥ //
219.d:
श्वेतश् च शृङवान् मेरुर्माल्यवान् गन्धमादनः /
महेन्द्रो मलयः सह्यः शक्तिमानृक्षवान् गिरिः //
219.m: Śveta, Śṛṅgavān, Meru, Mālyavān, Gandhamādana, / Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, Śaktimān, and mount Ṛkṣavān;

219.s:
vindhyaś ca pāripātraś ca girayaḥ śāntidāstu te /
ṛgvedādyāḥ ṣaḍaṅgāni itihāsapurāṇakaṃ //
219.d:
विन्ध्यश् च पारिपात्रश् च गिरयः शान्तिदास्तु ते /
ऋग्वेदाद्याः षडङ्गानि इतिहासपुराणकं //
219.m: the Vindhya and Pāripātra—may these mountains grant you peace! / The [Vedas] beginning with the Ṛgveda, the six auxiliary limbs, the epics and Purāṇas;

219.s:
āyurvedaś ca gandharvadhanurvedopavedakāḥ /
śikṣā kalpo vyākaraṇaṃ niruktaṃ jyotiṣāṅgatiḥ //
219.d:
आयुर्वेदश् च गन्धर्वधनुर्वेदोपवेदकाः /
शिक्षा कल्पो व्याकरणं निरुक्तं ज्योतिषाङ्गतिः //
219.m: Āyurveda, and the secondary Vedas: the Gandharva-veda and Dhanur-veda; / phonetics, ritual, grammar, etymology, and astronomy;

219.s:
chandogāni ca vedāś ca mīmāṃsā nyāyavistaraḥ /
dharmaśāstraṃ purāṇañca vidyā hy etāś caturdaśa //
219.d:
छन्दोगानि च वेदाश् च मीमांसा न्यायविस्तरः /
धर्मशास्त्रं पुराणञ्च विद्या ह्य् एताश् चतुर्दश //
219.m: metrics and the Vedas, Mīmāṃsā, the extensive system of Nyāya, / the Dharmaśāstra, and the Purāṇa—these are indeed the fourteen branches of learning;

219.s:
sāṅkhyaṃ yogaḥ pāśupataṃ vedā vai pañcarātrakaṃ /
kṛtāntapañcakaṃ hy etad gāyatrī ca śivā tathā //
219.d:
साङ्ख्यं योगः पाशुपतं वेदा वै पञ्चरात्रकं /
कृतान्तपञ्चकं ह्य् एतद् गायत्री च शिवा तथा //
219.m: Sāṅkhya, Yoga, Pāśupata, the Vedas, and the Pāñcarātra— / this indeed is the group of five doctrines; and Gāyatrī, Śivā,

219.s:
durgā vidyā ca gāndhārī pāntu tvāṃ śāntidāś ca te /
lavaṇekṣusurāsarpidadhidugdhajalābdhayaḥ //
219.d:
दुर्गा विद्या च गान्धारी पान्तु त्वां शान्तिदाश् च ते /
लवणेक्षुसुरासर्पिदधिदुग्धजलाब्धयः //
219.m: Durgā, Vidyā, and Gāndhārī—may they protect you and grant you peace! / The oceans of salt water, sugarcane juice, wine, clarified butter, curd, milk, and water;

219.s:
catvāraḥ sāgarāḥ pāntu tīrthāni vividhāni ca /
:n
1 hairaṇyakastatheti gha.. , ṅa.. , ja.. ca / hiraṇmayaśtatheti cha..
:p 300
puṣkaraś ca prayāgaś ca prabhāso naimiṣaḥ paraḥ //
219.d:
चत्वारः सागराः पान्तु तीर्थानि विविधानि च /
:न्
1 हैरण्यकस्तथेति घ.. , ङ.. , ज.. च / हिरण्मयश्तथेति छ..
:प् 300
पुष्करश् च प्रयागश् च प्रभासो नैमिषः परः //
219.m:
may the four oceans protect [you], as well as the various sacred fords:
[…]
1 "hairaṇyakas tathā" thus in gha, ṅa, and ja; "hiraṇmayaś tathā" thus in cha. / [Page] 300
Puṣkara, Prayāga, Prabhāsa, the supreme Naimiṣa,

219.s:
gayāśīrṣo brahmaśirastīrthamuttramānasaṃ /
kālodako nandikuṇḍastīrthaṃ pañcanadas tathā //
219.d:
गयाशीर्षो ब्रह्मशिरस्तीर्थमुत्त्रमानसं /
कालोदको नन्दिकुण्डस्तीर्थं पञ्चनदस् तथा //
219.m: Gayāśīrṣa, Brahmaśiras, the sacred ford Uttaramānasa, / Kālodaka, Nandikuṇḍa, and the sacred ford Pañcanada;

219.s:
bhṛgutīrthaṃ prabhāsañca tathā cāmarakaṇṭakaṃ /
jambumārgaś ca vimalaḥ kapilasya tathāśramaḥ //
219.d:
भृगुतीर्थं प्रभासञ्च तथा चामरकण्टकं /
जम्बुमार्गश् च विमलः कपिलस्य तथाश्रमः //
219.m: Bhṛgutīrtha, Prabhāsa, and likewise Amarakaṇṭaka, / Jambūmārga, Vimala, and the hermitage of Kapila;

219.s:
gaṅgādvārakuśāvartau vindhyako nīlaparvataḥ /
varāhaparvataś caiva tīrthaṅkaṇakhalaṃ tathā //
219.d:
गङ्गाद्वारकुशावर्तौ विन्ध्यको नीलपर्वतः /
वराहपर्वतश् चैव तीर्थङ्कणखलं तथा //
219.m: Gaṅgādvāra, Kuśāvarta, mount Vindhya, Nīlaparvata, / the Varāha mountain, and likewise the sacred ford Kanakhala;

219.s:
kālañjaraś ca kedāro rudrakoṭistathaiva ca /
vārāṇasī mahātīrthaṃ vadaryāśrama eva ca //
219.d:
कालञ्जरश् च केदारो रुद्रकोटिस्तथैव च /
वाराणसी महातीर्थं वदर्याश्रम एव च //
219.m: Kālañjara, Kedāra, and Rudrakoṭi as well, / the great sacred ford Vārāṇasī, and Badaryāśrama;

219.s:
dvārakā śrīgiristīrthaṃ tīrthañca puruṣottamaḥ /
śālagrāmotha vārāhaḥ sindhusāgarasaṅgamaḥ //
219.d:
द्वारका श्रीगिरिस्तीर्थं तीर्थञ्च पुरुषोत्तमः /
शालग्रामोथ वाराहः सिन्धुसागरसङ्गमः //
219.m: Dvārakā, the sacred ford Śrīśaila, the sacred ford Puruṣottama, / Śālagrāma, Vārāha, the confluence of the Sindhu and the ocean;

219.s:
phalgutīrthaṃ vindusaraḥ karavīrāśramas tathā /
nadyo gaṅgāsarasvatyaḥ śatadurgaṇḍakī tathā //
219.d:
फल्गुतीर्थं विन्दुसरः करवीराश्रमस् तथा /
नद्यो गङ्गासरस्वत्यः शतदुर्गण्डकी तथा //
219.m: Phalgutīrtha, Bindusaras, and the Karavīra hermitage; / the rivers Gaṅgā, Sarasvatī, Śatadru, and Gaṇḍakī;

219.s:
acchodā ca vipāśā ca vitastā devikā nadī /
kāverī varuṇā caiva niś carā gomatī nadī //
219.d:
अच्छोदा च विपाशा च वितस्ता देविका नदी /
कावेरी वरुणा चैव निश् चरा गोमती नदी //
219.m: Acchodā, Vipāśā, Vitastā, the river Devikā, / Kāverī, Varuṇā, the river Niścarā, and Gomatī;

219.s:
pārā carmaṇvatī rūpā mandākinī mahānadī /
tāpī payoṣṇī veṇā ca gaurī vaitaraṇī tathā //
219.d:
पारा चर्मण्वती रूपा मन्दाकिनी महानदी /
तापी पयोष्णी वेणा च गौरी वैतरणी तथा //
219.m: Pārā, Carmaṇvatī, Rūpā, Mandākinī, the Mahānadī, / Tāpī, Payoṣṇī, Veṇā, Gaurī, and Vaitaraṇī;

219.s:
godāvarī bhīmarathī tuṅgabhadrā praṇī tathā /
candrabhāgā śivā gaurī abhiṣiñcantu pāntu vaḥ(1) //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe abhiṣekamantrā
nāmonaviṃśatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 abhiṣiñcantu pānta ceti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , cha.. , ja.. , ña.. , ṭa..
ca
:p 301
:ś atha viṃśatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
sahāyasampattiḥ
219.d:
गोदावरी भीमरथी तुङ्गभद्रा प्रणी तथा /
चन्द्रभागा शिवा गौरी अभिषिञ्चन्तु पान्तु वः(1) //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे अभिषेकमन्त्रा
नामोनविंशत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 अभिषिञ्चन्तु पान्त चेति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. , छ.. , ज.. , ञ.. , ट..
च
:प् 301
:श् अथ विंशत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
सहायसम्पत्तिः
219.m:
Godāvarī, Bhīmarathī, Tuṅgabhadrā, and Praṇīthā, / Candrabhāgā, Śivā, and Gaurī—may they sprinkle and protect you!
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the two hundred and nineteenth chapter, entitled "Mantras for Consecration by Aspersion".
[…]
1 "abhiṣiñcantu pānta ca" thus in kha, ga, gha, ṅa, cha, ja, ña, and ṭa. / [Page] 301
Now the two hundred and twentieth chapter:
The Acquisition of Allies

220.s:
puṣkara uvāca
so 'bhiṣiktaḥ sahāmātyo jayecchatrūnnṛpottamaḥ /
rājñā senāpatiḥ kāryo brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo 'tha vā //
220.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
सो ऽभिषिक्तः सहामात्यो जयेच्छत्रून्नृपोत्तमः /
राज्ञा सेनापतिः कार्यो ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियो ऽथ वा //
220.m: Puṣkara said: / Once consecrated, the best of kings, accompanied by his ministers, should conquer his enemies. / The king should appoint as commander-in-chief a brāhmaṇa or a kṣatriya,

220.s:
kulīno nītiśāstrajñaḥ pratīhāraś ca nītivit /
dūtaś ca priyavādī syādakṣīṇo 'tibalānvitaḥ //
220.d:
कुलीनो नीतिशास्त्रज्ञः प्रतीहारश् च नीतिवित् /
दूतश् च प्रियवादी स्यादक्षीणो ऽतिबलान्वितः //
220.m: of noble birth and knowledgeable in the science of polity; and a chamberlain skilled in statecraft. / An envoy should speak pleasantly, be undaunted, and be endowed with great strength.

220.s:
tāmbūladhārī nā strī vā bhaktaḥ kleśasahapriyaḥ /
sāndhivigrahikaḥ kāryaḥ ṣāḍguṇyādiviśāradaḥ //
220.d:
ताम्बूलधारी ना स्त्री वा भक्तः क्लेशसहप्रियः /
सान्धिविग्रहिकः कार्यः षाड्गुण्यादिविशारदः //
220.m: The betel-bearer—a man or a woman—should be devoted, fond [of the king], and able to endure hardship. / The minister of peace and war should be appointed, who is adept in the six measures of foreign policy.

220.s:
khaḍgadhārī rakṣakaḥ syātdārathiḥ syādbalādivit /
sūdādhyakṣo hito vijño mahānasagato hi saḥ //
220.d:
खड्गधारी रक्षकः स्यात्दारथिः स्याद्बलादिवित् /
सूदाध्यक्षो हितो विज्ञो महानसगतो हि सः //
220.m: The sword-bearer should be a protector; the charioteer should understand forces and related matters; / the superintendent of the kitchen, stationed in the royal kitchen, should be loyal and discerning.

220.s:
sabhāsadastu dharmajñā lekhako 'kṣaraviddhitaḥ /
āhvānakālavijñāḥ syurhitā dauvārikā janāḥ //
220.d:
सभासदस्तु धर्मज्ञा लेखको ऽक्षरविद्धितः /
आह्वानकालविज्ञाः स्युर्हिता दौवारिका जनाः //
220.m: The court councillors should be knowledgeable in law; the scribe should be proficient in writing and loyal; / the attendants at the door should be loyal and knowledgeable in the proper times for summoning people.

220.s:
ratnādijño dhanādhyakṣaḥ anudvāre hito naraḥ /
syādāyurvedavidvaidyo gajadhyakṣo 'tha hayādivit //
220.d:
रत्नादिज्ञो धनाध्यक्षः अनुद्वारे हितो नरः /
स्यादायुर्वेदविद्वैद्यो गजध्यक्षो ऽथ हयादिवित् //
220.m: The treasurer should know precious gems and the like; the man at the inner gate should be loyal. / The physician should know Āyurveda; the superintendent of elephants should understand horses and related matters;

220.s:
jitaśramo gajāroho hayādhyakṣo hayādivat /
durgādhyakṣo hito dhīmān sthapatirvāstuvedavit //
220.d:
जितश्रमो गजारोहो हयाध्यक्षो हयादिवत् /
दुर्गाध्यक्षो हितो धीमान् स्थपतिर्वास्तुवेदवित् //
220.m: the elephant-rider should be enduring of fatigue; the superintendent of horses should know horses and the like; / the superintendent of the fortress should be loyal and wise; the architect should know the science of site architecture.

220.s:
yantramukte pāṇimukte amukte muktadhārite /
astrācāryo niyuddhe ca kuśalo nṛpaterhitaḥ //
220.d:
यन्त्रमुक्ते पाणिमुक्ते अमुक्ते मुक्तधारिते /
अस्त्राचार्यो नियुद्धे च कुशलो नृपतेर्हितः //
220.m: The master of weapons, skilled in missiles discharged from machines, hand-thrown weapons, / handheld non-projectiles, and retained-and-released weapons, as well as in hand-to-hand combat, should be loyal to the king.

220.s:
vṛddhaścāntaḥpurādhyakṣaḥ pañcāśadvārṣikāḥstriyaḥ /
:p 302
saptatyavdāstu puruṣāś careyuḥ sarvakarmasu //
220.d:
वृद्धश्चान्तःपुराध्यक्षः पञ्चाशद्वार्षिकाःस्त्रियः /
:प् 302
सप्तत्यव्दास्तु पुरुषाश् चरेयुः सर्वकर्मसु //
220.m:
The overseer of the women's quarters should be elderly; women of fifty years [of age],
[Page 302]
and men of seventy years should perform duties in all affairs.

220.s:
jāgratsyādāyudhāgāre jñātvā vṛttirvidhīyate /
uttamādhamamadhyāni buddhvā karmāṇi pārthivaḥ //
220.d:
जाग्रत्स्यादायुधागारे ज्ञात्वा वृत्तिर्विधीयते /
उत्तमाधममध्यानि बुद्ध्वा कर्माणि पार्थिवः //
220.m: The guard in the armoury should be alert; having assessed them, livelihoods are assigned. / Having understood high, low, and intermediate tasks, the king

220.s:
uttamādhamamadhyāni puruṣāṇi niyojayet /
jyecchuḥ pṛthivīṃ rājā sahāyānanayoddhitān //
220.d:
उत्तमाधममध्यानि पुरुषाणि नियोजयेत् /
ज्येच्छुः पृथिवीं राजा सहायाननयोद्धितान् //
220.m: should appoint men to high, low, and intermediate [positions]. / Desiring to conquer the earth, the king, supported by his helpers,

220.s:
dharmiṣṭhān dharmakāyeṣu śūrān saṅgrāmakarmasu /
nipuṇānarthakṛtyeṣu(1) sarvatra ca tathā śucīn //
220.d:
धर्मिष्ठान् धर्मकायेषु शूरान् सङ्ग्रामकर्मसु /
निपुणानर्थकृत्येषु(1) सर्वत्र च तथा शुचीन् //
220.m: [should appoint] the most righteous to pious works, the valiant to duties of war, / the skilled to financial duties, and the pure everywhere;

220.s:
strīṣu ṣaṇḍānniyuñjīta tīkṣṇān dāruṇakarmasu /
yo yatra vidito rājñā śucitvena tu tannaraṃ //
220.d:
स्त्रीषु षण्डान्नियुञ्जीत तीक्ष्णान् दारुणकर्मसु /
यो यत्र विदितो राज्ञा शुचित्वेन तु तन्नरं //
220.m: he should appoint eunuchs among women, the fierce to harsh tasks; / and whatever man is known by the king to be honest in a particular post,

220.s:
dharme cārthe ca kāme ca niyuñjītādhame 'dhamān /
rājā yathārhaṃ kuryācca upādhābhiḥ parīkṣitān //
220.d:
धर्मे चार्थे च कामे च नियुञ्जीताधमे ऽधमान् /
राजा यथार्हं कुर्याच्च उपाधाभिः परीक्षितान् //
220.m: he should assign him to virtue, wealth, and pleasure, and base men to base tasks. / The king should assign appropriately those tested through secret tests.

220.s:
samantro ca yathānyāyāt kuryāddhastivanecarān /
tatpadānveṣaṇe yattānadhyakṣāṃstatra kārayet //
220.d:
समन्त्रो च यथान्यायात् कुर्याद्धस्तिवनेचरान् /
तत्पदान्वेषणे यत्तानध्यक्षांस्तत्र कारयेत् //
220.m: He should appoint counsellors, and, according to rule, elephant-trackers; / he should set overseers over them who are diligent in tracking footsteps.

220.s:
yasmin karmaṇi kauśalyaṃ yasya tasmin niyojayet /
pitṛpaitāmahān bhṛtyān sarvakarmasu yojayet //
220.d:
यस्मिन् कर्मणि कौशल्यं यस्य तस्मिन् नियोजयेत् /
पितृपैतामहान् भृत्यान् सर्वकर्मसु योजयेत् //
220.m: One should appoint a man to whatever work he possesses skill in. / One should employ hereditary servants in all duties,

220.s:
vinā dāyādakṛtyeṣu tatra te hi samāgatāḥ /
pararājagṛhāt prāptān janān saṃśrayakāmyayā(2) //
220.d:
विना दायादकृत्येषु तत्र ते हि समागताः /
परराजगृहात् प्राप्तान् जनान् संश्रयकाम्यया(2) //
220.m: except in affairs concerning heirs, for there they have connections. / Those people who have arrived from another king's domain seeking refuge,

220.s:
duṣṭānapyatha vāduṣṭān saṃśrayeta prayatnataḥ /
duṣṭaṃ jñātvā viśvasenna tadvṛttiṃ vartayedvaśe //
220.d:
दुष्टानप्यथ वादुष्टान् संश्रयेत प्रयत्नतः /
दुष्टं ज्ञात्वा विश्वसेन्न तद्वृत्तिं वर्तयेद्वशे //
220.m: whether wicked or virtuous, he should take into refuge with care; / knowing one to be wicked, he should not trust him, but should keep his livelihood under control.

220.s:
deśāntarāgatān pārśve cāraijñātvā hi pūjayet /
śatravo 'gnivarṣaṃ sarpo nistriṃśamapi caikataḥ //
:n
1 ripananarthakṛtyeṣviti kha..
2 janānāśrayakāmyayeti kha..
:p 303
220.d:
देशान्तरागतान् पार्श्वे चारैज्ञात्वा हि पूजयेत् /
शत्रवो ऽग्निवर्षं सर्पो निस्त्रिंशमपि चैकतः //
:न्
1 रिपननर्थकृत्येष्विति ख..
2 जनानाश्रयकाम्ययेति ख..
:प् 303
220.m:
Having ascertained through spies those who have arrived from other lands, he should honour them at his side. / Enemies, a shower of fire, a serpent, and a sword, on the one hand,
[…]
1 "ripān anarthakṛtyeṣu" thus in kha
2 "janān āśrayakāmyayā" thus in kha. / [Page] 303

220.s:
bhṛtyā vaśiṣṭaṃ vijñeyāḥ kubhṛṭyāś ca tathaikataḥ /
cāracakṣurbhavedrājā niyuñjīta sadācarān //
220.d:
भृत्या वशिष्टं विज्ञेयाः कुभृट्याश् च तथैकतः /
चारचक्षुर्भवेद्राजा नियुञ्जीत सदाचरान् //
220.m: Subservient servants should be known, and likewise bad servants, all on one side. / The king should have spies for his eyes; he should always employ spies

220.s:
janasyāvihitān saumyāṃs tathājñātān parasparaṃ /
vaṇijo mantrakuśalān sāṃvatsaracikitsakān //
220.d:
जनस्याविहितान् सौम्यांस् तथाज्ञातान् परस्परं /
वणिजो मन्त्रकुशलान् सांवत्सरचिकित्सकान् //
220.m: who are unobtrusive to the people, mild-mannered, and unknown to one another: / merchants skilled in consultation, astrologers, physicians,

220.s:
tathā pravrajitākārān balābalavivekinaḥ /
naikasya rājā śraddadhyācchraddadhyād bahuvākyataḥ //
220.d:
तथा प्रव्रजिताकारान् बलाबलविवेकिनः /
नैकस्य राजा श्रद्दध्याच्छ्रद्दध्याद् बहुवाक्यतः //
220.m: likewise those having the appearance of ascetics, who discern strength and weakness. / The king should not trust a single [spy]; he should trust [only] from multiple reports.

220.s:
rāgāparāgau bhṛtyānāṃ janasya ca guṇāguṇān /
śubhānāmaśubhānāñca jñānaṅkuryādvaśāya ca //
220.d:
रागापरागौ भृत्यानां जनस्य च गुणागुणान् /
शुभानामशुभानाञ्च ज्ञानङ्कुर्याद्वशाय च //
220.m: The affection and disaffection of servants, and the virtues and flaws of the people, / and auspicious and inauspicious matters he should investigate for the sake of control.

220.s:

220.m:
He should perform acts that produce affection and avoid deceitful acts that cause disaffection. / Endowed with the fortune of his people's affection, a king becomes truly a king by pleasing his people.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the two hundred and twentieth chapter, named "The Acquisition of Allies."
Now, the two hundred and twenty-first chapter.
Puṣkara said:
A servant should obey the king's command like a disciple [serving] a master of true fortune.
He should not disregard the king's speech; he should speak pleasantly and agreeably.
When [the king] is in private, that which is disagreeable but beneficial should be spoken.
When appointed, he should not steal wealth, nor should he disregard [the king's] honor.
And he should not imitate the king's dress, speech, or conduct.
An officer who frequents the inner apartments, with enemies and rejected persons,
[Page 304]
a servant should not associate; and he should keep the king's secret.
Displaying some skill, he should distinguish the king.
What secret is disclosed by the king, he should not reveal to the world.
Or, when another is being commanded, he should say: 'What may I do?'
And he should wear the clothing, jewel, and ornament given by the king.

220.m:
Without being instructed, he should not enter at the door, nor look at the king in an unsuitable place.
Yawning, spitting, coughing, anger, reclining on a couch,
frowning, breaking wind, and belching—he should avoid these in his presence.
In proclaiming his own virtues, he should skillfully employ others instead.
Deceit, fickleness, slander, atheism, meanness,
and restlessness must always be avoided by one who depends on the king.
Endowing himself through his own effort with learning, sciences, and crafts,
one who enhances prosperity should then serve the king for the sake of prosperity.
His sons, favorites, and ministers should always be greeted with respect.
He should not place trust in the counsellors; he should act pleasingly to the king's heart.
He should abandon one who is disaffected; from one who is favorably disposed, one who knows kings should seek his livelihood.
And when not asked, he should not speak to him; yet he may do so in times of danger.
He is pleased, he accepts words, and he does not suspect [one] in secret;

he inquires after health and the like, and he offers a seat;
he is delighted by hearing stories of him, and even disagreeable things cause joy;
he accepts even a small [gift] that is given, and remembers him even in other conversations—
such service should be rendered to one who is favorably disposed; he should avoid serving another.
Thus, in the Great Purāṇa of Agni, the two hundred and twentieth chapter, entitled “The Conduct of a Dependent [of a King]”.
Now, the two hundred and twenty-first chapter:
The Excellence of Fortresses.
Puṣkara said:
I shall declare the assets of a fortress: the king should reside in a fortified region,
predominantly populated by Vaiśyas and Śūdras, inaccessible to adversaries,
having a few Brahmins, and many laborers.
A territory not dependent on rain, possessing well-distributed water, is praised,
unharassed by enemies, endowed with flowers, fruits, and grain,
impenetrable to hostile armies, free from beasts of prey and thieves.
Having constructed one of the six [types of] fortresses there, the strong [king] should reside [there]:

220.m:
a desert fortress, an earthen fortress, and likewise a human fortress,
a forest fortress, a water fortress, and a mountain fortress, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
Best of all is the mountain fortress, impregnable and capable of defeating others.
[Notes]
1. "puṣpaphaladhānyadhanānvitaḥ" according to manuscripts ga, gha, ña, and ṭa. / [Page 306]
There [should be] a city with markets and the like, sanctuaries of deities, and so forth;
provided with machines and weapons, and endowed with water, it is an excellent fortress.
I shall declare the protection of the king: the ruler must be protected from poison and other [harms].
The śirīṣa with its five parts, ground in urine, destroys poison.
Śatāvarī, chinnaruhā, and taṇḍulīyaka are poison-destroying,
as well as koṣātakī, kalhārī, brāhmī, citrapaṭolikā,
maṇḍūkaparṇī, vārāhī, and dhātryānandaka.
unmādinī, somarājī, antidote [herbs], and gemstones.
Living in a fortress endowed with the characteristics of proper site architecture, he should sacrifice to the gods.
And he should protect the subjects, conquer the wicked, and cause gifts to be distributed.
By stealing the property of the gods and the like, one would dwell in hell for a kalpa.
A king devoted to the worship of the gods should build temples.

ऐष्टकाच्छैलजं पुण्यं शैलजात् स्वर्णरत्नजं //
क्रीडन् सुरगृहं कुर्वन् भुक्तिमुक्तिमवाप्नुयात् ///
चित्रक्वद् गीतवाद्यादिप्रेक्षणीयादिदानकृत् //
तैलाज्यमधुदुग्धाद्यैः स्नाप्य देवं दिवं व्रजेत् ///
पूजयेत् पालयेद्विप्रान् द्विजस्वन्न हरेन्नृपः //
सुवर्णमेकं गामेकां भूमेरप्येकमङ्गुलं ///
हरन्नरकमाप्नोति यावदाहूतसम्प्लवं //
दुराचारन्न द्विषेच्च सर्वपापेष्वपि स्थितं ///
नैवास्ति ब्राह्मणबधात् पापं गुरुतरं क्वचित् //

220.m:
Temples must be protected, and deities must be installed.
A wooden [shrine] yields more merit than an earthen one; one made of bricks yields more than a wooden one;
a stone [shrine] yields more merit than a brick one; and one made of gold and gems yields more than a stone one.
Even while playing, one who builds a house for the gods obtains worldly enjoyment and liberation;
likewise one who paints pictures and provides shows such as songs and instrumental music.
Bathing the deity with oil, clarified butter, honey, milk, and other liquids, one goes to heaven.
The king should worship and protect Brahmins; he should not confiscate a Brahmin's property.
By taking [even] a single piece of gold, a single cow, or a single finger's breadth of land,
one enters hell until the universal dissolution.
One should not hate [a Brahmin] of wicked conduct, even if he is immersed in all sins.
Nowhere is there any sin heavier than killing a Brahmin.
[page 307]
They can make a non-god into a god, and make a god into a non-god;
for Brahmins are illustrious; he must always bow down to them.
A weeping Brahmin woman destroys family, kingdom, and subjects.
And a righteous king should protect virtuous women.
A woman should be cheerful, exclusively skilled in household duties,

220.s:

mṛte bhartari svaryāyāt brahmacarye sthitāṅganā //
paraveśmarucir nasyānna syāt kalahaśālinī ///
maṇḍanaṃ varjayennārī tathā proṣitabhartṛkā //
devatārādhanaparā tiṣṭhedbhartṛhite ratā ///
dhārayenmaṅgalārthāya kiñcidābharaṇantathā //
bhartrāgniṃ yā viśennārī sāpi svagamavāpnuyāt ///
śriyaḥ sampūjanaṅkāryaṃ gṛhasammārjanādikaṃ //
dvādaśyāṃ kārttike viṣṇuṃ gāṃ savatsāṃ dadettathā ///
sāvitryā rakṣito bhartā satyācāravratena ca(2) //
saptamyāṃ mārgaśīrṣe tu site 'bhyarcya divākaraṃ ///
putrānāpnoti ca strīha nātra kāryā vicāraṇā //26///
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe rājadharmo nāma
ekaviṃśatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 tānna hiṃsyādyadaiva tu iti ja..
220.d:
सुसंस्कृतोपस्करया व्यये चामुक्तहस्तया //
यस्मै दद्यात्पिता त्वेनां शुश्रूषेत्तं पतिं सदा ///
मृते भर्तरि स्वर्यायात् ब्रह्मचर्ये स्थिताङ्गना //
परवेश्मरुचिर् नस्यान्न स्यात् कलहशालिनी ///
मण्डनं वर्जयेन्नारी तथा प्रोषितभर्तृका //
देवताराधनपरा तिष्ठेद्भर्तृहिते रता ///
धारयेन्मङ्गलार्थाय किञ्चिदाभरणन्तथा //
भर्त्राग्निं या विशेन्नारी सापि स्वगमवाप्नुयात् ///
श्रियः सम्पूजनङ्कार्यं गृहसम्मार्जनादिकं //
द्वादश्यां कार्त्तिके विष्णुं गां सवत्सां ददेत्तथा ///
सावित्र्या रक्षितो भर्ता सत्याचारव्रतेन च(2) //
सप्तम्यां मार्गशीर्षे तु सिते ऽभ्यर्च्य दिवाकरं ///
पुत्रानाप्नोति च स्त्रीह नात्र कार्या विचारणा //26///
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे राजधर्मो नाम
एकविंशत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 तान्न हिंस्याद्यदैव तु इति ज..
220.m:
with well-maintained utensils, and not liberal in spending.
She should always attend upon that husband to whom her father gives her.
When her husband has died, a woman who remains in celibacy goes to heaven.
She should have no desire for another's house, nor should she be quarrelsome.
A woman whose husband is away on a journey should likewise abandon adornment;
she should remain devoted to the worship of the gods, delighting in her husband's welfare,
and she should wear a small ornament for the sake of auspiciousness.
A woman who enters the fire with her husband also attains heaven.
Worship of Śrī should be performed, as well as sweeping the house and other tasks.
On the twelfth lunar day in the month of Kārttika, [she should worship] Viṣṇu and give a cow with its calf.
A husband is protected by the Sāvitrī [mantra] and by the votive observance of truthful conduct.
Having worshipped the Sun on the seventh lunar day in the bright fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa,
a woman in this world obtains sons; here there is no doubt. //26//
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the two hundred and twenty-first chapter, entitled 'Duties of the King'.
[note]
1. 'tānna hiṃsyādyadaiva tu' in manuscript ja.

220.s:
2 satyavān suvratena ceti gha.. , ña.. ca
:p 308
:ś atha dvāviṃśatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
rājadharmāḥ
220.d:
2 सत्यवान् सुव्रतेन चेति घ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 308
:श् अथ द्वाविंशत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
राजधर्माः
220.m:
2. 'satyavān suvratena ca' in manuscripts gha and ña.
[page 308]
Now the two hundred and twenty-second chapter:
Duties of the King.

222.s:
puṣkara uvāca
grāmasyādhipatiṃ kuryāddaśagrāmādhipaṃ nṛpaḥ /
śatagrāmādhipañcānyaṃ tathaiva viṣayeśvaraṃ //
222.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
ग्रामस्याधिपतिं कुर्याद्दशग्रामाधिपं नृपः /
शतग्रामाधिपञ्चान्यं तथैव विषयेश्वरं //
222.m:
Puṣkara said:
The king should appoint a lord over a village, a lord over ten villages, / and another lord over a hundred villages, as well as a ruler over a province.

222.s:
teṣāṃ bhogavibhāgaś ca bhavet karmānurūpataḥ /
nityameva tathā kāryaṃ teṣāñcāraiḥ parīkṣaṇaṃ //
222.d:
तेषां भोगविभागश् च भवेत् कर्मानुरूपतः /
नित्यमेव तथा कार्यं तेषाञ्चारैः परीक्षणं //
222.m: The division of their emoluments should be according to their work; / and an examination of them through spies should constantly be conducted.

222.s:
grāme doṣān samutpannān grāmeśaḥ prasamaṃ nayet /
aśakto daśapālasya sa tu gatvā nivedayet //
222.d:
ग्रामे दोषान् समुत्पन्नान् ग्रामेशः प्रसमं नयेत् /
अशक्तो दशपालस्य स तु गत्वा निवेदयेत् //
222.m: The village lord should settle wrongs that arise in the village; / if unable, he should go and report [them] to the protector of ten [villages].

222.s:
śrutvāpi daśapālo 'pi tatra yuktimupācaret /
vittādyāpnoti rājā vai viṣayāttu surakṣitāt //
222.d:
श्रुत्वापि दशपालो ऽपि तत्र युक्तिमुपाचरेत् /
वित्ताद्याप्नोति राजा वै विषयात्तु सुरक्षितात् //
222.m: Having heard it, even the protector of ten [villages] should apply a remedy there. / For the king obtains wealth and the like from a well-protected province.

222.s:
dhanavāndharmamāpnoti dhanavān kāmamaśnute /
ucchidyante vinā hy arthaiḥ(1) kriyā grīṣme saridyathā //
222.d:
धनवान्धर्ममाप्नोति धनवान् काममश्नुते /
उच्छिद्यन्ते विना ह्य् अर्थैः(1) क्रिया ग्रीष्मे सरिद्यथा //
222.m: A man of wealth attains righteousness; a man of wealth experiences desire. / Without resources, actions are cut off, just as a river in the hot season.

222.s:
viśeṣo nāsti lokeṣe patitasyādhanasya ca /
patitānna tu gṛhṇanti daridro na prayacchati //
222.d:
विशेषो नास्ति लोकेषे पतितस्याधनस्य च /
पतितान्न तु गृह्णन्ति दरिद्रो न प्रयच्छति //
222.m: In this world, there is no difference between a fallen man and a man without wealth: / people do not take food from a fallen man, and a poor man does not give [it].

222.s:
dhanahīnasya bhāryāpi naikā syādupavartinī(2) /
rāṣṭrapīḍākaro rājā narake vasate ciraṃ //
222.d:
धनहीनस्य भार्यापि नैका स्यादुपवर्तिनी(2) /
राष्ट्रपीडाकरो राजा नरके वसते चिरं //
222.m: Even his single wife does not attend upon a man devoid of wealth. / A king who oppresses his realm dwells in hell for a long time.

222.s:
nityaṃ rājñā tathā bhāvyaṃ garbhiṇī sahadharmiṇī /
yahā svaṃ sukhamutsṛjya garbhasya sukhamāvahet(3) //
:n
1 vinā hy arthamiti gha.. , ña.. ca
2 naiva syādvaśavartinīti kha.. , ṭa.. ca / naiva syādvaśavartinīti gha.. , ja..
, ña.. ca
3 sukhamāharediti ja.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 309
222.d:
नित्यं राज्ञा तथा भाव्यं गर्भिणी सहधर्मिणी /
यहा स्वं सुखमुत्सृज्य गर्भस्य सुखमावहेत्(3) //
:न्
1 विना ह्य् अर्थमिति घ.. , ञ.. च
2 नैव स्याद्वशवर्तिनीति ख.. , ट.. च / नैव स्याद्वशवर्तिनीति घ.. , ज..
, ञ.. च
3 सुखमाहरेदिति ज.. , ट.. च
:प् 309
222.m:
The king should always be like a pregnant lawful wife: / just as she, relinquishing her own comfort, brings comfort to the child in her womb.
[note]
1. 'vinā hy artham' in manuscripts gha and ña.
2. 'naiva syādvaśavartinī' in manuscripts kha and ṭa; 'naiva syādvaśavartinī' in manuscripts gha, ja, and ña.
3. 'sukhamāhared' in manuscripts ja and ṭa.
[page 309]

222.s:
kiṃ yajñaistapasā tasya prajā yasya na rakṣitāḥ /
surakṣitāḥ prajā yasya svargastasya gṛhopamaḥ //
222.d:
किं यज्ञैस्तपसा तस्य प्रजा यस्य न रक्षिताः /
सुरक्षिताः प्रजा यस्य स्वर्गस्तस्य गृहोपमः //
222.m: What use are sacrifices and ascetic austerity to him whose subjects are not protected? / For him whose subjects are well-protected, heaven is like [his own] home.

222.s:
arakṣitāḥ prajā yasya narakaṃ tasya mandiraṃ /
rājā ṣaḍbhāgamādatte sukṛtādduṣkṛtādapi //
222.d:
अरक्षिताः प्रजा यस्य नरकं तस्य मन्दिरं /
राजा षड्भागमादत्ते सुकृताद्दुष्कृतादपि //
222.m: For him whose subjects are unprotected, hell is his residence. / The king receives a sixth share of good deeds as well as of bad deeds.

222.s:
dharmāgamo rakṣaṇācca pāpamāpnotyarakṣaṇāt /
subhagā viṭabhīteva rājavallabhataskaraiḥ //
222.d:
धर्मागमो रक्षणाच्च पापमाप्नोत्यरक्षणात् /
सुभगा विटभीतेव राजवल्लभतस्करैः //
222.m: The arrival of merit comes from protection; from non-protection he incurs sin. / Like a charming woman afraid of a libertine, subjects being devoured

222.s:
bhakṣyamāṇāḥ prajā rakṣyāḥ kāyasthaiś ca viśeṣataḥ /
rakṣitā tadbhayebhyastu rājño bhavati sā prajā(1)
222.d:
भक्ष्यमाणाः प्रजा रक्ष्याः कायस्थैश् च विशेषतः /
रक्षिता तद्भयेभ्यस्तु राज्ञो भवति सा प्रजा(1)
222.m: by royal favourites and thieves, and especially by scribes, are to be protected. / But when protected from those fears, they become the king's own subjects;

222.s:
arakṣitā sā bhavati teṣāmeveha bhojanaṃ /
duṣṭasammardanaṃ kuryācchāstroktaṃ karamādadet(2) //
222.d:
अरक्षिता सा भवति तेषामेवेह भोजनं /
दुष्टसम्मर्दनं कुर्याच्छास्त्रोक्तं करमाददेत्(2) //
222.m: unprotected, they become food for those very people here. / He should suppress the wicked and collect the tax prescribed by the scripture.

222.s:
koṣe praveśayedardhaṃ nityañcārdhaṃ dvije dadet(3) /
nidhiṃ dvijottamaḥ prāpya gṛhṇīyātsakalaṃ tathā //
222.d:
कोषे प्रवेशयेदर्धं नित्यञ्चार्धं द्विजे ददेत्(3) /
निधिं द्विजोत्तमः प्राप्य गृह्णीयात्सकलं तथा //
222.m: He should put half into the treasury, and constantly give half to the twice-born. / An eminent twice-born man, finding a treasure trove, may take it entirely.

222.s:
caturthamaṣṭamaṃ bhāgaṃ tathā ṣoḍaśamaṃ dvijaḥ /
varṇakrameṇa dadyācca nidhiṃ pātre tu dharmataḥ //
222.d:
चतुर्थमष्टमं भागं तथा षोडशमं द्विजः /
वर्णक्रमेण दद्याच्च निधिं पात्रे तु धर्मतः //
222.m: A twice-born man should give a fourth, an eighth, or a sixteenth part, / in order of caste, of the treasure trove to a worthy recipient according to dharma.

222.s:
anṛtantu vadan daṇḍyaḥ(4) suvittasyāṃśamaṣṭamaṃ /
praṇaṣṭasvāmikamṛkthaṃ rājātryabdaṃ nidhāpayet //
222.d:
अनृतन्तु वदन् दण्ड्यः(4) सुवित्तस्यांशमष्टमं /
प्रणष्टस्वामिकमृक्थं राजात्र्यब्दं निधापयेत् //
222.m: One speaking untruth, however, should be fined an eighth part of the valuable property. / A property whose owner is lost, the king should keep in deposit for three years.

222.s:
arvāk tryabdāddharet svāmī pareṇa nṛpatirharet /
mamedamiti yo brūyāt so 'rthayukto yathāvidhi //
222.d:
अर्वाक् त्र्यब्दाद्धरेत् स्वामी परेण नृपतिर्हरेत् /
ममेदमिति यो ब्रूयात् सो ऽर्थयुक्तो यथाविधि //
222.m: Before three years, the owner may take it; after that, the king may take it. / Whoever should say, 'This is mine', having substantiated it in accordance with rule,

222.s:
sampādya rūpasaṅkhyādīn svāmī tad dravyamarhati /
:n
1 satprajā iti gha.. , ña.. ca
2 subhagā viṭabhītevetyādiḥ, karamādadedityantaḥ pāṭhaḥ jha..
pustake nāsti
3 dvije 'rpayediti ña.. , ṭa.. ca
4 amṛtaṃ vadato grāhyamiti ṭa..
:p 310
bāladāyādikamṛkthaṃ(1) tāvadrājānupālayet //
222.d:
सम्पाद्य रूपसङ्ख्यादीन् स्वामी तद् द्रव्यमर्हति /
:न्
1 सत्प्रजा इति घ.. , ञ.. च
2 सुभगा विटभीतेवेत्यादिः, करमाददेदित्यन्तः पाठः झ..
पुस्तके नास्ति
3 द्विजे ऽर्पयेदिति ञ.. , ट.. च
4 अमृतं वदतो ग्राह्यमिति ट..
:प् 310
बालदायादिकमृक्थं(1) तावद्राजानुपालयेत् //
222.m:
establishing its form, quantity, and so forth, as the owner, is entitled to that property.
[note]
1. 'satprajā' in manuscripts gha and ña.
2. The text beginning with 'subhagā viṭabhīteva' up to 'karamādadet' is not found in manuscript jha.
3. 'dvije 'rpayed' in manuscripts ña and ṭa.
4. 'amṛtaṃ vadato grāhyam' in manuscript ṭa.
[page 310]
The inheritance of a minor heir and the like the king should protect

222.s:
yāvatsyātsa samāvṛtto yāvadvātītaśaiśavaḥ /
bālaputrāsu caivaṃ syādrakṣaṇaṃ niṣkalāsu ca //
222.d:
यावत्स्यात्स समावृत्तो यावद्वातीतशैशवः /
बालपुत्रासु चैवं स्याद्रक्षणं निष्कलासु च //
222.m: until he has returned from study or until his childhood is past. / And there should be protection in the same manner for women with young sons, for childless women,

222.s:
pativratāsu ca strīṣu vidhabāsvāturāsu ca /
jīvantīnāntu tāsāṃ ye saṃhareyuḥ svavāndhavāḥ //
222.d:
पतिव्रतासु च स्त्रीषु विधबास्वातुरासु च /
जीवन्तीनान्तु तासां ये संहरेयुः स्ववान्धवाः //
222.m: for women devoted to their husbands, for widows, and for the diseased. / But if their own kinsmen should seize [the property] of those women while they are alive,

222.s:
tāñchiṣyāccauradaṇḍena dhārmikaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ /
sāmānyato hṛtañcauraistadvai dadyāt svayaṃ nṛpaḥ //
222.d:
ताञ्छिष्याच्चौरदण्डेन धार्मिकः पृथिवीपतिः /
सामान्यतो हृतञ्चौरैस्तद्वै दद्यात् स्वयं नृपः //
222.m: the righteous ruler of the earth should punish them with the punishment for thieves. / What has been stolen by thieves in general, the king himself should indeed restore.

222.s:
caurarakṣādhikāribhyo rājāpi hṛtamāpnuyāt /
ahṛte yo hṛtaṃ brūyānniḥsāryo daṇḍya eva saḥ //
222.d:
चौररक्षाधिकारिभ्यो राजापि हृतमाप्नुयात् /
अहृते यो हृतं ब्रूयान्निःसार्यो दण्ड्य एव सः //
222.m: The king should also recover what was stolen from the officers in charge of guarding against thieves. / He who claims a theft when nothing was stolen should be expelled and fined.

222.s:
na tadrājñā pradātavyaṃ gṛhe yad gṛhagair hṛtaṃ /
svarāṣṭrapaṇyādādadyādrājā viṃśatimaṃ dvija //
222.d:
न तद्राज्ञा प्रदातव्यं गृहे यद् गृहगैर् हृतं /
स्वराष्ट्रपण्यादादद्याद्राजा विंशतिमं द्विज //
222.m: What is stolen in a house by members of the household is not to be made good by the king. / O twice-born one, from merchandise of his own kingdom the king should take a twentieth [part]

222.s:
śulkāṃśaṃ paradeśācca kṣayavyayaprakāśakaṃ /
jñātvā saṅkalpayecchulkaṃ lābhaṃ vaṇigyathāpnuyāt //
222.d:
शुल्कांशं परदेशाच्च क्षयव्ययप्रकाशकं /
ज्ञात्वा सङ्कल्पयेच्छुल्कं लाभं वणिग्यथाप्नुयात् //
222.m: as a customs share; and knowing [the merchandise] from foreign countries with its loss and expenditure clearly demonstrated, / he should determine the customs duty so that the merchant may make a profit.

222.s:
viṃśāṃśaṃ lābhamādadyāddaṇḍanīyastato 'nyathā /
strīṇāṃ pravrajitānāñca(2) taraśulkaṃ vivarjayet //
222.d:
विंशांशं लाभमादद्याद्दण्डनीयस्ततो ऽन्यथा /
स्त्रीणां प्रव्रजितानाञ्च(2) तरशुल्कं विवर्जयेत् //
222.m:
He should take a twentieth part of the profit; otherwise he should be punished.
He should exempt women and ascetics from the ferry-toll.

222.s:
tareṣu dāsadoṣeṇa naṣṭaṃ dāsāṃstu dāpayet /
śūkadhānyeṣu ṣaḍbhāgaṃ śimbidhānye tathāṣṭamaṃ //
222.d:
तरेषु दासदोषेण नष्टं दासांस्तु दापयेत् /
शूकधान्येषु षड्भागं शिम्बिधान्ये तथाष्टमं //
222.m:
For what is lost at ferries through the fault of the boatmen, he should make the boatmen pay.
[He should take] a sixth part of bearded grains, and an eighth part of pod-grains.

222.s:
rājā vanyārthamādadyāddeśakālānurūpakaṃ /
pañcaṣaḍbhāgamādadyād rājā paśuhiraṇyayoḥ //
222.d:
राजा वन्यार्थमादद्याद्देशकालानुरूपकं /
पञ्चषड्भागमादद्याद् राजा पशुहिरण्ययोः //
222.m:
The king should take forest produce in accordance with place and time.
He should take a fifth or a sixth part of cattle and gold.

222.s:
gandhauṣadhirasānāñca puṣpamūlaphalasya ca /
:n
1 bāladāyādikaṃ yuktamiti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ña.. ca
2 strīṇāñcaiva dvijātīnāmiti ṭa..
:p 311
patraśākatṛṇānāñca vaṃśavaiṇavacarmaṇāṃ //
222.d:
गन्धौषधिरसानाञ्च पुष्पमूलफलस्य च /
:न्
1 बालदायादिकं युक्तमिति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ञ.. च
2 स्त्रीणाञ्चैव द्विजातीनामिति ट..
:प् 311
पत्रशाकतृणानाञ्च वंशवैणवचर्मणां //
222.m:
And of perfumes, medicinal herbs, and plant juices, and of flowers, roots, and fruits,
[...]
[Variant reading:] 1 "bāladāyādikaṃ yuktam" in MSS kha, ga, gha, and ña.
[Variant reading:] 2 "strīṇāñcaiva dvijātīnām" in MS ṭa.
and of leaves, vegetables, and grasses, and of bamboo, cane, and hides,

222.s:
vaidalānāñca bhāṇḍānāṃ sarvasyāśmamayasya ca /
ṣaḍbhāgameva cādadyān madhumāṃsasya sarpiṣaḥ //
222.d:
वैदलानाञ्च भाण्डानां सर्वस्याश्ममयस्य च /
षड्भागमेव चादद्यान् मधुमांसस्य सर्पिषः //
222.m:
and of earthen pots and everything made of stone,
he should take only a sixth part, and also of honey, meat, and clarified butter.

222.s:
mriyannapi na cādadyād brāhmaṇebhyas tathā karaṃ /
yasya rājñastu viṣaye śrotriyaḥ sīdati kṣudhā //
222.d:
म्रियन्नपि न चादद्याद् ब्राह्मणेभ्यस् तथा करं /
यस्य राज्ञस्तु विषये श्रोत्रियः सीदति क्षुधा //
222.m:
Even when dying, he should not take a tax from brāhmaṇas.
In whosever realm a learned brāhmaṇa wastes away from hunger,

222.s:
tasya sīdati tadrāṣṭraṃ vyādhidurbhikṣataskaraiḥ /
śrutaṃ vṛttantu vijñāya vṛttiṃ tasya prakalpayet //
222.d:
तस्य सीदति तद्राष्ट्रं व्याधिदुर्भिक्षतस्करैः /
श्रुतं वृत्तन्तु विज्ञाय वृत्तिं तस्य प्रकल्पयेत् //
222.m:
that king's kingdom wastes away through disease, famine, and thieves.
Having ascertained his learning and conduct, he should arrange a livelihood for him,

222.s:
rakṣecca sarvatastvenaṃ pitā putramivaurasaṃ /
saṃrakṣyamaṇo rājñā yaḥ kurute dharmamanvahaṃ //
222.d:
रक्षेच्च सर्वतस्त्वेनं पिता पुत्रमिवौरसं /
संरक्ष्यमणो राज्ञा यः कुरुते धर्ममन्वहं //
222.m:
and he should protect him from all sides as a father protects his own begotten son.
When he is protected by the king, whatever religious duty he performs day by day,

222.s:
tenāyurvardhate rājño draviṇaṃ rāṣṭrameva ca /
karma kuryur narendrasya māsenaikañca(1) śilpinaḥ //
222.d:
तेनायुर्वर्धते राज्ञो द्रविणं राष्ट्रमेव च /
कर्म कुर्युर् नरेन्द्रस्य मासेनैकञ्च(1) शिल्पिनः //
222.m:
thereby the king's lifespan, wealth, and realm increase.
Artisans should do one day's work each month for the king,

222.s:
bhuktamātreṇa ye cānye svaśarīropajīyinaḥ //34//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe rājadharmo nāma
dvāviṃśatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha trayoviṃśatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
rājadharmāḥ
222.d:
भुक्तमात्रेण ये चान्ये स्वशरीरोपजीयिनः //34//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे राजधर्मो नाम
द्वाविंशत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ त्रयोविंशत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
राजधर्माः
222.m:
as well as any others who subsist by their own manual labor, in exchange for food alone. //34
Thus ends the two hundred and twenty-second chapter, entitled Duties of Kings, in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the two hundred and twenty-third chapter:
Duties of Kings.

223.s:
puṣkara uvāca
vakṣye 'ntaḥpuracintāṃ ca dharmādyāḥ puruṣārthakāḥ /
anyonyarakṣayā teṣāṃ sevā kāryā striyā nṛpaiḥ //
:n
1 māsenaikeneti cha.. , ja.. ca
:p 312
223.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
वक्ष्ये ऽन्तःपुरचिन्तां च धर्माद्याः पुरुषार्थकाः /
अन्योन्यरक्षया तेषां सेवा कार्या स्त्रिया नृपैः //
:न्
1 मासेनैकेनेति छ.. , ज.. च
:प् 312
223.m:
Puṣkara said:
I shall explain care for the inner apartments. Religious duty and the other ends of human life
are preserved by mutual protection; therefore, women should be served by kings.
[...]
[Variant reading:] 1 "māsenaikena" in MSS cha and ja.

223.s:
dharmamūlo 'rthaviṭapas tathā karmaphalo mahān /
trivargapādapastatra rakṣayā phalabhāgaṃ bhavet //
223.d:
धर्ममूलो ऽर्थविटपस् तथा कर्मफलो महान् /
त्रिवर्गपादपस्तत्र रक्षया फलभागं भवेत् //
223.m:
Having religious duty as its root, wealth as its branch, and action as its great fruit,
the tree of the three ends of life yields its fruit by protection.

223.s:
kāmādhīnāḥ(1) striyo rāma tadarthaṃ ratnasaṅgrahaḥ /
sevyāstā nātisevyāś ca bhūbhujā viṣayaiṣiṇā //
223.d:
कामाधीनाः(1) स्त्रियो राम तदर्थं रत्नसङ्ग्रहः /
सेव्यास्ता नातिसेव्याश् च भूभुजा विषयैषिणा //
223.m:
Women are subject to desire, O Rāma, and for their sake jewels are gathered.
They should be enjoyed by the earth-ruler seeking worldly pleasure, but not enjoyed to excess.

223.s:
āhāro maithunannidrā sevyā nāti hi rug bhavet /
mañcādhikāre(2) kartavyāḥ striyaḥ sevyāḥ svarāmikāḥ(3) //
223.d:
आहारो मैथुनन्निद्रा सेव्या नाति हि रुग् भवेत् /
मञ्चाधिकारे(2) कर्तव्याः स्त्रियः सेव्याः स्वरामिकाः(3) //
223.m:
Food, sexual intercourse, and sleep should not be indulged in excessively, for disease arises.
Women should be kept under the authority of the couch and enjoyed within one's own pleasure-grounds.

223.s:
duṣṭānyācarate(4) yā tu nābinandati tatkathāṃ /
aikyaṃ dviṣadbhirvrajati garvaṃ vahati coddhatā //
223.d:
दुष्टान्याचरते(4) या तु नाबिनन्दति तत्कथां /
ऐक्यं द्विषद्भिर्व्रजति गर्वं वहति चोद्धता //
223.m:
She who behaves wickedly, does not welcome his conversation,
sides with his enemies, and haughtily displays pride,

223.s:
cumbitā mārṣṭi vadanaṃ dattanna bahu manyate /
svapityādau prasuptāpi tathā paścādvibudhyate //
223.d:
चुम्बिता मार्ष्टि वदनं दत्तन्न बहु मन्यते /
स्वपित्यादौ प्रसुप्तापि तथा पश्चाद्विबुध्यते //
223.m:
wipes her face when kissed, does not value what is given,
sleeps first and, even when asleep, wakes up afterward,

223.s:
spṛṣṭā dhunoti gātrāṇi gātrañca viruṇaddhi yā /
īṣacchṛṇoti vākyāni priyāṇyapi parāṅmukhī //
223.d:
स्पृष्टा धुनोति गात्राणि गात्रञ्च विरुणद्धि या /
ईषच्छृणोति वाक्यानि प्रियाण्यपि पराङ्मुखी //
223.m:
shakes her limbs when touched and recoils her body,
barely listens to words, even affectionate ones, turning her face away,

223.s:
na paśyatyagradattantu jaghanañca nigūhati /
dṛṣṭe vivarṇavadanā mitreṣvatha parāṅmukhī(5) //
223.d:
न पश्यत्यग्रदत्तन्तु जघनञ्च निगूहति /
दृष्टे विवर्णवदना मित्रेष्वथ पराङ्मुखी(5) //
223.m:
does not look at what is offered in front of her, hides her hips,
turns pale in the face when seen, and turns away from his friends,

223.s:
tatkāmitāsu ca strīsu madhyastheva ca lakṣyate /
jñātamaṇḍanakālāpi na karoti ca maṇḍanaṃ //
223.d:
तत्कामितासु च स्त्रीसु मध्यस्थेव च लक्ष्यते /
ज्ञातमण्डनकालापि न करोति च मण्डनं //
223.m:
and appears indifferent toward women who desire him,
and does not adorn herself even knowing the time for adornment—

223.s:
yā sā viraktā tāntyaktvā sānurāgāṃ striyambhajet(6) /
dṛṣṭvaiva hṛṣṭā bhavati vīkṣite ca parāṅmukhī //
:n
1 kāmādharā iti gha.. , ña.. ca
2 lajjādhikāre iti kha.. , cha.. ca
3 suvāsikā iti ka..
4 dviṣṭānyācakṣate iti ña..
5 na paśyatyagradattantvityādiḥ, mitreṣvatha parāṅmukhītyantaḥ
pāṭhaḥ ja.. pustake nāsti
6 striyaṃ vrajediti gha.. , ña.. ca
:p 313
223.d:
या सा विरक्ता तान्त्यक्त्वा सानुरागां स्त्रियम्भजेत्(6) /
दृष्ट्वैव हृष्टा भवति वीक्षिते च पराङ्मुखी //
:न्
1 कामाधरा इति घ.. , ञ.. च
2 लज्जाधिकारे इति ख.. , छ.. च
3 सुवासिका इति क..
4 द्विष्टान्याचक्षते इति ञ..
5 न पश्यत्यग्रदत्तन्त्वित्यादिः, मित्रेष्वथ पराङ्मुखीत्यन्तः
पाठः ज.. पुस्तके नास्ति
6 स्त्रियं व्रजेदिति घ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 313
223.m:
she is averse; having abandoned her, he should resort to a woman who is affectionate.
[An affectionate woman] becomes delighted merely upon seeing him, and turns her face away when gazed at;
[...]
[Variant reading:] 1 "kāmādharāḥ" in MSS gha and ña.
[Variant reading:] 2 "lajjādhikāre" in MSS kha and cha.
[Variant reading:] 3 "suvāsikāḥ" in MS ka.
[Variant reading:] 4 "dviṣṭānyācakṣate" in MS ña.
[Variant reading:] 5 The passage from "na paśyatyagradattantv" up to "mitreṣvatha parāṅmukhī" is missing in MS ja.
[Variant reading:] 6 "striyaṃ vrajet" in MSS gha and ña.

223.s:
dṛśyamanā tathānyatra dṛṣṭiṃ kṣipati cañcalāṃ /
tathāpyupāvartayituṃ naiva śaknotyaśeṣataḥ //
223.d:
दृश्यमना तथान्यत्र दृष्टिं क्षिपति चञ्चलां /
तथाप्युपावर्तयितुं नैव शक्नोत्यशेषतः //
223.m:
when being looked at, she casts a restless glance elsewhere,
yet she is not entirely able to turn it away.

223.s:
vivṛṇīti tathāṅgāni svasyā guhyāni bhārgava /
garhitañca tathaivāṅgaṃ prayatnena nigūhati //
223.d:
विवृणीति तथाङ्गानि स्वस्या गुह्यानि भार्गव /
गर्हितञ्च तथैवाङ्गं प्रयत्नेन निगूहति //
223.m:
She exposes her private parts, O descendant of Bhṛgu,
and carefully conceals any flawed limb.

223.s:
taddarśane ca kurute bālāliṅganacumbanaṃ /
ābhāṣyamāṇā bhavati satyavākyā tathaiva ca //
223.d:
तद्दर्शने च कुरुते बालालिङ्गनचुम्बनं /
आभाष्यमाणा भवति सत्यवाक्या तथैव च //
223.m:
When he is seen, she embraces and kisses a child;
and when addressed, she speaks truthful words.

223.s:
spṛṣṭā pulakitair aṅgaiḥ svedenaiva ca bhujyate /
karoti ca tathā rāma sulabhadravyayācanaṃ //
223.d:
स्पृष्टा पुलकितैर् अङ्गैः स्वेदेनैव च भुज्यते /
करोति च तथा राम सुलभद्रव्ययाचनं //
223.m:
When touched, her limbs bristle with thrill and she is covered with perspiration;
and likewise, O Rāma, she asks only for easily obtainable things.

223.s:
tataḥ svalpamapi prāpya karoti paramāṃ mudaṃ /
nāmasaṅkīrtanādeva muditā bahu manyate //
223.d:
ततः स्वल्पमपि प्राप्य करोति परमां मुदं /
नामसङ्कीर्तनादेव मुदिता बहु मन्यते //
223.m:
Then, having obtained even a little, she experiences great joy;
merely by the mention of his name, she rejoices and values it greatly.

223.s:
karajāṅkāṅkitānyasya phalāni preṣayatyapi /
tatpreṣitañca hṛdaye vinyasatyapi cādarāt //
223.d:
करजाङ्काङ्कितान्यस्य फलानि प्रेषयत्यपि /
तत्प्रेषितञ्च हृदये विन्यसत्यपि चादरात् //
223.m:
She sends him fruits marked with her fingernails,
and places what is sent by him upon her heart with reverent affection.

223.s:
āliṅganaiś ca gātrāṇi limpatīvāmṛtena yā /
supte svapityathādau ca tathā tasya vibudhyate //
223.d:
आलिङ्गनैश् च गात्राणि लिम्पतीवामृतेन या /
सुप्ते स्वपित्यथादौ च तथा तस्य विबुध्यते //
223.m:
With her embraces she seems to smear his limbs with nectar;
she sleeps only after he sleeps, and wakes before him.

223.s:
urū spṛśati cātyarthaṃ suptañcainaṃ vibudhyate /
kapitthacūrṇayogena tathā daghnaḥ srajā tathā //
223.d:
उरू स्पृशति चात्यर्थं सुप्तञ्चैनं विबुध्यते /
कपित्थचूर्णयोगेन तथा दघ्नः स्रजा तथा //
223.m:
She strokes his thighs intensely and awakens him when asleep.
With a mixture of powdered wood-apple and a garland of curd,

223.s:
ghṛtaṃ sugandhi bhavati dugdhaiḥ kṣiptais tathā yavaiḥ /
bhojyasya kalpanaivaṃ syādgandhamuktiḥ pradarśyate //
223.d:
घृतं सुगन्धि भवति दुग्धैः क्षिप्तैस् तथा यवैः /
भोज्यस्य कल्पनैवं स्याद्गन्धमुक्तिः प्रदर्श्यते //
223.m:
clarified butter becomes fragrant, as it does with milk cast with barley.
Such should be the preparation of food; now the release of fragrance is demonstrated.

223.s:
śaucamācamanaṃ rāma tathaiva ca virecanaṃ /
bhāvanā caiva pākaś ca bodhanaṃ dhūpanantathā //
223.d:
शौचमाचमनं राम तथैव च विरेचनं /
भावना चैव पाकश् च बोधनं धूपनन्तथा //
223.m:
Purification, rinsing the mouth, O Rāma, and purgation,
infusion, boiling, excitation, and fumigation,

223.s:
vāsanañcaiva nirdiṣṭaṃ karmāṣṭakamidaṃ smṛtaṃ /
kapitthabilvajamvāmrakaravīrakapallavaiḥ //
223.d:
वासनञ्चैव निर्दिष्टं कर्माष्टकमिदं स्मृतं /
कपित्थबिल्वजम्वाम्रकरवीरकपल्लवैः //
223.m:
and perfuming: these are stated to be the eight processes.
With the tender leaves of wood-apple, bael, rose-apple, mango, and oleander,

223.s:
kṛtvodakantu yaddravyaṃ śaucitaṃ śaucanantu tat /
:p 314
teṣāmabhāve śaucantu mṛgadarpāmbhasā bhavet //
223.d:
कृत्वोदकन्तु यद्द्रव्यं शौचितं शौचनन्तु तत् /
:प् 314
तेषामभावे शौचन्तु मृगदर्पाम्भसा भवेत् //
223.m:
having made water, whatever ingredient is cleansed, that is purification.
[Page 314]
In their absence, purification may be performed with musk-water.

223.s:
nakhaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ ghanaṃ māṃsī spṛkkaśaileyajaṃ jalaṃ /
tathaiva kuṅkumaṃ lākṣā candanāgurunīradaṃ(1) //
223.d:
नखं कुष्ठं घनं मांसी स्पृक्कशैलेयजं जलं /
तथैव कुङ्कुमं लाक्षा चन्दनागुरुनीरदं(1) //
223.m:
Unguis odoratus, costus, nut-grass, spikenard, delphinium, lichen,
as well as saffron, lac, sandalwood, agallochum, cyperus,

223.s:
saralaṃ devakāṣṭhañca(2) karpūraṃ kāntayā saha /
bālaḥ kundurukaś caiva gugguluḥ śrīnivāsakaḥ //
223.d:
सरलं देवकाष्ठञ्च(2) कर्पूरं कान्तया सह /
बालः कुन्दुरुकश् चैव गुग्गुलुः श्रीनिवासकः //
223.m:
chir pine, deodar, camphor along with priyaṅgu,
hrivera, olibanum, bdellium, and liquidambar,

223.s:
saha sarjarasenaivaṃ dhūpadravyaikaviṃśatiḥ /
dhūpadravyagaṇādasmādekaviṃśādyathecchayā //
223.d:
सह सर्जरसेनैवं धूपद्रव्यैकविंशतिः /
धूपद्रव्यगणादस्मादेकविंशाद्यथेच्छया //
223.m:
together with resin of shorea: these are the twenty-one incense ingredients.
From this group of twenty-one incense ingredients, according to one's wish,

223.s:
dve dve dravye samādāya sarjabhāgair niyojayet /
nakhapiṇyākamalayaiḥ saṃyojya madhunā tathā //
223.d:
द्वे द्वे द्रव्ये समादाय सर्जभागैर् नियोजयेत् /
नखपिण्याकमलयैः संयोज्य मधुना तथा //
223.m:
taking two substances each, one should combine them with portions of sal-resin,
combining them with unguis odoratus, deodar, and sandalwood, along with honey.

223.s:
dhūpayogā bhavantīha yathāvat svecchayā kṛtāḥ /
tvacannāḍīṃ phalantailaṃ kuṅkumaṃ granthi pravartakaṃ(3) //
223.d:
धूपयोगा भवन्तीह यथावत् स्वेच्छया कृताः /
त्वचन्नाडीं फलन्तैलं कुङ्कुमं ग्रन्थि प्रवर्तकं(3) //
223.m:
The incense compounds properly prepared here at will are produced thus.
Cinnamon bark, costus-root, fruit, sesame oil, saffron, ginger, and cumin,

223.s:
śaileyantagaraṃ krāntāṃ colaṅkarpūrameva ca(4) /
māṃsīṃ surāñca kuṣṭhañca snānadravyāṇi nirdiśet //
223.d:
शैलेयन्तगरं क्रान्तां चोलङ्कर्पूरमेव च(4) /
मांसीं सुराञ्च कुष्ठञ्च स्नानद्रव्याणि निर्दिशेत् //
223.m:
lichen, tagara, kāntā, cardamoms, and camphor,
spikenard, liquor, and costus: these are declared to be the bath ingredients.

223.s:
etebhyastu samādāya dravyatrayamathecchayā /
mṛgadarpayutaṃ snānaṃ kāryaṃ kandarpavardhanaṃ //
223.d:
एतेभ्यस्तु समादाय द्रव्यत्रयमथेच्छया /
मृगदर्पयुतं स्नानं कार्यं कन्दर्पवर्धनं //
223.m:
Taking three substances from these according to one's wish,
a bath mixed with musk should be prepared, which enhances love.

223.s:
tvaṅmurānaladaistulyair vālakārdhasamāyutaiḥ /
snānamutpalagandhi syāt satailaṃ kuṅkumāyate //
223.d:
त्वङ्मुरानलदैस्तुल्यैर् वालकार्धसमायुतैः /
स्नानमुत्पलगन्धि स्यात् सतैलं कुङ्कुमायते //
223.m:
With equal parts of cinnamon bark, murā, and spikenard, combined with half a part of bālaka,
the bath acquires the fragrance of a blue lotus; mixed with oil, it smells like saffron.

223.s:
jātīpuṣasugandhi syāt tagarārdhena yojitaṃ /
saddhyāmakaṃ syādvakulaistulyagandhi manoharaṃ //
:n
1 candanāguruśailajamiti kha.. , cha.. ca
2 devadāruśceti gha.. , ña.. ca
3 granthiparṇakamiti ga.. , gha.. , ña.. ca
4 saha sarjarasenetyādiḥ colaṃ karpūrameva cetyantaḥ pāṭhaḥ ṭa..
pustake nāsti
:p 315
223.d:
जातीपुषसुगन्धि स्यात् तगरार्धेन योजितं /
सद्ध्यामकं स्याद्वकुलैस्तुल्यगन्धि मनोहरं //
:न्
1 चन्दनागुरुशैलजमिति ख.. , छ.. च
2 देवदारुश्चेति घ.. , ञ.. च
3 ग्रन्थिपर्णकमिति ग.. , घ.. , ञ.. च
4 सह सर्जरसेनेत्यादिः चोलं कर्पूरमेव चेत्यन्तः पाठः ट..
पुस्तके नास्ति
:प् 315
223.m:
Combined with half a part of tagara, it has the fragrance of jasmine;
with dhyāmaka, it has the enchanting fragrance equal to that of bakula flowers.
[...]
1. "candanāguruśailajam" in manuscripts kha and cha.
2. "devadāruś ca" in manuscripts gha and ña.
3. "granthiparṇakam" in manuscripts ga, gha, and ña.
4. The passage beginning "saha sarjarasena" up to "colaṃ karpūrameva ca" is missing in manuscript ṭa.

223.s:
mañjiṣṭhātagaraṃ colaṃ tvacaṃ vyaghranakhaṃ nakkhaṃ /
gandhapatrañca vinyasya gandhatailaṃ bhavecchubhaṃ //
223.d:
मञ्जिष्ठातगरं चोलं त्वचं व्यघ्रनखं नक्खं /
गन्धपत्रञ्च विन्यस्य गन्धतैलं भवेच्छुभं //
223.m:
Having added Indian madder, tagara, cardamom, cinnamon, tiger's-claw, nakha,
and gandhapatra, an auspicious perfumed oil is produced.

223.s:
tailaṃ nipīḍitaṃ rāma tilaiḥ puṣpādhivāsitaiḥ /
vāsanāt puṣpasadṛśaṃ gandhena tu bhaved dhruvaṃ //
223.d:
तैलं निपीडितं राम तिलैः पुष्पाधिवासितैः /
वासनात् पुष्पसदृशं गन्धेन तु भवेद् ध्रुवं //
223.m:
The oil pressed, O Rāma, from sesame seeds scented with flowers,
becomes by that perfuming surely equal in scent to those flowers.

223.s:
elālavaṅgakakkolajātīphalaniśākarāḥ /
jātīpatrikayā sārdhaṃ svatantrā mukhavāsakāḥ //
223.d:
एलालवङ्गकक्कोलजातीफलनिशाकराः /
जातीपत्रिकया सार्धं स्वतन्त्रा मुखवासकाः //
223.m:
Cardamom, cloves, cubebs, nutmeg, and camphor,
together with mace, are mouth-perfumers in their own right.

223.s:
karpūraṃ kuṅkumaṃ kāntā mṛgadarpaṃ hareṇukaṃ /
kakkolailālavaṅgañca jātau kośakameva ca //
223.d:
कर्पूरं कुङ्कुमं कान्ता मृगदर्पं हरेणुकं /
कक्कोलैलालवङ्गञ्च जातौ कोशकमेव च //
223.m:
Camphor, saffron, pryaṅgu, musk, hareṇuka,
cubeb, cardamom, and clove, and also the aril of nutmeg,

223.s:
tvakpatraṃ truṭimustau ca latāṃ kastūrikaṃ tathā /
kaṇṭakāni lavaṅgasya phalapatre ca jātitaḥ //
223.d:
त्वक्पत्रं त्रुटिमुस्तौ च लतां कस्तूरिकं तथा /
कण्टकानि लवङ्गस्य फलपत्रे च जातितः //
223.m:
cinnamon bark, cardamom, nut grass, latā, and likewise musk,
clove stems, and nutmeg fruit and mace,

223.s:
kaṭukañca(1) phalaṃ rāma kārṣikāṇyupakalpayet /
taccūrṇe khadiraṃ sāraṃ dadyātturyaṃ tu vāsitaṃ(2) //
223.d:
कटुकञ्च(1) फलं राम कार्षिकाण्युपकल्पयेत् /
तच्चूर्णे खदिरं सारं दद्यात्तुर्यं तु वासितं(2) //
223.m:
and kaṭukaphala, O Rāma—one should take one karṣa of each.
To this powder one should add one-fourth scented khadira extract.

223.s:
sahakārarasenāsmāt kartavyā guṭikāḥ śubhāḥ(3) /
mukha nyastāḥ sugandhāstā mukharogavināśanāḥ //
223.d:
सहकाररसेनास्मात् कर्तव्या गुटिकाः शुभाः(3) /
मुख न्यस्ताः सुगन्धास्ता मुखरोगविनाशनाः //
223.m:
From this, with the juice of mango, auspicious pills should be made.
Placed in the mouth, they are fragrant and destroy diseases of the mouth.

223.s:
pūgaṃ prakṣālitaṃ samyak pañcapallavavāriṇā /
śaktyā tu guṭikādravyair vāsitaṃ mukhavāsakaṃ //
223.d:
पूगं प्रक्षालितं सम्यक् पञ्चपल्लववारिणा /
शक्त्या तु गुटिकाद्रव्यैर् वासितं मुखवासकं //
223.m:
Areca nut thoroughly washed with the water of the five tender sprouts,
and scented according to capacity with the pill ingredients, is a mouth-perfumer.

223.s:
kaṭukaṃ dantakāṣṭhañca gomūtre vāsitaṃ tryahaṃ /
kṛtañca pūgavadrāma mukhasaugandhikārakaṃ //
223.d:
कटुकं दन्तकाष्ठञ्च गोमूत्रे वासितं त्र्यहं /
कृतञ्च पूगवद्राम मुखसौगन्धिकारकं //
223.m:
And a kaṭuka tooth-stick soaked in cow's urine for three days,
and prepared like the areca nut, O Rāma, produces fragrance in the mouth.

223.s:
tvakpathyayoḥ samāvaṃśau śaśibhāgārdhasaṃyutau /
nāgavallīsamo bhāti mukhavāso manoharaḥ //
:n
1 kandukañceti kha.. , cha.. ca
2 dadyātturthaṃ tulonmitamiti ṭa.. , cha.. ca
3 kakkolailetyādiḥ guṭikāḥ śubhā ity antaḥ pāṭhaḥ gha.. , ja..
pustakadvaye nāsti
:p 316
223.d:
त्वक्पथ्ययोः समावंशौ शशिभागार्धसंयुतौ /
नागवल्लीसमो भाति मुखवासो मनोहरः //
:न्
1 कन्दुकञ्चेति ख.. , छ.. च
2 दद्यात्तुर्थं तुलोन्मितमिति ट.. , छ.. च
3 कक्कोलैलेत्यादिः गुटिकाः शुभा इत्य् अन्तः पाठः घ.. , ज..
पुस्तकद्वये नास्ति
:प् 316
223.m:
Equal parts of cinnamon bark and harītakī, combined with half a part of camphor,
shines as a charming mouth-perfumer equal to betel leaves.
[...]
1. "kandukañca" in manuscripts kha and cha.
2. "dadyātturthaṃ tulonmitam" in manuscripts ṭa and cha.
3. The passage beginning "kakkolailā" up to "guṭikāḥ śubhāḥ" is missing in the two manuscripts gha and ja.

223.s:
evaṃ kuryāt sadā strīṇāṃ rakṣaṇaṃ pṛthivīpatiḥ /
na cāsāṃ viśvasejjātu putramāturviśeṣataḥ //
223.d:
एवं कुर्यात् सदा स्त्रीणां रक्षणं पृथिवीपतिः /
न चासां विश्वसेज्जातु पुत्रमातुर्विशेषतः //
223.m:
In this way the ruler of the earth should always protect the women,
and he should never trust them, especially the mother of his son.

223.s:
na svapet strīgṛhe rātrau viśvāsaḥ kṛtrimo bhavet //
:e ity āgneye mahāopurāṇe strīrakṣādikāmaśāstraṃ nāma
trayoviṃśatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha caturviṃśatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
rājadharmāḥ
223.d:
न स्वपेत् स्त्रीगृहे रात्रौ विश्वासः कृत्रिमो भवेत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महाओपुराणे स्त्रीरक्षादिकामशास्त्रं नाम
त्रयोविंशत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ चतुर्विंशत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
राजधर्माः
223.m:
He should not sleep at night in the women's quarters; trust may be feigned.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the two hundred and twenty-third chapter, entitled "The Treatise on Love: The Protection of Women and Related Matters."
Now begins the two hundred and twenty-fourth chapter.
The Duties of Kings.

224.s:
puṣkara uvāca
rājaputrasya rakṣā ca kartavyā pṛthivīkṣitā /
dharmārthakāmaśāstrāṇi dhanurvedañca śikṣayet //
224.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
राजपुत्रस्य रक्षा च कर्तव्या पृथिवीक्षिता /
धर्मार्थकामशास्त्राणि धनुर्वेदञ्च शिक्षयेत् //

224.s:
śilpāni śikṣayeccaivamāptair mithyāpriyaṃvadaiḥ /
śarīrarakṣāvyājena rakṣiṇo 'sya niyojayet //
224.d:
शिल्पानि शिक्षयेच्चैवमाप्तैर् मिथ्याप्रियंवदैः /
शरीररक्षाव्याजेन रक्षिणो ऽस्य नियोजयेत् //
224.m:
He should also instruct him in the arts through trusted persons who speak pleasant truths.
Under the pretext of protecting his body, he should assign guards to him.

224.s:
na cāsya saṅgo dātavyaḥ kruddhalubdhavimānitaiḥ /
aśakyantu guṇādhānaṃ kartuṃ taṃ bandhayet mukhaiḥ //
224.d:
न चास्य सङ्गो दातव्यः क्रुद्धलुब्धविमानितैः /
अशक्यन्तु गुणाधानं कर्तुं तं बन्धयेत् मुखैः //
224.m:
He should not allow him association with those who are angry, greedy, or insulted.
If it is impossible to instill virtues in him, he should bind him through trusted agents.

224.s:
adhikāreṣu sarveṣu vinītaṃ viniyojayet /
mṛgayāṃ pānamakṣāṃś ca rājyanāśaṃstyajennṛpaḥ //
224.d:
अधिकारेषु सर्वेषु विनीतं विनियोजयेत् /
मृगयां पानमक्षांश् च राज्यनाशंस्त्यजेन्नृपः //
224.m:
He should appoint the disciplined [prince] to all offices.
The king should abandon hunting, drinking, gambling, and ruin of the realm.

224.s:
divāsvapnaṃ vṛthāṭyāñca vākpāruṣyaṃ vivarjayet /
nindāñca daṇḍapāruṣyamarthadūṣaṇamutsṛjet //
224.d:
दिवास्वप्नं वृथाट्याञ्च वाक्पारुष्यं विवर्जयेत् /
निन्दाञ्च दण्डपारुष्यमर्थदूषणमुत्सृजेत् //
224.m:
He should avoid sleeping by day, roaming about in vain, and harshness of speech;
he should cast off censure, harshness of punishment, and misuse of wealth.

224.s:
ākārāṇāṃ samuchedo durgādīnāmasatkriyā /
:p 317
arthānāṃ dūṣaṇaṃ proktaṃ viprakīrṇatvameva ca //
224.d:
आकाराणां समुछेदो दुर्गादीनामसत्क्रिया /
:प् 317
अर्थानां दूषणं प्रोक्तं विप्रकीर्णत्वमेव च //
224.m:
Cutting off sources of revenue, neglect of fortresses and the like,
[Page 317]
and also scattering them—these are declared to be the misuse of wealth.

224.s:
adeśakāle yaddānamapātre dānameva ca /
artheṣu dūṣaṇaṃ proktamasatkarmapravartanaṃ //
224.d:
अदेशकाले यद्दानमपात्रे दानमेव च /
अर्थेषु दूषणं प्रोक्तमसत्कर्मप्रवर्तनं //
224.m:
Gift given out of place and time, and gift given to an unworthy recipient,
and engagement in improper actions are declared to be ruin with regard to wealth.
