224.s:
kāmaṃ krodhaṃ madaṃ mānaṃ lobhaṃ darpañca varjayet /
tato bhṛtyajayaṅkṛtvā paurajānapadaṃ jayet //
224.d:
कामं क्रोधं मदं मानं लोभं दर्पञ्च वर्जयेत् /
ततो भृत्यजयङ्कृत्वा पौरजानपदं जयेत् //
224.m:
He should avoid desire, anger, intoxication, pride, greed, and arrogance.
Then, having won over his servants, he should win over the citizens and countryside folk.

224.s:
jayedvāhyānarīn paścādvāhyāś ca trividhārayaḥ /
guravaste yathā pūrvaṃ kulyānantarakṛtrimāḥ //
224.d:
जयेद्वाह्यानरीन् पश्चाद्वाह्याश् च त्रिविधारयः /
गुरवस्ते यथा पूर्वं कुल्यानन्तरकृत्रिमाः //
224.m: Afterwards he should conquer external enemies; and external enemies are threefold: / of increasing weight, just as previously stated, [namely] born of the same family, contiguous, and artificial.

224.s:
pitṛpaitāmahaṃ mitraṃ sāmantañca tathā ripoḥ /
kṛtrimañca mahābhāga mitrantrividhamucyate //
224.d:
पितृपैतामहं मित्रं सामन्तञ्च तथा रिपोः /
कृत्रिमञ्च महाभाग मित्रन्त्रिविधमुच्यते //
224.m: Inherited from father and grandfather, the neighboring ruler of an enemy, / and artificial, O noble one—an ally is said to be threefold.

224.s:
svāmyamātyañjanapadā durgaṃ daṇdastathaiva ca /
koṣo mitrañca dharmajña saptāṅgaṃ rājyamucyate //
224.d:
स्वाम्यमात्यञ्जनपदा दुर्गं दण्दस्तथैव च /
कोषो मित्रञ्च धर्मज्ञ सप्ताङ्गं राज्यमुच्यते //
224.m: The sovereign, minister, territory, fortress, and likewise the army, / treasury, and ally, O knower of righteousness—the realm is said to have seven limbs.

224.s:
mūlaṃ svāmī sa vai rakṣyastasmādrājyaṃ(1) viśeṣataḥ /
rājyāṅgadrohiṇaṃ hanyātkāle tīkṣṇo mṛdurbhavet //
224.d:
मूलं स्वामी स वै रक्ष्यस्तस्माद्राज्यं(1) विशेषतः /
राज्याङ्गद्रोहिणं हन्यात्काले तीक्ष्णो मृदुर्भवेत् //
224.m: The sovereign is the root; he must indeed be protected, and especially the realm from that [basis]. / He should slay one who betrays the limbs of the realm; at the proper time he should be severe, [and at others] gentle.

224.s:
evaṃ lokadvayaṃ rājño bhṛtyair hāsaṃ vivarjayet /
bhṛtyāḥ paribhavantīha nṛpaṃ harṣaṇasatkathaṃ //
224.d:
एवं लोकद्वयं राज्ञो भृत्यैर् हासं विवर्जयेत् /
भृत्याः परिभवन्तीह नृपं हर्षणसत्कथं //
224.m: Thus [he gains] both worlds; the king should avoid jesting with his servants. / Servants show contempt in this world for a king who indulges in pleasant conversation.

224.s:
lokasaṅgrahaṇārthāya kṛtakavyasano bhavet /
smitapūrvābhibhāṣī syāt lokānāṃ rañjanaṃ caret //
224.d:
लोकसङ्ग्रहणार्थाय कृतकव्यसनो भवेत् /
स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषी स्यात् लोकानां रञ्जनं चरेत् //
224.m: For the purpose of winning over the people, he should feign vices. / He should be one who speaks with a smile, and should conduct the pleasing of the people.

224.s:
dīrghasūtrasya nṛpateḥ karmahānirdhruvaṃ bhavet /
rāge darpe ca māne ca drohe pāpe ca karmaṇi //
224.d:
दीर्घसूत्रस्य नृपतेः कर्महानिर्ध्रुवं भवेत् /
रागे दर्पे च माने च द्रोहे पापे च कर्मणि //
224.m: For a procrastinating king, loss of business is certain. / In passion, in pride, in arrogance, in betrayal, in sinful action,

224.s:
apriye caiva vaktavye dīrghasūtraḥ praśasyate /
suptamantro bhavedrājā nāpado guptamantrataḥ //
:n
1 tasmādrāṣṭramiti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , cha.. , ja.. , ña.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 318
224.d:
अप्रिये चैव वक्तव्ये दीर्घसूत्रः प्रशस्यते /
सुप्तमन्त्रो भवेद्राजा नापदो गुप्तमन्त्रतः //
:न्
1 तस्माद्राष्ट्रमिति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , छ.. , ज.. , ञ.. , ट.. च
:प् 318
224.m:
and when unpleasant words must be spoken, procrastination is praised. / The king should be one whose counsel is kept hidden; no misfortune arises from secret counsel.
[Footnote mark]
1. *tasmādrāṣṭram* in manuscripts kha, ga, gha, cha, ja, ña, and ṭa. / [Page 318]

224.s:
jñāyate hi kṛtaṃ karma nārabdhaṃ tasya rājyakaṃ(1) /
ākārair iṅgitair gatyā ceṣṭayā bhāṣitena ca //
224.d:
ज्ञायते हि कृतं कर्म नारब्धं तस्य राज्यकं(1) /
आकारैर् इङ्गितैर् गत्या चेष्टया भाषितेन च //
224.m: For his undertaking is known once accomplished, not when merely begun, [in his] kingdom; / by gestures, hints, gait, movement, speech,

224.s:
netravaktavikārābhyāṃ gṛhyate 'ntargataṃ punaḥ /
naikastu mantrayen mantraṃ na rājā bahubhiḥ saha //
224.d:
नेत्रवक्तविकाराभ्यां गृह्यते ऽन्तर्गतं पुनः /
नैकस्तु मन्त्रयेन् मन्त्रं न राजा बहुभिः सह //
224.m: and by changes in eyes and face, the internal thought is seized. / The king should not deliberate alone, nor should he deliberate with many.

224.s:
bahubhirmantrayet kāmaṃ rājā mantrān pṛthak pṛthak /
mantriṇāmapi no kuryān mantrī mantraprakāśanaṃ //
224.d:
बहुभिर्मन्त्रयेत् कामं राजा मन्त्रान् पृथक् पृथक् /
मन्त्रिणामपि नो कुर्यान् मन्त्री मन्त्रप्रकाशनं //
224.m: The king may deliberate at will with many, one by one; / even to a minister, a minister should not disclose counsel.

224.s:
kvāpi kasyāpi(2) viśvāso bhavatīha sadā nṛṇāṃ /
niś cayaś ca tathā mantre kārya ekena sūriṇā //
224.d:
क्वापि कस्यापि(2) विश्वासो भवतीह सदा नृणां /
निश् चयश् च तथा मन्त्रे कार्य एकेन सूरिणा //
224.m: Nowhere is there always trust in anyone among men in this world; / and likewise, decision regarding counsel should be made with a single wise man.

224.s:
naśyedavinayādrājā rājyañca vinayāllabhet /
traividyebhyastrayīṃ vidyāṃ daṇḍanītiñca śāśvatīṃ //
224.d:
नश्येदविनयाद्राजा राज्यञ्च विनयाल्लभेत् /
त्रैविद्येभ्यस्त्रयीं विद्यां दण्डनीतिञ्च शाश्वतीं //
224.m: Through lack of discipline a king perishes, and through discipline he obtains kingship: / from the masters of the three Vedas, the three Vedas; and the eternal science of government,

224.s:
ānvīkṣikīñcārthavidyāṃ vārtārambhāṃś ca lokataḥ /
jitendriyo hi śaknoti vaśe sthāpayituṃ prajāḥ //
224.d:
आन्वीक्षिकीञ्चार्थविद्यां वार्तारम्भांश् च लोकतः /
जितेन्द्रियो हि शक्नोति वशे स्थापयितुं प्रजाः //
224.m: and logic, the science of wealth, and practical pursuits from the world. / For one with subdued senses is able to keep subjects under control.

224.s:
pūjyā devā dvijāḥ sarve dadyāddānāni teṣu ca /
dvije dānañcākṣayo 'yaṃ nidhiḥ kaiścinna nāśyate //
224.d:
पूज्या देवा द्विजाः सर्वे दद्याद्दानानि तेषु च /
द्विजे दानञ्चाक्षयो ऽयं निधिः कैश्चिन्न नाश्यते //
224.m: All gods and twice-born are to be worshipped, and he should bestow gifts upon them; / and a gift to a twice-born is an inexhaustible treasure that is destroyed by no one.

224.s:
saṅgrāmeṣvanivartitvaṃ prajānāṃ paripālanaṃ /
dānāni brāhmaṇānāñca rājño niḥśreyasamparaṃ //
224.d:
सङ्ग्रामेष्वनिवर्तित्वं प्रजानां परिपालनं /
दानानि ब्राह्मणानाञ्च राज्ञो निःश्रेयसम्परं //
224.m: Not turning back in battles, protection of the subjects, / and gifts to Brahmins are the supreme good for a king.

224.s:
kṛpaṇānāthavṛddhānāṃ vidhavānāñca yoṣitāṃ /
yogakṣemañca vṛttiñca tathaiva parikalpayet //
224.d:
कृपणानाथवृद्धानां विधवानाञ्च योषितां /
योगक्षेमञ्च वृत्तिञ्च तथैव परिकल्पयेत् //
224.m: For the wretched, the helpless, the aged, and widowed women, / he should likewise provide security, acquisition, and livelihood.

224.s:
varṇāśramavyavasthānaṃ kāryantāpasapūjanaṃ /
na viśvasecca sarvatra tāpaseṣu ca viśvaset //
224.d:
वर्णाश्रमव्यवस्थानं कार्यन्तापसपूजनं /
न विश्वसेच्च सर्वत्र तापसेषु च विश्वसेत् //
224.m: The maintenance of the castes and stages of life must be done, and the worship of ascetics. / He should not trust everywhere, but he should trust in ascetics.

224.s:
viśvāsayeccāpi parantattvabhūtena hetunā /
:n
1 tasya karmakamiti kha..
2 kvacit kasyāpi iti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ja.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 319
vakaviccintayedarthaṃ siṃhavacca parākramet //
224.d:
विश्वासयेच्चापि परन्तत्त्वभूतेन हेतुना /
:न्
1 तस्य कर्मकमिति ख..
2 क्वचित् कस्यापि इति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ज.. , ट.. च
:प् 319
वकविच्चिन्तयेदर्थं सिंहवच्च पराक्रमेत् //
224.m:
And he should make the other trust him through a genuine reason.
[Footnote mark]
1. *tasya karmakam* in manuscript kha.
2. *kvacit kasyāpi* in manuscripts kha, ga, gha, ja, and ṭa. / [Page 319]
He should deliberate on matters like a crane, and display prowess like a lion.

224.s:
vṛkavaccāvalumpeta śaśavacca viniṣpatet /
dṛḍhapraharī ca bhavet tathā śūkaravannṛpaḥ //
224.d:
वृकवच्चावलुम्पेत शशवच्च विनिष्पतेत् /
दृढप्रहरी च भवेत् तथा शूकरवन्नृपः //
224.m: He should seize prey like a wolf, and dash forth like a hare; / the king should also strike firmly like a boar.

224.s:
citrakāraś ca śikhivad dṛḍhabhaktis tathāśvavat /
bhavecca madhurābhāṣī tathā kokilavannṛpaḥ //
224.d:
चित्रकारश् च शिखिवद् दृढभक्तिस् तथाश्ववत् /
भवेच्च मधुराभाषी तथा कोकिलवन्नृपः //
224.m: He should be colorful like a peacock, and possess firm devotion like a horse; / and the king should speak sweetly like a cuckoo.

224.s:
kākaśaṅkī bhavennityamajñātāṃ vasatiṃ vaset /
nāparīkṣitapūrvañca bhojanaṃ śayanaṃ spṛśet //
224.d:
काकशङ्की भवेन्नित्यमज्ञातां वसतिं वसेत् /
नापरीक्षितपूर्वञ्च भोजनं शयनं स्पृशेत् //
224.m: He should always be suspicious like a crow, and dwell in an unknown lodging; / he should not touch food or a bed not examined beforehand.

224.s:
nāvijñātāṃ striyaṃ gacchennājñātāṃ nāvamārudvet /
rāṣṭrakarṣī bhrasyate ca rājyārthāccaiva jīvitāt //
224.d:
नाविज्ञातां स्त्रियं गच्छेन्नाज्ञातां नावमारुद्वेत् /
राष्ट्रकर्षी भ्रस्यते च राज्यार्थाच्चैव जीवितात् //
224.m: He should not approach an unknown woman, nor should he board an unknown boat. / One who oppresses the realm falls away from kingship, wealth, and life itself.

224.s:
bhṛto vatso jātabalaḥ karmayogyo yathā bhavet /
tathā rāṣṭraṃ mahābhāga bhṛtaṃ karmasahaṃ bhavet //
224.d:
भृतो वत्सो जातबलः कर्मयोग्यो यथा भवेत् /
तथा राष्ट्रं महाभाग भृतं कर्मसहं भवेत् //
224.m: Just as a nourished calf, when strength is gained, becomes fit for work, / so, O noble one, a nourished realm becomes capable of work.

224.s:
sarvaṃ karmedamāyattaṃ vidhāne daivapauruṣe /
tayordaivamacintyaṃ hi pauruṣe vidyate kriyā //
224.d:
सर्वं कर्मेदमायत्तं विधाने दैवपौरुषे /
तयोर्दैवमचिन्त्यं हि पौरुषे विद्यते क्रिया //
224.m: All this action is dependent upon fate and human effort in its arrangement; / of the two, fate is indeed unfathomable, while in human effort action exists.

224.s:
janānurāgaprabhavā rājño rājyamahīśriyaḥ //34//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe rājadharmo nāma
caturviṃśatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha pañcaviṃśatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
rājadharmāḥ
224.d:
जनानुरागप्रभवा राज्ञो राज्यमहीश्रियः //34//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे राजधर्मो नाम
चतुर्विंशत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ पञ्चविंशत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
राजधर्माः
224.m:
The king's sovereignty and fortune of the earth arise from the affection of the people. //34
Thus in the great Agni Purāṇa, the two hundred and twenty-fourth chapter, entitled "The Duties of Kings."
Now the two hundred and twenty-fifth chapter:
The Duties of Kings.

225.s:
puṣkara uvāca
svayameva karma daivākhyaṃ viddhi dehāntarārjitaṃ /
tasmāt pauruṣameveha śreṣṭhamāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ //
:p 320
225.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
स्वयमेव कर्म दैवाख्यं विद्धि देहान्तरार्जितं /
तस्मात् पौरुषमेवेह श्रेष्ठमाहुर्मनीषिणः //
:प् 320
225.m:
Puṣkara said: / Know that fate itself is action acquired in another body; / therefore, the wise declare human effort alone to be superior in this world.
[Page 320]

225.s:
pratikūlaṃ tathā daivaṃ pauruṣeṇa vihanyate /
sāttvikāt karmaṇaḥ pūrvāt siddhiḥ syātpauruṣaṃ vinā //
225.d:
प्रतिकूलं तथा दैवं पौरुषेण विहन्यते /
सात्त्विकात् कर्मणः पूर्वात् सिद्धिः स्यात्पौरुषं विना //
225.m: Even adverse fate is struck down by human effort; / through past action rooted in *sattva*, success may occur without [present] human effort.

225.s:
pauruṣaṃ daivasampattyā kāle phalati bhārgava /
daivaṃ puruṣakāraś ca dvayaṃ puṃsaḥ phalāvahaṃ //
225.d:
पौरुषं दैवसम्पत्त्या काले फलति भार्गव /
दैवं पुरुषकारश् च द्वयं पुंसः फलावहं //
225.m: Human effort, through the favor of fate, bears fruit in time, O descendant of Bhṛgu; / fate and human effort are the two that yield results for a man.

225.s:
kṛṣervṛṣṭisamāyogāt kāle syuḥ phalasiddhayaḥ /
sadharmaṃ pauruṣaṃ kuryānnālaso na ca daivavān //
225.d:
कृषेर्वृष्टिसमायोगात् काले स्युः फलसिद्धयः /
सधर्मं पौरुषं कुर्यान्नालसो न च दैववान् //
225.m: From agriculture combined with rain, accomplishments of fruit occur in due time. / One should undertake righteous human effort, neither indolent nor relying merely on fate.

225.s:
sāmādibhirupāyaistu sarve siddhyantyupakramāḥ /
sāma copapradānañca bhedadaṇḍau tathāparau //
225.d:
सामादिभिरुपायैस्तु सर्वे सिद्ध्यन्त्युपक्रमाः /
साम चोपप्रदानञ्च भेददण्डौ तथापरौ //
225.m: By the expedients beginning with conciliation, all undertakings succeed: / conciliation and gift-giving, and dissension and punishment as the other two,

225.s:
māyopekṣendrajālañca upāyāḥ sapta tāñchṛṇu /
dvividhaṃ kathitaṃ sāma tathyañcātathyameva ca //
225.d:
मायोपेक्षेन्द्रजालञ्च उपायाः सप्त ताञ्छृणु /
द्विविधं कथितं साम तथ्यञ्चातथ्यमेव च //
225.m: and illusion, indifference, and conjuring—hear those seven expedients: / conciliation is declared to be twofold, true and untrue.

225.s:
tatrāpyatathyaṃ sādhūnāmākrośāyaiva jāyate /
mahākulīnā hy ṛjavo dharmanityā jitendriyāḥ //
225.d:
तत्राप्यतथ्यं साधूनामाक्रोशायैव जायते /
महाकुलीना ह्य् ऋजवो धर्मनित्या जितेन्द्रियाः //
225.m: Even there, the untrue [conciliation] only leads to reproach from the virtuous; / for those of noble birth, upright, constant in virtue, with restrained senses,

225.s:
sāmasādhyā atathyaiś ca gṛhyante rākṣasā api /
tathā taduprakārāṇāṃ kṛtānāñcaiva varṇanaṃ //
225.d:
सामसाध्या अतथ्यैश् च गृह्यन्ते राक्षसा अपि /
तथा तदुप्रकाराणां कृतानाञ्चैव वर्णनं //
225.m: are to be won by conciliation; even demoniac beings are captured through false [promises]. / Likewise, the description of benefits that have been rendered [is useful].

225.s:
parasparantu ye dviṣṭāḥ kruddhabhītāvamānitāḥ /
teṣānbhedaṃ prayuñjīta paramaṃ darśayedbhayaṃ(1) //
225.d:
परस्परन्तु ये द्विष्टाः क्रुद्धभीतावमानिताः /
तेषान्भेदं प्रयुञ्जीत परमं दर्शयेद्भयं(1) //
225.m: Towards those who are mutually hostile, angered, frightened, or insulted, / he should employ dissension; he should show great danger.

225.s:
ātmīyān darśayedāśāṃ yena doṣeṇa bibhyati /
parāstenaiva te bhedyā rakṣyo vai jñātibhedakaḥ //
225.d:
आत्मीयान् दर्शयेदाशां येन दोषेण बिभ्यति /
परास्तेनैव ते भेद्या रक्ष्यो वै ज्ञातिभेदकः //
225.m: He should show hope to his own people; through whatever fault enemies fear, / they are to be divided by that very fault; one who causes dissension among kinsmen should indeed be guarded.

225.s:
sāmantakoṣo vāhyastu mantrāmātyātmajādikaḥ(2) /
antaḥkoṣañcopaśāmya kurvan śatroś ca taṃ jayet //
225.d:
सामन्तकोषो वाह्यस्तु मन्त्रामात्यात्मजादिकः(2) /
अन्तःकोषञ्चोपशाम्य कुर्वन् शत्रोश् च तं जयेत् //
225.m: The outer circle consists of neighboring rulers; the inner consists of counsellors, ministers, sons, and the like; / having subdued the inner circle and making [dissension] in the enemy's, he should conquer him.

225.s:
upāyaśreṣṭhaṃ dānaṃ syāddānādubhayalokabhāk /
na so 'sti nāma dānena vaśago yo na jāyate //
:n
1 parasmādarśayedbhayamiti ña..
2 mantrāmātyānujādika iti ña..
:p 321
225.d:
उपायश्रेष्ठं दानं स्याद्दानादुभयलोकभाक् /
न सो ऽस्ति नाम दानेन वशगो यो न जायते //
:न्
1 परस्मादर्शयेद्भयमिति ञ..
2 मन्त्रामात्यानुजादिक इति ञ..
:प् 321
225.m:
The gift is the best of expedients; through a gift one partakes of both worlds. / There is surely no one who does not come under control through a gift.
[Footnote mark]
1. *parasmādarśayedbhayam* in manuscript ña.
2. *mantrāmātyānujādikaḥ* in manuscript ña. / [Page 321]

225.s:
dānavāneva śaknoti saṃhatān bhedituṃ parān /
trayāsādhyaṃ sādhayettaṃ daṇḍena ca kṛtena ca //
225.d:
दानवानेव शक्नोति संहतान् भेदितुं परान् /
त्रयासाध्यं साधयेत्तं दण्डेन च कृतेन च //
225.m: Only a generous man is able to divide united enemies; / what cannot be accomplished by the three, he should accomplish through punishment when applied.

225.s:
daṇḍe sarvaṃ sthitaṃ daṇḍo nāśayedduṣpraṇīkṛtaḥ /
adaṇḍyān daṇḍayannaśyeddaṇḍyānrājāpyadaṇḍayan //
225.d:
दण्डे सर्वं स्थितं दण्डो नाशयेद्दुष्प्रणीकृतः /
अदण्ड्यान् दण्डयन्नश्येद्दण्ड्यान्राजाप्यदण्डयन् //
225.m: Everything is established in punishment; punishment improperly administered causes ruin. / Punishing those who should not be punished, or a king not punishing those who should be punished, brings ruin.

225.s:
daivadaityoraganarāḥ siddhā bhūtāḥ patatriṇaḥ /
utkrameyuḥ svamaryādāṃ yadi daṇḍān na pālayet //
225.d:
दैवदैत्योरगनराः सिद्धा भूताः पतत्रिणः /
उत्क्रमेयुः स्वमर्यादां यदि दण्डान् न पालयेत् //
225.m: Gods, demons, serpents, men, perfected beings, spirits, and birds / would transgress their own boundaries if he did not protect with punishment.

225.s:
yasmādadāntān damayatyadaṇḍyāndaṇḍayatyapi /
damanāddaṇḍanāccaiva tasmāddaṇḍa vidurbudhāḥ //
225.d:
यस्माददान्तान् दमयत्यदण्ड्यान्दण्डयत्यपि /
दमनाद्दण्डनाच्चैव तस्माद्दण्ड विदुर्बुधाः //
225.m: Because it tames the untamed, and punishes those deserving of punishment, / therefore, from taming and punishing, the wise know it as punishment.

225.s:
tejasā dur nirīkṣyo hi rājā bhāskaravattataḥ /
lokaprasādaṃ gaccheta darśanāccandravattataḥ //
225.d:
तेजसा दुर् निरीक्ष्यो हि राजा भास्करवत्ततः /
लोकप्रसादं गच्छेत दर्शनाच्चन्द्रवत्ततः //
225.m: By his splendor the king is difficult to behold, like the sun; / then he should attain the favor of the people by his appearance, like the moon.

225.s:
jagadvyāpnoti vai cārair ato rājā samīraṇaḥ /
doṣanigrahakāritvādrājā vaivasvataḥ prabhuḥ //
225.d:
जगद्व्याप्नोति वै चारैर् अतो राजा समीरणः /
दोषनिग्रहकारित्वाद्राजा वैवस्वतः प्रभुः //
225.m:
The king pervades the world through his spies; therefore the king is the Wind.
Because he suppresses faults, the sovereign king is Vaivasvata (Yama).

225.s:
yadā dahati durbuddhiṃ tadā bhavati pāvakaḥ /
yadā dānaṃ dvijātibhyo dadyāt tasmāddhaneśvaraḥ //
225.d:
यदा दहति दुर्बुद्धिं तदा भवति पावकः /
यदा दानं द्विजातिभ्यो दद्यात् तस्माद्धनेश्वरः //
225.m:
When he burns the evil-minded, he is then Fire.
When he gives gifts to the twice-born, he is on that account the Lord of Wealth (Kubera).

225.s:
dhanadhārāpravarṣitvāddevādau varuṇaḥ smṛtaḥ /
kṣamayā dhārayaṃllekān pārthivaḥ pārthivo bhavet //
225.d:
धनधाराप्रवर्षित्वाद्देवादौ वरुणः स्मृतः /
क्षमया धारयंल्लेकान् पार्थिवः पार्थिवो भवेत् //
225.m:
Because he showers down streams of wealth, he is regarded as Varuṇa among the gods and others.
Supporting the worlds with forbearance, the earthly king becomes the Earth.

225.s:
utsāhamantraśaktyādyai rakṣedyasmāddharistataḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe sāmādyupāyo nāma
pañcaviṃśatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:p 322
:ś atha ṣaḍviṃśatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
rājadharmāḥ
225.d:
उत्साहमन्त्रशक्त्याद्यै रक्षेद्यस्माद्धरिस्ततः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे सामाद्युपायो नाम
पञ्चविंशत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:प् 322
:श् अथ षड्विंशत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
राजधर्माः
225.m:
Because he protects through energy, counsel, power, and the like, he is therefore Hari.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the two hundred and twenty-fifth chapter, entitled "The Expedients Beginning with Conciliation."
[Page 322]
Now begins the two hundred and twenty-sixth chapter.
The Duties of Kings.

226.s:
puṣkara uvāca
daṇḍapraṇayanaṃ vakṣye yena rājñaḥ parā gatiḥ /
triyavaṃ kṛṣṇalaṃ viddhi pāpastatpañcakaṃ bhavet //
226.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
दण्डप्रणयनं वक्ष्ये येन राज्ञः परा गतिः /
त्रियवं कृष्णलं विद्धि पापस्तत्पञ्चकं भवेत् //
226.m:
Puṣkara said:
I shall describe the administration of punishment, by which the highest state belongs to the king.
Know three barley-grains to be a kṛṣṇala; five of those are a māṣa.

226.s:
kṛṣṇalānāṃ tathā ṣaṣṭyā(1) karṣārdhaṃ rāmakīrtitaṃ /
suvarṇaś ca vinirdiṣṭo rāma ṣoḍaśamāpakaḥ //
226.d:
कृष्णलानां तथा षष्ट्या(1) कर्षार्धं रामकीर्तितं /
सुवर्णश् च विनिर्दिष्टो राम षोडशमापकः //
226.m:
Likewise, half a karṣa is declared, O Rāma, to be made of sixty kṛṣṇalas.
And a suvarṇa, O Rāma, is designated as sixteen māṣas.

226.s:
niṣkaḥ suvarṇāś catvāro dharaṇaṃ daśabhistu taiḥ /
tāmrarūpyasuvarṇānāṃ manametat prakīrtitaṃ //
226.d:
निष्कः सुवर्णाश् चत्वारो धरणं दशभिस्तु तैः /
ताम्ररूप्यसुवर्णानां मनमेतत् प्रकीर्तितं //
226.m:
Four suvarṇas are a niṣka, and ten of those are a dharaṇa.
This is declared to be the measure of copper, silver, and gold.

226.s:
tāmrakaiḥ kārṣiko rāma proktaḥ kārṣāpaṇo budhaiḥ /
paṇānāṃ dve śate sārdhaṃ prathamaḥ sāhasaḥ smṛtaḥ(2) //
226.d:
ताम्रकैः कार्षिको राम प्रोक्तः कार्षापणो बुधैः /
पणानां द्वे शते सार्धं प्रथमः साहसः स्मृतः(2) //
226.m:
A copper coin weighing a karṣa, O Rāma, is called a kārṣāpaṇa by the wise.
Two hundred and fifty paṇas is recorded as the first degree of fine.

226.s:
madhyamaḥ pañca vijñeyaḥ sahasramapi cottamaḥ /
caurair amūṣito yastu mūṣito 'smīti bhāṣate //
226.d:
मध्यमः पञ्च विज्ञेयः सहस्रमपि चोत्तमः /
चौरैर् अमूषितो यस्तु मूषितो ऽस्मीति भाषते //
226.m:
The middle [fine] is to be known as five [hundred], and the highest as a thousand.
One who, not having been robbed by thieves, declares, "I have been robbed,"

226.s:
tatpradātari bhāpāle sa daṇḍyastāvadeva tu /
yo yāvadviparītārthaṃ mithyā vā yo vadettu taṃ //
226.d:
तत्प्रदातरि भापाले स दण्ड्यस्तावदेव तु /
यो यावद्विपरीतार्थं मिथ्या वा यो वदेत्तु तं //
226.m:
when the king makes compensation to him, shall be fined that very amount.
Whoever speaks of a matter contrary [to fact] or falsely to that extent—

226.s:
tau nṛpeṇa hy adharmajñau dāpyau taddviguṇaṃ damaṃ(3) /
kūṭasākṣyantu kurvāṇāṃstrīn varṇāṃś ca pradāpayet //
226.d:
तौ नृपेण ह्य् अधर्मज्ञौ दाप्यौ तद्द्विगुणं दमं(3) /
कूटसाक्ष्यन्तु कुर्वाणांस्त्रीन् वर्णांश् च प्रदापयेत् //
226.m:
both of those, ignorant of righteousness, the king must compel to pay double that fine.
Those of the three castes who give false witness he should fine;

226.s:
vivāsayedbrāhmaṇantu bhojyo vidhir na hīrataḥ /
nikṣepasya samaṃ mūlyaṃ daṇḍyo nikṣepabhuk tathā //
:n
1 tathācāṣṭau iti cha.. , ja.. ca
2 tāmrikaiḥ kārṣika ity ādiḥ, sāhasaḥ smṛta ity antaḥ
pāṭhaḥ jha.. pustake nāsti
3 yo yāvadityādiḥ, taddviguṇaṃ damamityantaḥ pāṭhaḥ jha..
pustake nāsti
:p 323
226.d:
विवासयेद्ब्राह्मणन्तु भोज्यो विधिर् न हीरतः /
निक्षेपस्य समं मूल्यं दण्ड्यो निक्षेपभुक् तथा //
:न्
1 तथाचाष्टौ इति छ.. , ज.. च
2 ताम्रिकैः कार्षिक इत्य् आदिः, साहसः स्मृत इत्य् अन्तः
पाठः झ.. पुस्तके नास्ति
3 यो यावदित्यादिः, तद्द्विगुणं दममित्यन्तः पाठः झ..
पुस्तके नास्ति
:प् 323
226.m:
a brāhmaṇa, however, he should banish; for [capital] punishment is not prescribed for him.
One who consumes a deposit should be fined equal to the value of the deposit.
[...]
1. "tathā cāṣṭau" in manuscripts cha and ja.
2. The passage beginning "tāmrikaiḥ kārṣikaḥ" up to "sāhasaḥ smṛtaḥ" is missing in manuscript jha.
3. The passage beginning "yo yāvat" up to "taddviguṇaṃ damam" is missing in manuscript jha.

226.s:
vastrādikasya dharmajña tathā dharmo na hīyate /
yo nikṣepaṃ ghātayati yaścānikṣipya yācate //
226.d:
वस्त्रादिकस्य धर्मज्ञ तथा धर्मो न हीयते /
यो निक्षेपं घातयति यश्चानिक्षिप्य याचते //
226.m:
For garments and the like, O knower of duty, the duty is not lost in that way.
He who misappropriates a deposit and he who demands without having deposited,

226.s:
tāvubhau cauravacchāsyau daṇḍyau vā dviguṇaṃ dama /
ajñānādyaḥ pumān kuryāt paradravyasya vikrayaṃ //
226.d:
तावुभौ चौरवच्छास्यौ दण्ड्यौ वा द्विगुणं दम /
अज्ञानाद्यः पुमान् कुर्यात् परद्रव्यस्य विक्रयं //
226.m:
both of them are to be punished like a thief or fined twice the amount.
A person who sells another's property through ignorance

226.s:
nirdoṣo jñānapūrvakantu cauravaddaṇḍamarhati(1) /
mūlyamādāya yaḥ śilpaṃ na dadyād daṇḍya eva saḥ //
226.d:
निर्दोषो ज्ञानपूर्वकन्तु चौरवद्दण्डमर्हति(1) /
मूल्यमादाय यः शिल्पं न दद्याद् दण्ड्य एव सः //
226.m:
is blameless; but one who does so knowingly deserves punishment like a thief.
He who takes the price but does not deliver the craftwork is indeed to be fined.

226.s:
pratiśrutyāpradātāraṃ suvarṇaṃ daṇḍayennṛpaḥ /
bhṛtiṃ gṛhya na kuryādyaḥ karmāṣṭau kṛṣṇalā damaḥ //
226.d:
प्रतिश्रुत्याप्रदातारं सुवर्णं दण्डयेन्नृपः /
भृतिं गृह्य न कुर्याद्यः कर्माष्टौ कृष्णला दमः //
226.m:
The king should fine one suvarṇa him who does not give after promising.
He who, having accepted wages, does not perform the work, his fine is eight kṛṣṇalas.

226.s:
akāle tu tyajan bhṛtyaṃ daṇḍyaḥ syāttāvadeva tu /
krītvā vikrīya vā kiñcidyasyehānuśayo bhavet //
226.d:
अकाले तु त्यजन् भृत्यं दण्ड्यः स्यात्तावदेव तु /
क्रीत्वा विक्रीय वा किञ्चिद्यस्येहानुशयो भवेत् //
226.m:
Dismissing a servant at the wrong time, however, one shall be fined that very amount.
When someone here has regret after having bought or sold something,

226.s:
so 'ntardaśāhāttatsvāmī dadyāccaivādadīta ca /
pareṇa tu daśāhasya nādadyānnaiva dāpayet //
226.d:
सो ऽन्तर्दशाहात्तत्स्वामी दद्याच्चैवाददीत च /
परेण तु दशाहस्य नादद्यान्नैव दापयेत् //
226.m: Within ten days its owner may return it and take it back; / but beyond ten days he shall neither take it back nor cause it to be given.

226.s:
ādadaddhi dadaccaiva rājñā daṇḍyaḥ śatāni ṣaṭ /
vare doṣānavikhyāpya yaḥ kanyāṃ varayediha(2) //
226.d:
आददद्धि ददच्चैव राज्ञा दण्ड्यः शतानि षट् /
वरे दोषानविख्याप्य यः कन्यां वरयेदिह(2) //
226.m: For taking it back or giving it, he should be fined six hundred [paṇas] by the king. / Whoever here chooses a bride without disclosing her blemishes to the groom,

226.s:
dattāpyadattā sā tasya rājñā daṇḍyaḥ śatadvayaṃ /
pradāya kanyāṃ yo 'nyasmai punastāṃ samprayacchati //
226.d:
दत्ताप्यदत्ता सा तस्य राज्ञा दण्ड्यः शतद्वयं /
प्रदाय कन्यां यो ऽन्यस्मै पुनस्तां सम्प्रयच्छति //
226.m: she is not [truly] given even if given; he should be fined two hundred by the king. / Whoever, having given a maiden, bestows her again upon another,

226.s:
daṇḍaḥ kāryo narendreṇa tasyāpyuttamasāhasaḥ /
satyaṅkāreṇa vācā ca yuktaṃ puṇyamasaṃśayaṃ //
226.d:
दण्डः कार्यो नरेन्द्रेण तस्याप्युत्तमसाहसः /
सत्यङ्कारेण वाचा च युक्तं पुण्यमसंशयं //
226.m: a fine of the highest degree of violence should be imposed on him by the king. / A transaction confirmed by an earnest-money pledge and by word is undoubtedly binding.

226.s:
lubdho 'nyatra ca vikretā ṣaṭśataṃ daṇḍamarhati /
dadyāddhenuṃ na yaḥ pālo gṛhītvā bhaktavetanaṃ //
226.d:
लुब्धो ऽन्यत्र च विक्रेता षट्शतं दण्डमर्हति /
दद्याद्धेनुं न यः पालो गृहीत्वा भक्तवेतनं //
226.m: A greedy seller who sells elsewhere deserves a fine of six hundred. / A herdsman who, having received food and wages, does not deliver the cow,

226.s:
sa tu daṇḍyaḥ śataṃ rājñā suvarṇaṃ vāpyarakṣitā /
:n
1 cauravadvadhamarhatoti gha.. , ña.. ca
2 varayedyadi iti gha.. , ña.. ca
:p 324
dhanuḥśataṃ parīṇāho grāmasya tu samantataḥ //
226.d:
स तु दण्ड्यः शतं राज्ञा सुवर्णं वाप्यरक्षिता /
:न्
1 चौरवद्वधमर्हतोति घ.. , ञ.. च
2 वरयेद्यदि इति घ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 324
धनुःशतं परीणाहो ग्रामस्य तु समन्ततः //
226.m:
he, failing to protect it, should be fined one hundred or a suvarṇa by the king.
:n
1. "Deserves death like a thief" in manuscripts gha and ña.
2. "If he chooses" in manuscripts gha and ña. / [Page 324]
The perimeter all around a village should be a hundred bows;

226.s:
dviguṇaṃ triguṇaṃ vāpi nagarasya ca kalpayet /
vṛtiṃ tatra prakurvīta yāmuṣṭro nāvalokayet //
226.d:
द्विगुणं त्रिगुणं वापि नगरस्य च कल्पयेत् /
वृतिं तत्र प्रकुर्वीत यामुष्ट्रो नावलोकयेत् //
226.m: and for a town, one should make it twice or thrice as much. / There one should construct a fence that a camel cannot peer over.

226.s:
tatrāparivṛte dhānye hiṃsite naiva daṇḍanaṃ /
gṛhantaḍāgamārāmaṃ kṣetraṃ vā bhīṣayā haran //
226.d:
तत्रापरिवृते धान्ये हिंसिते नैव दण्डनं /
गृहन्तडागमारामं क्षेत्रं वा भीषया हरन् //
226.m: There, if crops are not fenced in and are damaged, there is no fine. / One who seizes by intimidation a house, a pond, a garden, or a field,

226.s:
śatāni pañca daṇḍyāḥ syādajñānād dviśato damaḥ /
maryādābhedakāḥ sarve daṇḍyāḥ prathamasāhasaṃ //
226.d:
शतानि पञ्च दण्ड्याः स्यादज्ञानाद् द्विशतो दमः /
मर्यादाभेदकाः सर्वे दण्ड्याः प्रथमसाहसं //
226.m: should be fined five hundred; out of ignorance, the fine is two hundred. / All who breach boundary marks are to be fined the first degree of violence.

226.s:
śataṃ brāhmaṇamākruśya kṣatriyo daṇḍamarhati /
vaiśyaś ca dviśataṃ rāma śūdraś ca badhamarhati //
226.d:
शतं ब्राह्मणमाक्रुश्य क्षत्रियो दण्डमर्हति /
वैश्यश् च द्विशतं राम शूद्रश् च बधमर्हति //
226.m: A kṣatriya insulting a brāhmaṇa deserves a fine of one hundred; / a vaiśya [deserves a fine of] two hundred, O Rāma, and a śūdra deserves execution.

226.s:
pañcāśadbrāhmaṇo daṇḍyaḥ kṣatriyasyābhiśaṃsane /
vaiśye vāpyardhapañcāśacchūdre dvādaśako damaḥ //
226.d:
पञ्चाशद्ब्राह्मणो दण्ड्यः क्षत्रियस्याभिशंसने /
वैश्ये वाप्यर्धपञ्चाशच्छूद्रे द्वादशको दमः //
226.m: A brāhmaṇa is to be fined fifty for defaming a kṣatriya; / twenty-five [for defaming] a vaiśya, and a fine of twelve [for defaming] a śūdra.

226.s:
kṣatriyasyāpnuyādvaiśyaḥ sāhasaṃ pūrvameva tu /
śūdraḥ kṣatriyamākruśya jihvācchedanamāpnuyāt //
226.d:
क्षत्रियस्याप्नुयाद्वैश्यः साहसं पूर्वमेव तु /
शूद्रः क्षत्रियमाक्रुश्य जिह्वाच्छेदनमाप्नुयात् //
226.m: Against a kṣatriya, a vaiśya shall incur the first degree of violence; / a śūdra who abuses a kṣatriya shall suffer the cutting off of his tongue.

226.s:
dharmopadeśaṃ viprāṇāṃ śūdraḥ kurvaṃś ca daṇḍabhāk /
śrutadeśādivitathī dāpyo dviguṇasāhasaṃ //
226.d:
धर्मोपदेशं विप्राणां शूद्रः कुर्वंश् च दण्डभाक् /
श्रुतदेशादिवितथी दाप्यो द्विगुणसाहसं //
226.m: A śūdra giving religious instruction to brāhmaṇas incurs punishment. / One who falsifies learning, country, and the like should be made to pay double the violence fine.

226.s:
uttamaḥ sāhasastasya yaḥ pāpair uttamān kṣipet /
pramādādyair mayā proktaṃ prītyā daṇḍārdhamarhati //
226.d:
उत्तमः साहसस्तस्य यः पापैर् उत्तमान् क्षिपेत् /
प्रमादाद्यैर् मया प्रोक्तं प्रीत्या दण्डार्धमर्हति //
226.m: His fine is the highest violence who insults superiors with sins. / For those spoken of by me [as acting] out of negligence, through affection he deserves half the fine.

226.s:
mātaraṃ pitaraṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ bhrātaraṃ śvaśuraṃ guruṃ /
ākṣārayañcchataṃ daṇḍyaḥ panthānaṃ cādadadguroḥ //
226.d:
मातरं पितरं ज्येष्ठं भ्रातरं श्वशुरं गुरुं /
आक्षारयञ्च्छतं दण्ड्यः पन्थानं चाददद्गुरोः //
226.m: Reviling mother, father, eldest brother, father-in-law, or teacher, / and not giving way to a teacher, one should be fined one hundred.

226.s:
antyajātirdvijātintu yenāṅgenāparādhnuyāt /
tadeva cchedayettasya kṣipramevāvicārayan //
226.d:
अन्त्यजातिर्द्विजातिन्तु येनाङ्गेनापराध्नुयात् /
तदेव च्छेदयेत्तस्य क्षिप्रमेवाविचारयन् //
226.m: With whatever limb an outcaste offends against a twice-born man, / that very limb [the king] should have cut off swiftly without hesitation.

226.s:
avaniṣṭhīvato darpād dvāvoṣṭhau chedayennṛpaḥ /
apamūtrayato meḍhramapaśabdayato gudaṃ //
:p 325
226.d:
अवनिष्ठीवतो दर्पाद् द्वावोष्ठौ छेदयेन्नृपः /
अपमूत्रयतो मेढ्रमपशब्दयतो गुदं //
:प् 325
226.m:
The king should cut off both lips of one who spits out of pride, / the penis of one who urinates [at someone], and the anus of one who breaks wind [at someone].
:p 325

226.s:
utkṛṣṭāsanasaṃsthasya nīcasyādhonikṛntanaṃ /
yo yadaṅgaṃ ca rujayettadaṅgantasya kartayet //
226.d:
उत्कृष्टासनसंस्थस्य नीचस्याधोनिकृन्तनं /
यो यदङ्गं च रुजयेत्तदङ्गन्तस्य कर्तयेत् //
226.m: A low-caste person sitting on an elevated seat shall have his buttocks excised. / Whichever limb one injures, that limb of his [the king] shall have cut off.

226.s:
ardhapādakarāḥ kāryā gogajāśvoṣṭraghātakāḥ /
vṛkṣantu viphalaṃ kṛttvā suvarṇaṃ daṇḍamarhati //
226.d:
अर्धपादकराः कार्या गोगजाश्वोष्ट्रघातकाः /
वृक्षन्तु विफलं कृत्त्वा सुवर्णं दण्डमर्हति //
226.m: Those who kill cows, elephants, horses, and camels should have half their feet and hands cut off. / Cutting down a barren tree, one deserves a fine of a suvarṇa;

226.s:
dviguṇaṃ dāpayecchinne pathi sīmni jalāśaye /
dravyāṇi yo haredyasya jñānato 'jñānato 'pivā //
226.d:
द्विगुणं दापयेच्छिन्ने पथि सीम्नि जलाशये /
द्रव्याणि यो हरेद्यस्य ज्ञानतो ऽज्ञानतो ऽपिवा //
226.m: if it is cut on a road, a boundary, or a reservoir, he should be made to pay double. / Whoever steals another’s property, whether knowingly or unknowingly,

226.s:
sa tasyotpādya tuṣṭintu rājñe dadyāttato damaṃ /
yastu rajjuṃ ghaṭaṃ kūpāddharecchindyācca tāṃ prapāṃ //
226.d:
स तस्योत्पाद्य तुष्टिन्तु राज्ञे दद्यात्ततो दमं /
यस्तु रज्जुं घटं कूपाद्धरेच्छिन्द्याच्च तां प्रपां //
226.m: he, having first satisfied the owner, should then pay a fine to the king. / Whoever steals a rope or a pot from a well, or breaks a water-station,

226.s:
sa daṇḍaṃ prāpnuyān māsaṃ daṇḍyaḥ syāt prāṇitā.rane /
dhānyaṃ daśabhyaḥ kumbhebhyo harato 'bhyadhikaṃ badhaḥ //
226.d:
स दण्डं प्राप्नुयान् मासं दण्ड्यः स्यात् प्राणिता.रने /
धान्यं दशभ्यः कुम्भेभ्यो हरतो ऽभ्यधिकं बधः //
226.m: shall incur a fine of a māṣa, and should be fined for crossing over living beings. / For one stealing more than ten kumbhas of grain, the penalty is execution;

226.s:
śeṣe 'pyekādaśaguṇaṃ tasya daṇḍaṃ prakalpayet /
suvarṇarajatādīnāṃ nṛstrīṇāṃ haraṇe badhaḥ //
226.d:
शेषे ऽप्येकादशगुणं तस्य दण्डं प्रकल्पयेत् /
सुवर्णरजतादीनां नृस्त्रीणां हरणे बधः //
226.m: for the remainder, one should fix a fine of eleven times the amount. / In the theft of gold, silver, and the like, or of men and women, the penalty is execution.

226.s:
yena yena yathāṅgena steno nṛṣu viceṣṭate /
tattadeva haredasy pratyādeśāya pārthivaḥ //
226.d:
येन येन यथाङ्गेन स्तेनो नृषु विचेष्टते /
तत्तदेव हरेदस्य् प्रत्यादेशाय पार्थिवः //
226.m: With whatever limb and in whatever manner a thief operates against men, / the king should confiscate that very [limb] of his to deter others.

226.s:
brāhmaṇaḥ śākadhānyādi alpaṃ gṛhṇanna doṣabhāk /
godevārthaṃ haraṃścāpi hanyādduṣṭaṃ badhīdyataṃ //
226.d:
ब्राह्मणः शाकधान्यादि अल्पं गृह्णन्न दोषभाक् /
गोदेवार्थं हरंश्चापि हन्याद्दुष्टं बधीद्यतं //
226.m: A brāhmaṇa taking a small quantity of vegetables, grain, and the like incurs no fault; / nor one taking for the sake of cows or deities. One should slay a villain intent on murder,

226.s:
gṛhakṣetrāpahartāraṃ tathā patnyabhigāminaṃ /
agnidaṃ garadaṃ hanyāttathā cābhyudyatāyudhaṃ //
226.d:
गृहक्षेत्रापहर्तारं तथा पत्न्यभिगामिनं /
अग्निदं गरदं हन्यात्तथा चाभ्युद्यतायुधं //
226.m: one who seizes a house or land, one who violates a wife, / an arsonist, a poisoner, and likewise one with an upraised weapon.

226.s:
rājā gavābhicārādyaṃ hanyāccaivātatāyinaḥ /
parastriyaṃ na bhāṣeta pratiṣiddho viśenna hi //
226.d:
राजा गवाभिचाराद्यं हन्याच्चैवाततायिनः /
परस्त्रियं न भाषेत प्रतिषिद्धो विशेन्न हि //
226.m: The king should slay desperate assailants, such as those who practice sorcery against cattle. / One should not speak to another man's wife; when forbidden, one must certainly not enter.

226.s:
adaṇḍyā strī bhavedrājñā varayanto patiṃ svayaṃ /
uttamāṃ sevamānaḥ strī jaghanyo badhamarhati //
226.d:
अदण्ड्या स्त्री भवेद्राज्ञा वरयन्तो पतिं स्वयं /
उत्तमां सेवमानः स्त्री जघन्यो बधमर्हति //
226.m: A woman who chooses a husband herself shall not be punished by the king. / A base man consorting with a superior woman deserves execution.

226.s:
bhartāraṃ laṅghayedyā tāṃ śvabhiḥ saṅghātayet striyaṃ /
:p 326
savarṇadūṣitāṃ kuryāt piṇḍamātropajīvinīṃ //
226.d:
भर्तारं लङ्घयेद्या तां श्वभिः सङ्घातयेत् स्त्रियं /
:प् 326
सवर्णदूषितां कुर्यात् पिण्डमात्रोपजीविनीं //
226.m:
A woman who transgresses against her husband he should have torn to pieces by dogs.
:p 326
A woman defiled by an equal-class man he should make live on a mere morsel of food.

226.s:
jyāyasā dūṣitā nārī muṇḍanaṃ samavāpnuyāt /
vaiśyāgame tu viprasya kṣatriyasyāntyajāgame //
226.d:
ज्यायसा दूषिता नारी मुण्डनं समवाप्नुयात् /
वैश्यागमे तु विप्रस्य क्षत्रियस्यान्त्यजागमे //
226.m: A woman violated by a man of higher caste shall undergo shaving of the head. / In the case of a brāhmaṇa consorting with a vaiśya woman, or a kṣatriya consorting with an outcaste woman,

226.s:
kṣatriyaḥ prathamaṃ vaiśyo daṇḍyaḥ śūdrāgame bhavet /
gṛhītvā vetanaṃ veśyā lobhādanyatra gacchati //
226.d:
क्षत्रियः प्रथमं वैश्यो दण्ड्यः शूद्रागमे भवेत् /
गृहीत्वा वेतनं वेश्या लोभादन्यत्र गच्छति //
226.m: the kṣatriya incurs the first fine; a vaiśya incurs it for consorting with a śūdra woman. / If a courtesan, having received a wage, goes elsewhere out of greed,

226.s:
vetanandviguṇaṃ dadyāddaṇdañca dviguṇaṃ tathā /
bhāryā putrāś ca dāsāś ca śiṣyo bhrātā ca sodaraḥ //
226.d:
वेतनन्द्विगुणं दद्याद्दण्दञ्च द्विगुणं तथा /
भार्या पुत्राश् च दासाश् च शिष्यो भ्राता च सोदरः //
226.m: she should give twice the wage, and likewise double that as a fine. / A wife, sons, slaves, a pupil, and a full brother,

226.s:
kṛṭāparādhāstāḍyāḥ sūrajvā veṇudalena vā /
pṛṣṭhe na mastake hanyāccaurasyāpnoti kilviṣaṃ //
226.d:
कृटापराधास्ताड्याः सूरज्वा वेणुदलेन वा /
पृष्ठे न मस्तके हन्याच्चौरस्याप्नोति किल्विषं //
226.m: when they have committed an offense, may be struck with a rope or with a split bamboo; / one should strike on the back, not on the head; [otherwise] one incurs the sin of a thief.

226.s:
rakṣāsvadhikṛtaiyastu prajātyarthaṃ vilupyate /
teṣāṃ sarvasvamādāya rājā kuryāt pravāsanaṃ //
226.d:
रक्षास्वधिकृतैयस्तु प्रजात्यर्थं विलुप्यते /
तेषां सर्वस्वमादाय राजा कुर्यात् प्रवासनं //
226.m: When subjects are excessively plundered by those appointed to protect them, / the king, having confiscated all their property, should banish them.

226.s:
ye niyuktāḥ svakāryeṣu hanyuḥ kāryāṇi karmiṇāṃ /
nirghṛṇāḥ krūramanasastānniḥsvān kārayennṛpaḥ //
226.d:
ये नियुक्ताः स्वकार्येषु हन्युः कार्याणि कर्मिणां /
निर्घृणाः क्रूरमनसस्तान्निःस्वान् कारयेन्नृपः //
226.m: Those who, being appointed to their duties, ruin the affairs of workers, / being ruthless and cruel-minded, the king should reduce to destitution.

226.s:
amātyaḥ prāḍvivāko vā yaḥ kuryāt kāryamanyathā /
tasya sarvasvamādāya taṃ rājā vipravāsayet //
226.d:
अमात्यः प्राड्विवाको वा यः कुर्यात् कार्यमन्यथा /
तस्य सर्वस्वमादाय तं राजा विप्रवासयेत् //
226.m: A minister or a judge who handles a matter improperly, / the king, having confiscated all his property, should banish him.

226.s:
gurutalpe bhayaḥ kāryaḥ surāpāṇe surādhvajaḥ /
steyeṣu śvapadaṃ vidyād brahmahatyāśiraḥ pumān //
226.d:
गुरुतल्पे भयः कार्यः सुरापाणे सुराध्वजः /
स्तेयेषु श्वपदं विद्याद् ब्रह्महत्याशिरः पुमान् //
226.m: On the violator of a guru’s bed the mark of a vulva should be made; in liquor-drinking, the tavern-flag; / on thefts, one should brand a dog’s foot; and the headless torso of a man for murdering a brāhmaṇa.

226.s:
śūdrādīn ghātayedrājā pāpān viprān pravāsayet /
mahāpātakināṃ vittaṃ varuṇāyopapādayet //
226.d:
शूद्रादीन् घातयेद्राजा पापान् विप्रान् प्रवासयेत् /
महापातकिनां वित्तं वरुणायोपपादयेत् //
226.m: The king should execute śūdras and the like who are sinful; he should banish brāhmaṇas. / The wealth of perpetrators of heinous crimes he should surrender to Varuṇa.

226.s:
grāmeṣvapi ca ye keciccaurāṇāṃ bhaktadāyakāḥ /
bhāṇḍārakoṣadāś caiva sarvāṃstānapi ghātayet //
226.d:
ग्रामेष्वपि च ये केचिच्चौराणां भक्तदायकाः /
भाण्डारकोषदाश् चैव सर्वांस्तानपि घातयेत् //
226.m: Any persons in villages who give food to thieves / or provide them with goods and shelter, all of them too he should execute.

226.s:
rāṣṭreṣu rāṣṭrādhikṛtān sāmantān pāpino haret /
sandhiṃ kṛtvā tu ye cauryaṃ rātrau kurvanti taskarāḥ //
:p 327
226.d:
राष्ट्रेषु राष्ट्राधिकृतान् सामन्तान् पापिनो हरेत् /
सन्धिं कृत्वा तु ये चौर्यं रात्रौ कुर्वन्ति तस्कराः //
:प् 327
226.m:
In the territories, the king should eliminate wicked district governors and feudatories. / As for robbers who break into houses and commit theft at night,
:p 327

226.s:
teṣāṃ cchitvā nṛpo hastau tīkṣṇe śūle niveśayet /
taḍāgadevatāgārabhedakān ghātayennṛpaḥ //
226.d:
तेषां च्छित्वा नृपो हस्तौ तीक्ष्णे शूले निवेशयेत् /
तडागदेवतागारभेदकान् घातयेन्नृपः //
226.m: having cut off their hands, the king should impale them on a sharp stake. / The king should execute those who destroy reservoirs or temples of the deities.

226.s:
samutsṛjedrājamārge yastvamedhyamanāpadi /
sa hi kārṣāpaṇandaṇḍyastamamedhyañca śodhayet //
226.d:
समुत्सृजेद्राजमार्गे यस्त्वमेध्यमनापदि /
स हि कार्षापणन्दण्ड्यस्तममेध्यञ्च शोधयेत् //
226.m: Whoever discharges filth on the royal highway when there is no emergency, / he should be fined a kārṣāpaṇa and made to clean up that filth.

226.s:
pratimāsaṅkramabhido dadyuḥ pañcaśatāni te /
samaiś ca viṣamaṃ yo vā carate mūlyato 'pi vā //
226.d:
प्रतिमासङ्क्रमभिदो दद्युः पञ्चशतानि ते /
समैश् च विषमं यो वा चरते मूल्यतो ऽपि वा //
226.m: Those who destroy icons and causeways should pay five hundred [paṇas]. / One who deals dishonestly with standard measures or with prices,

226.s:
samāpnuyānnaraḥ pūrvaṃ damaṃ madhyamameva vā /
dravyamādāya vaṇijāmanargheṇāvarundhatāṃ //
226.d:
समाप्नुयान्नरः पूर्वं दमं मध्यममेव वा /
द्रव्यमादाय वणिजामनर्घेणावरुन्धतां //
226.m: that man shall incur the first or the middle degree of punishment. / Against merchants who withhold goods by cornering stock at an unfair price,

226.s:
rājā pṛthak pṛthak kuryāddaṇḍamuttamasāhasaṃ /
dravyāṇāṃ dūṣako yaś ca praticchandakavikrayī //
226.d:
राजा पृथक् पृथक् कुर्याद्दण्डमुत्तमसाहसं /
द्रव्याणां दूषको यश् च प्रतिच्छन्दकविक्रयी //
226.m: the king should impose, individually on each, a fine of the highest degree of violence. / One who adulterates commodities and one who sells counterfeit goods,

226.s:
madhyamaṃ prāpnuyāddaṇḍaṃ kūṭakartā tathottamaṃ /
kalahāpakṛtaṃ deyaṃ daṇḍaś ca dviguṇastataḥ //
226.d:
मध्यमं प्राप्नुयाद्दण्डं कूटकर्ता तथोत्तमं /
कलहापकृतं देयं दण्डश् च द्विगुणस्ततः //
226.m: shall incur the middle fine, and a forger likewise the highest. / What was caused by a brawl must be made good, and the fine is double that.

226.s:
abhakṣyabhakṣye vipre vā śūdre vā kṛṣṇalo damaḥ /
tulāśāsanakartā ca kūṭakṛnnāśakasya ca //
226.d:
अभक्ष्यभक्ष्ये विप्रे वा शूद्रे वा कृष्णलो दमः /
तुलाशासनकर्ता च कूटकृन्नाशकस्य च //
226.m:
When inedible food is eaten, whether by a Brahmin or a Śūdra, the fine is a kṛṣṇala;
as well as for a maker of [false] scales or edicts, and one who destroys a counterfeiter's [work].

226.s:
ebhiś ca vyavahartā yaḥ sa dāpyo damamuttamaṃ /
viṣāgnidāṃ patiguruviprāpatyapramāpiṇīṃ //
226.d:
एभिश् च व्यवहर्ता यः स दाप्यो दममुत्तमं /
विषाग्निदां पतिगुरुविप्रापत्यप्रमापिणीं //
226.m:
And whoever transacts business with these [false items] must be made to pay the highest fine.
A woman who administers poison or fire, or who slays her husband, elder, a Brahmin, or her child,

226.s:
vikarṇakaranāsauṣṭhī kṛtvā gobhiḥ pravāsayet /
kṣetraveśmagrāmavanavidārakās tathā narāḥ //
226.d:
विकर्णकरनासौष्ठी कृत्वा गोभिः प्रवासयेत् /
क्षेत्रवेश्मग्रामवनविदारकास् तथा नराः //
226.m:
after having her ears, hands, nose, and lips cut off, he should have her torn apart by bulls.
Likewise, men who burn down fields, houses, villages, or forests,

226.s:
rājapatnyabhigāmī ca dagdhavyāstu kaṭāgninā /
ūnaṃ vāpyadhikaṃ vāpi likhedyo rājaśāsanaṃ //
226.d:
राजपत्न्यभिगामी च दग्धव्यास्तु कटाग्निना /
ऊनं वाप्यधिकं वापि लिखेद्यो राजशासनं //
226.m:
and one who approaches the king's wife, are to be burned by a fire of straw mats.
Whoever writes an edict of the king with something omitted or added,

226.s:
pārajāyikacaurau ca muñcato daṇḍa uttamaḥ /
rājayānāsanāroḍhurdaṇḍa uttamasāhasaḥ //
226.d:
पारजायिकचौरौ च मुञ्चतो दण्ड उत्तमः /
राजयानासनारोढुर्दण्ड उत्तमसाहसः //
226.m:
or one who releases an adulterer or a thief, the fine is the highest.
For one who mounts the king’s vehicle or seat, the fine is the highest degree of punishment.

226.s:
yo manyetājito 'smīti nyāyenāpi parājitaḥ /
:p 328
tamāyāntaṃ parājitya(1) daṇḍayed dviguṇaṃ damaṃ //
226.d:
यो मन्येताजितो ऽस्मीति न्यायेनापि पराजितः /
:प् 328
तमायान्तं पराजित्य(1) दण्डयेद् द्विगुणं दमं //
226.m:
One who thinks, “I am not defeated,” even when defeated according to justice—
[Page 328]
having defeated him when he returns, [the king] should fine him double the punishment.

226.s:
āhvānakārī badhyaḥ syādanāhūtamathāhvayan /
dāṇḍikasya ca yo hastādabhimuktaḥ palāyate //
226.d:
आह्वानकारी बध्यः स्यादनाहूतमथाह्वयन् /
दाण्डिकस्य च यो हस्तादभिमुक्तः पलायते //
226.m:
The summoner who summons one who was not summoned is liable to execution.
And whoever escapes after slipping from the hands of the officer of justice,

226.s:
hīnaḥ puruṣakāreṇa tad dadyāddāṇḍiko dhanaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe daṇḍapraṇayanaṃ nāma
ṣaḍviṃśatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha saptaviṃśatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
yuddhayātrā
226.d:
हीनः पुरुषकारेण तद् दद्याद्दाण्डिको धनं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे दण्डप्रणयनं नाम
षड्विंशत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ सप्तविंशत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
युद्धयात्रा
226.m:
failing through his lack of manly effort, that officer must pay the money.
Thus in the great Agni Purāṇa, the two hundred and twenty-sixth chapter, entitled “The Administration of Punishment.”
Now the two hundred and twenty-seventh chapter.
Expedition for War

227.s:
puṣkara uvāca
yadā manyeta nṛpatirākrandena balīyasā /
pārṣṇigrāho 'bhibhūto me tadā yātrāṃ prayojayet //
227.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
यदा मन्येत नृपतिराक्रन्देन बलीयसा /
पार्ष्णिग्राहो ऽभिभूतो मे तदा यात्रां प्रयोजयेत् //
227.m:
Puṣkara said:
When the king considers, “My rear enemy is overcome / by a stronger ally of the rear,” then he should undertake an expedition.

227.s:
puṣtā yodhā bhṛṭā bhṛtyāḥ prabhūtañca balaṃ mama /
mūlarakṣāsamartho 'smi tair gatvā(2) śivire vrajet //
227.d:
पुष्ता योधा भृटा भृत्याः प्रभूतञ्च बलं मम /
मूलरक्षासमर्थो ऽस्मि तैर् गत्वा(2) शिविरे व्रजेत् //
227.m:
“My warriors are nourished, my servants maintained, and my army is abundant;
I am capable of guarding the base”; having gone with them, he should enter the camp.

227.s:
śatrorvā vyasane yāyāt daivādyaiḥ pīḍitaṃ paraṃ /
bhūkampo yāndiśaṃ yāti yāñca keturvyadūṣayat //
227.d:
शत्रोर्वा व्यसने यायात् दैवाद्यैः पीडितं परं /
भूकम्पो यान्दिशं याति याञ्च केतुर्व्यदूषयत् //
227.m:
Or he should march during an enemy’s misfortune, when the foe is oppressed by fate or the like,
towards the direction an earthquake goes, and [the direction] which a comet has afflicted,

227.s:
vidviṣṭanāśakaṃ sainyaṃ sambhūtāntaḥprakopanaṃ(3) /
śarīrasphuraṇe dhanye tathā susvapradarśane //
227.d:
विद्विष्टनाशकं सैन्यं सम्भूतान्तःप्रकोपनं(3) /
शरीरस्फुरणे धन्ये तथा सुस्वप्रदर्शने //
227.m:
against an army that destroys the hated enemy and whose internal anger has arisen,
when there is an auspicious throbbing of the body and likewise upon seeing a good dream,

227.s:
nimitte śakune dhanye jāte śatrupuraṃ vrajet /
:n
1 punarjitveti ga.. , gha.. , ja.. ca
2 tair vṛtvā iti sādhuḥ
3 sambhūtāntaḥkopadamiti kha.. , cha.. ca
:p 329
padātināgabahulāṃ senāṃ prāvṛṣi yojayet //
227.d:
निमित्ते शकुने धन्ये जाते शत्रुपुरं व्रजेत् /
:न्
1 पुनर्जित्वेति ग.. , घ.. , ज.. च
2 तैर् वृत्वा इति साधुः
3 सम्भूतान्तःकोपदमिति ख.. , छ.. च
:प् 329
पदातिनागबहुलां सेनां प्रावृषि योजयेत् //
227.m:
and when an auspicious omen or bird-sign has occurred, he should advance toward the enemy's city.
[...]
1 ga., gha., and ja. read "punarjitvā"
2 "tair vṛtvā" is correct
3 kha. and cha. read "sambhūtāntaḥkopadam"
[Page 329]
He should deploy an army rich in infantry and elephants in the rainy season;

227.s:
hemante śiśire caiva rathavājisamākulāṃ /
caturaṅgabalopetāṃ vasante vā śaranmmukhe(1) //
227.d:
हेमन्ते शिशिरे चैव रथवाजिसमाकुलां /
चतुरङ्गबलोपेतां वसन्ते वा शरन्म्मुखे(1) //
227.m:
in early winter and late winter, one crowded with chariots and horses;
endowed with all four divisions of the army in the spring or at the beginning of autumn.

227.s:
senā padātibahulā śatrūn jayati sarvadā /
aṅgasakṣiṇabhāge tu śastaṃ prasphuraṇaṃ bhavet //
227.d:
सेना पदातिबहुला शत्रून् जयति सर्वदा /
अङ्गसक्षिणभागे तु शस्तं प्रस्फुरणं भवेत् //
227.m:
An army abundant in infantry conquers enemies at all times.
Throbbing on the right side of the body is auspicious,

227.s:
na śastantu tathā vāme pṛṣṭhasya hṛdayasya ca /
lāñchanaṃ piṭakañcaiva vijñeyaṃ sphuraṇaṃ tathā //
227.d:
न शस्तन्तु तथा वामे पृष्ठस्य हृदयस्य च /
लाञ्छनं पिटकञ्चैव विज्ञेयं स्फुरणं तथा //
227.m:
but is not auspicious likewise on the left, on the back, or on the heart.
A mark, an eruption, and likewise a throbbing are to be understood [in this manner].

227.s:
viparyayeṇābhihitaṃ savye strīṇāṃ śubhaṃ bhavet /
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe yātrā nāma saptaviṃśatyadhikadviśatatamo
'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś athāṣṭāviṃśatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
svapnādhyāyaḥ
227.d:
विपर्ययेणाभिहितं सव्ये स्त्रीणां शुभं भवेत् /
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे यात्रा नाम सप्तविंशत्यधिकद्विशततमो
ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथाष्टाविंशत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
स्वप्नाध्यायः
227.m:
In reverse it is declared [for women]: on the left side it is auspicious for women.
Thus in the great Agni Purāṇa, the two hundred and twenty-seventh chapter, entitled “The Expedition.”
Now the two hundred and twenty-eighth chapter.
Chapter on Dreams

228.s:
puṣkara uvāca
svapnaṃ śaubhāśubhaṃ vakṣye duḥkhapraharaṇantathā /
nābhiṃ vinānyatra gātre tṛṇavṛkṣasamudbhavaḥ //
228.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
स्वप्नं शौभाशुभं वक्ष्ये दुःखप्रहरणन्तथा /
नाभिं विनान्यत्र गात्रे तृणवृक्षसमुद्भवः //
228.m:
Puṣkara said:
I shall explain auspicious and inauspicious dreams, as well as the warding off of distress:
the sprouting of grass or trees on the body anywhere other than the navel,

228.s:
cūrṇaṃ mūrdhni kāṃsyānāṃ muṇḍanaṃ nagnatā tathā /
malināmbaradhāritvamabhyaṅgaḥ paṅkadigdhatā //
228.d:
चूर्णं मूर्ध्नि कांस्यानां मुण्डनं नग्नता तथा /
मलिनाम्बरधारित्वमभ्यङ्गः पङ्कदिग्धता //
228.m:
powder on the head, [breaking] of bell-metal vessels, shaving of the head, and nakedness;
wearing soiled garments, rubbing with oil, and being smeared with mud;

228.s:
uccāt prapatanañcaiva vivāho gītameva ca /
tantrīvādyavinodaś ca dolārohaṇameva ca //
228.d:
उच्चात् प्रपतनञ्चैव विवाहो गीतमेव च /
तन्त्रीवाद्यविनोदश् च दोलारोहणमेव च //
228.m:
falling from a high place, marriage, singing,
entertainment with stringed instruments, and mounting a swing;

228.s:
arjanaṃ padmalohānāṃ sarpāṇāmatha māraṇaṃ /
:n
1 śaradyaśceti ña.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 330
raktapuṣpadrumāṇāñca caṇḍālasya tathaiva ca //
228.d:
अर्जनं पद्मलोहानां सर्पाणामथ मारणं /
:न्
1 शरद्यश्चेति ञ.. , ट.. च
:प् 330
रक्तपुष्पद्रुमाणाञ्च चण्डालस्य तथैव च //

228.s:
varāhāśvakharoṣṭrāṇāṃ tathā cārohaṇakriyā /
bhakṣaṇaṃ pakṣimāṃsānāṃ tailasya kṛśarasya ca(1) //
228.d:
वराहाश्वखरोष्ट्राणां तथा चारोहणक्रिया /
भक्षणं पक्षिमांसानां तैलस्य कृशरस्य च(1) //
228.m:
the act of mounting boars, horses, donkeys, or camels;
eating the flesh of birds, oil, or rice cooked with sesamum;

228.s:
mātuḥ praveśo jaṭhare citārohaṇameva ca /
śakradhvajābhipatanaṃ patanaṃ śaśisūryayoḥ //
228.d:
मातुः प्रवेशो जठरे चितारोहणमेव च /
शक्रध्वजाभिपतनं पतनं शशिसूर्ययोः //
228.m:
entering the mother's womb, climbing onto a funeral pyre,
the falling of Indra's banner, the falling of the moon and sun;

228.s:
divyāntarīkṣabhaumānāmutpātānāñca darśanaṃ /
devadvijātibhūpānāṃ gurūṇāṅkopa eva ca //
228.d:
दिव्यान्तरीक्षभौमानामुत्पातानाञ्च दर्शनं /
देवद्विजातिभूपानां गुरूणाङ्कोप एव च //
228.m:
the sighting of celestial, atmospheric, and terrestrial portents;
and the anger of gods, twice-born, kings, or elders;

228.s:
nartanaṃ hasanañcaiva vivāho gītameva ca(2) /
tantrīvādyavihīnānāṃ vādyānāmapi vādanaṃ //
228.d:
नर्तनं हसनञ्चैव विवाहो गीतमेव च(2) /
तन्त्रीवाद्यविहीनानां वाद्यानामपि वादनं //
228.m:
dancing, laughing, marriage, and singing;
and the playing of musical instruments other than stringed instruments;

228.s:
srotovahādhogamanaṃ snānaṃ gomayavāriṇā /
paṅkodakena ca tathā maśītoyena vāpyatha //
228.d:
स्रोतोवहाधोगमनं स्नानं गोमयवारिणा /
पङ्कोदकेन च तथा मशीतोयेन वाप्यथ //
228.m:
going downstream in a river, bathing with cow dung water,
or with muddy water, or with ink water;

228.s:
āliṅganaṃ kumārīṇāṃ puruṣāñca maithunaṃ(3) /
hāniś caiva svagātrāṇāṃ vireko vamanakriyā //
228.d:
आलिङ्गनं कुमारीणां पुरुषाञ्च मैथुनं(3) /
हानिश् चैव स्वगात्राणां विरेको वमनक्रिया //
228.m:
embracing maidens, copulating with men,
loss of one's own limbs, purging, and vomiting;

228.s:
dakṣiṇāśāpragamanaṃ vyādhinābhibhavas tathā /
phalānāmupahāniś ca dhātūnāṃ bhedanaṃ tathā //
228.d:
दक्षिणाशाप्रगमनं व्याधिनाभिभवस् तथा /
फलानामुपहानिश् च धातूनां भेदनं तथा //
228.m:
setting out toward the southern quarter, being overcome by illness,
loss of fruits, and destruction of minerals [or bodily constituents];

228.s:
gṛhāṇāñcaiva patanaṃ gṛhasammārjanantathā /
krīḍā piśācakravyādavānarāntyanarair api //
228.d:
गृहाणाञ्चैव पतनं गृहसम्मार्जनन्तथा /
क्रीडा पिशाचक्रव्यादवानरान्त्यनरैर् अपि //
228.m:
the falling of houses, sweeping the house,
and sporting with Piśācas, carnivorous beasts, monkeys, or outcasts;

228.s:
parādabhibhavaś caiva tasmācca vyasanodbhavaḥ /
kāṣāyavastradhāritvaṃ tadvastraiḥ krīḍanaṃ tathā(4) //
:n
1 tantrīvādyavinodaścetyādiḥ, tailasya kṛśarasya cetyantaḥ
pāṭhaḥ cha.. , jha.. pustakadvaye nāsti
2 vivāhotsava eva ceti ja..
3 tāsāmeva ca maithunamiti ja..
4 hāniś caivetyādiḥ. krīḍanaṃ tathetyantaḥ pāṭhaḥ ja.. pustake
nāsti
:p 331
228.d:
परादभिभवश् चैव तस्माच्च व्यसनोद्भवः /
काषायवस्त्रधारित्वं तद्वस्त्रैः क्रीडनं तथा(4) //
:न्
1 तन्त्रीवाद्यविनोदश्चेत्यादिः, तैलस्य कृशरस्य चेत्यन्तः
पाठः छ.. , झ.. पुस्तकद्वये नास्ति
2 विवाहोत्सव एव चेति ज..
3 तासामेव च मैथुनमिति ज..
4 हानिश् चैवेत्यादिः. क्रीडनं तथेत्यन्तः पाठः ज.. पुस्तके
नास्ति
:प् 331
228.m:
defeat by another, and the arising of calamity therefrom;
wearing ochre robes and sporting with such robes;
[...]
1 The passage beginning with "tantrīvādyavinodaś ca" and ending with "tailasya kṛśarasya ca" is missing in the two manuscripts cha. and jha.
2 ja. reads "vivāhotsava eva ca"
3 ja. reads "tāsāmeva ca maithunam"
4 The passage beginning with "hāniś caiva" and ending with "krīḍanaṃ tathā" is missing in the manuscript ja.
[Page 331]

228.s:
snehapānāvagāhau ca raktamālyānulepanaṃ /
ityadhānyāni svapnāni teṣāmakathanaṃ śubhaṃ //
228.d:
स्नेहपानावगाहौ च रक्तमाल्यानुलेपनं /
इत्यधान्यानि स्वप्नानि तेषामकथनं शुभं //
228.m:
drinking oil and plunging into it, and anointing oneself with red garlands:
these are inauspicious dreams; not speaking of them is auspicious.

228.s:
bhūjaś ca svapanaṃ tadvat kāryāṃ snānaṃ dvijārcanaṃ /
tilair homo haribrahmaśivārkagaṇapūjanaṃ //
228.d:
भूजश् च स्वपनं तद्वत् कार्यां स्नानं द्विजार्चनं /
तिलैर् होमो हरिब्रह्मशिवार्कगणपूजनं //
228.m:
Sleeping again likewise, bathing, and worshiping twice-born are to be performed;
a fire oblation with sesamum, worship of Hari, Brahmā, Śiva, the Sun, and Gaṇeśa,

228.s:
tathā stutiprapaṭhanaṃ puṃsūktādijapas tathā /
svapnāstu prathame yāme(1) saṃvatsaravipākinaḥ //
228.d:
तथा स्तुतिप्रपठनं पुंसूक्तादिजपस् तथा /
स्वप्नास्तु प्रथमे यामे(1) संवत्सरविपाकिनः //
228.m:
likewise recitation of hymns of praise, and recitation of the Puruṣasūkta and other hymns.
Dreams [seen] in the first watch of the night bear fruit in a year;

228.s:
ṣaḍbhirmāsair dvitīye tu tribhirmāsair triyāmikāḥ /
caturthe tvardhamāsena daśāhādaruṇodaye //
228.d:
षड्भिर्मासैर् द्वितीये तु त्रिभिर्मासैर् त्रियामिकाः /
चतुर्थे त्वर्धमासेन दशाहादरुणोदये //
228.m:
in the second, in six months; those in the third watch, in three months;
in the fourth, in half a month; and at dawn, in ten days.

228.s:
ekasyāmatha cedrātrau śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubhaṃ /
paścādṛṣṭastu yastatra tasya pākaṃ vinirdiśet //
228.d:
एकस्यामथ चेद्रात्रौ शुभं वा यदि वाशुभं /
पश्चादृष्टस्तु यस्तत्र तस्य पाकं विनिर्दिशेत् //
228.m:
If in a single night [dreams are seen], whether auspicious or inauspicious,
whichever is seen later among them, its fruition one should predict.

228.s:
tasmāttu śobhane svapne paścātsvāpo na śasyate /
śailaprāsādanāgāśvavṛṣabhārohaṇaṃ hitaṃ //
228.d:
तस्मात्तु शोभने स्वप्ने पश्चात्स्वापो न शस्यते /
शैलप्रासादनागाश्ववृषभारोहणं हितं //
228.m:
Therefore, after an auspicious dream, sleeping again is not recommended.
Climbing a mountain, a palace, an elephant, a horse, or a bull is favorable;

228.s:
drumāṇāṃ śvetapuṣpāṇāṃ gagane ca tathā dvija /
drumatṛṇodbhavo nābhau tathā ca bahubāhutā //
228.d:
द्रुमाणां श्वेतपुष्पाणां गगने च तथा द्विज /
द्रुमतृणोद्भवो नाभौ तथा च बहुबाहुता //
228.m:
trees with white flowers, and likewise [flying] in the sky, O twice-born;
trees and grass growing in the navel, and having many arms;

228.s:
tathā ca bahuśīrṣatvaṃ palitodbhava eva ca /
suśukramālyadhāritvaṃ suśuklāmbaradhāritā //
228.d:
तथा च बहुशीर्षत्वं पलितोद्भव एव च /
सुशुक्रमाल्यधारित्वं सुशुक्लाम्बरधारिता //
228.m: Likewise, having many heads and the appearance of grey hair, / wearing bright white garlands, and wearing bright white garments,

228.s:
candrārkatārāgrahaṇaṃ parimārjanameva ca /
śakradhvajāliṅganañca dhvajocchrāyakriyā tathā //
228.d:
चन्द्रार्कताराग्रहणं परिमार्जनमेव च /
शक्रध्वजालिङ्गनञ्च ध्वजोच्छ्रायक्रिया तथा //
228.m: Seizing the moon, sun, and stars, and wiping them off, / embracing Indra's banner, and raising the banner,

228.s:
bhūmyabudhārāgrahaṇaṃ(2) śatrūṇāñcaiva vikriyā /
jayo vivāde dyūte ca saṅgrāme ca tathā dvija //
228.d:
भूम्यबुधाराग्रहणं(2) शत्रूणाञ्चैव विक्रिया /
जयो विवादे द्यूते च सङ्ग्रामे च तथा द्विज //
228.m: Seizing the earth and streams of water, the defeat of enemies, / and victory in dispute, gambling, and battle, O twice-born;

228.s:
bhakṣaṇañcārdramāṃsānāmpāyasasya ca bhakṣaṇaṃ /
darśanaṃ rudhirasyāpi snānaṃ vā rudhireṇa ca //
:n
1 prathame bhāge iti kha..
2 bhūmyambudhīnāṃ grahaṇamiti ka.. , cha.. , ña.. ca
:p 332
228.d:
भक्षणञ्चार्द्रमांसानाम्पायसस्य च भक्षणं /
दर्शनं रुधिरस्यापि स्नानं वा रुधिरेण च //
:न्
1 प्रथमे भागे इति ख..
2 भूम्यम्बुधीनां ग्रहणमिति क.. , छ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 332
228.m:
Eating raw meat and eating milk-rice, / seeing blood, or bathing in blood,
[Variant reading: 'in the first part' in manuscript kha.]
[Variant reading: 'seizing the earth and oceans' in manuscripts ka, cha, and ña. Page 332]

228.s:
sarārudhiramadyānāṃ pānaṃ kṣīrasya vāpyatha /
astrair viceṣṭanaṃ bhūmau nirmalaṃ gaganaṃ tathā //
228.d:
सरारुधिरमद्यानां पानं क्षीरस्य वाप्यथ /
अस्त्रैर् विचेष्टनं भूमौ निर्मलं गगनं तथा //
228.m: Drinking serum, blood, wine, or milk, / rolling about on the ground with weapons, and a clear sky;

228.s:
mukhena dohanaṃ śastaṃ mahiṣīṇāṃ tathā gavāṃ /
siṃhīnāṃ hastinīnāñca baḍavānāṃ tathaiva ca //
228.d:
मुखेन दोहनं शस्तं महिषीणां तथा गवां /
सिंहीनां हस्तिनीनाञ्च बडवानां तथैव च //
228.m: Milking she-buffaloes and cows with one's mouth is auspicious, / as well as lionesses, cow-elephants, and mares;

228.s:
prasādo devaviprebhyo gurubhyaś ca tathā dvija /
ambhasā cābhiṣekastu gavāṃ śṛṅgacyutena ca //
228.d:
प्रसादो देवविप्रेभ्यो गुरुभ्यश् च तथा द्विज /
अम्भसा चाभिषेकस्तु गवां शृङ्गच्युतेन च //
228.m: Grace from gods, brahmins, and teachers, O twice-born, / and consecration by aspersion with water falling from a cow's horn

228.s:
candrād bhraṣṭena vā rāma jñeyaṃ rājyapradaṃ hi tat /
rājyābhiṣekaś ca tathā chedanaṃ śiraso 'pyatha //
228.d:
चन्द्राद् भ्रष्टेन वा राम ज्ञेयं राज्यप्रदं हि तत् /
राज्याभिषेकश् च तथा छेदनं शिरसो ऽप्यथ //
228.m: Or fallen from the moon—that, O Rāma, should be known to bestow kingship; / as well as royal consecration by aspersion, and even the severing of one's head,

228.s:
maraṇaṃ vahnilābhaś ca vahnidāho gṛhādiṣu /
labdheś ca rājaliṅgānāṃ tantrīvādyābhivādanaṃ //
228.d:
मरणं वह्निलाभश् च वह्निदाहो गृहादिषु /
लब्धेश् च राजलिङ्गानां तन्त्रीवाद्याभिवादनं //
228.m: Death, obtaining fire, fire burning down houses and the like, / the acquisition of royal emblems, and the playing of stringed musical instruments.

228.s:
yastu paśyati svapnānte rājānaṃ kuñjaraṃ hayaṃ /
hiraṇyaṃ vṛṣabhaṅgāñca kuṭumbastasya vardhate //
228.d:
यस्तु पश्यति स्वप्नान्ते राजानं कुञ्जरं हयं /
हिरण्यं वृषभङ्गाञ्च कुटुम्बस्तस्य वर्धते //
228.m: He who sees at the end of a dream a king, an elephant, a horse, / gold, a bull, and a cow, his family prospers:

228.s:
vṛṣebhagṛhaśailāgravṛkṣārohaṇarodanaṃ /
ghṛṭaviṣṭhānulepo vā agamyāgamanaṃ tathā //
228.d:
वृषेभगृहशैलाग्रवृक्षारोहणरोदनं /
घृटविष्ठानुलेपो वा अगम्यागमनं तथा //
228.m: Mounting a bull, an elephant, a house, a mountain peak, or a tree; weeping; / anointing with ghee or feces; intercourse with forbidden women;

228.s:
sitavastraṃ prasannāmbhaḥ phalī vṛkṣo nabho 'malaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe svapnādhyāyī nāma
aṣṭāviṃśatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha ekonatriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
śakunāni
228.d:
सितवस्त्रं प्रसन्नाम्भः फली वृक्षो नभो ऽमलं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे स्वप्नाध्यायी नाम
अष्टाविंशत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ एकोनत्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
शकुनानि
228.m:
White garments, clear water, a fruit-bearing tree, and a spotless sky.
Thus ends the two hundred and twenty-eighth chapter, called 'The Chapter on Dreams', in the Great Purāṇa of Agni.
Now begins the two hundred and twenty-ninth chapter:
Omens.

229.s:
puṣkara uvāca
auṣadhāni ca yuktāni dhānyaṃ kṛṣṇamaśobhanaṃ /
kārpāsaṃ tṛṇaśuṣkañca gomayaṃ vai dhanāni ca //
:p 333
229.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
औषधानि च युक्तानि धान्यं कृष्णमशोभनं /
कार्पासं तृणशुष्कञ्च गोमयं वै धनानि च //
:प् 333
229.m:
Puṣkara said: / Medicines properly prepared, and black grain is inauspicious; / cotton, dry grass, cow dung, and riches;
[Page 333]

229.s:
aṅgāraṃ guḍasarjau ca(1) muṇḍābhyaktañca nagnakaṃ /
ayaḥ paṅkaṃ carmakeśau unmattañca napuṃsakaṃ //
229.d:
अङ्गारं गुडसर्जौ च(1) मुण्डाभ्यक्तञ्च नग्नकं /
अयः पङ्कं चर्मकेशौ उन्मत्तञ्च नपुंसकं //
229.m: Charcoal, jaggery and resin, a shaven-headed person anointed with oil, a naked person, / iron, mud, hide, hair, a madman, and a eunuch;

229.s:
caṇḍālaśvapacādyāni narā bandhanapālakāḥ /
garbhiṇī strī ca vidhavāḥ piṇyakādīni vai mṛtaṃ //
229.d:
चण्डालश्वपचाद्यानि नरा बन्धनपालकाः /
गर्भिणी स्त्री च विधवाः पिण्यकादीनि वै मृतं //
229.m: Caṇḍālas, dog-cookers, and the like, men who are prison guards, / a pregnant woman, widows, oil-cake and the like, and a corpse;
Chaff, ashes, skulls, bones, and broken vessels are inauspicious; / an inauspicious instrumental sound is harsh, fearful, and shrill.

229.s:
ehīti purataḥ śabdaḥ śasyate na tu pṛṣṭhataḥ /
gaccheti paścācchabdo 'gryaḥ purastāttu vigarhitaḥ //
229.d:
एहीति पुरतः शब्दः शस्यते न तु पृष्ठतः /
गच्छेति पश्चाच्छब्दो ऽग्र्यः पुरस्तात्तु विगर्हितः //
229.m: The sound 'Come!' in front is praised, but not behind; / the sound 'Go!' behind is excellent, but censured in front.

229.s:
kva yāsi tiṣṭha mā gaccha kinte tatra gatasya ca /
aniṣṭaśabdā mṛtyarthaṃ kravyādaś ca dhvajādigaḥ //
229.d:
क्व यासि तिष्ठ मा गच्छ किन्ते तत्र गतस्य च /
अनिष्टशब्दा मृत्यर्थं क्रव्यादश् च ध्वजादिगः //
229.m: Thus ends the two hundred and twenty-ninth chapter, called 'The Chapter on Auspicious Omens', in the Great Purāṇa of Agni.

229.s:
skhalanaṃ vāhanānāñca śastrabhaṅgastathaiva ca /
śiroghātaś ca dvārādyaiścchatravāsādipātanaṃ //
229.d:
स्खलनं वाहनानाञ्च शस्त्रभङ्गस्तथैव च /
शिरोघातश् च द्वाराद्यैश्च्छत्रवासादिपातनं //
229.m: The stumbling of mounts, the breaking of weapons, / striking the head on doors and the like, and the falling of an umbrella, garment, and the like:

229.s:
harimabhyarcya saṃstutya syādamaṅgalyanāśanaṃ /
dvitīyantu tato dṛṣṭvā viruddhaṃ praviśedgṛhaṃ //
229.d:
हरिमभ्यर्च्य संस्तुत्य स्यादमङ्गल्यनाशनं /
द्वितीयन्तु ततो दृष्ट्वा विरुद्धं प्रविशेद्गृहं //
229.m: By worshipping and praising Hari, inauspiciousness is destroyed; / but having seen a second contrary [omen] thereafter, one should enter the house.

229.s:
śvetāḥ sumanasaḥ śreṣṭhāḥ pūrṇakumbho mahottamaḥ /
māṃsaṃ matsyā dūraśabdā vṛddha ekaḥ paśustvajaḥ //
229.d:
श्वेताः सुमनसः श्रेष्ठाः पूर्णकुम्भो महोत्तमः /
मांसं मत्स्या दूरशब्दा वृद्ध एकः पशुस्त्वजः //
229.m: White flowers are best; a full pitcher is most excellent; / meat, fish, sounds from afar, one old animal, namely a goat;

229.s:
gāvastaraṅgamā nāgā devaś ca jvalito 'nalaḥ /
dūrvārdragomayaṃ veśyā svarṇarūpyañca ratnakaṃ //
229.d:
गावस्तरङ्गमा नागा देवश् च ज्वलितो ऽनलः /
दूर्वार्द्रगोमयं वेश्या स्वर्णरूप्यञ्च रत्नकं //
229.m: Cows, horses, elephants, a deity, and a blazing fire; / dūrvā grass, moist cow dung, a courtesan, gold, silver, and jewels;

229.s:
vacāsiddhārthakauṣadhyo mudga āyudhakhaḍgakaṃ /
chatraṃ pīṭhaṃ rājaliṅgaṃ śavaṃ ruditavarjitaṃ //
229.d:
वचासिद्धार्थकौषध्यो मुद्ग आयुधखड्गकं /
छत्रं पीठं राजलिङ्गं शवं रुदितवर्जितं //
229.m: Sweet flag, white mustard, medicinal herbs, kidney beans, weapons, swords, / an umbrella, a throne, a royal insignia, a corpse unaccompanied by weeping;

229.s:
phalaṃ ghṛṭaṃ dadhi payo akṣatādarśamākṣikaṃ /
śaṅkhaṃ ikṣuḥ śubhaṃ vākyaṃ bhaktavāditagītakaṃ //
:n
1 guḍasarpau ceti ga.. , gha.. , ña.. ca
:p 334
229.d:
फलं घृटं दधि पयो अक्षतादर्शमाक्षिकं /
शङ्खं इक्षुः शुभं वाक्यं भक्तवादितगीतकं //
:न्
1 गुडसर्पौ चेति ग.. , घ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 334

229.s:
gambhīrameghastanitaṃ taḍittuṣṭiś ca mānasī /
ekataḥ sarvaliṅgāni manasastuṣṭirekataḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe māṅgalyādhyāyo nāma
ekonatriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha triṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
śakunāni
229.d:
गम्भीरमेघस्तनितं तडित्तुष्टिश् च मानसी /
एकतः सर्वलिङ्गानि मनसस्तुष्टिरेकतः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे माङ्गल्याध्यायो नाम
एकोनत्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ त्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
शकुनानि
229.m:
Deep rumbling of clouds, lightning, and mental satisfaction: / on one side are all signs, and on the other is the satisfaction of the mind.
Thus ends the two hundred and twenty-ninth chapter, entitled "The Chapter on Auspicious Things," in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the two hundred and thirtieth chapter:
Omens.

230.s:
puṣkara uvāca
tiṣṭhato gamane praśne puruṣasya śubhāśubhaṃ /
nivedayanti śakunā deśasya nagarasya ca //
230.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
तिष्ठतो गमने प्रश्ने पुरुषस्य शुभाशुभं /
निवेदयन्ति शकुना देशस्य नगरस्य च //
230.m: Puṣkara said: / When a man is staying still, departing, or making an inquiry, omens indicate / the good and evil fortune of a region and a city.

230.s:
sarvaḥ pāpaphalo dīpto nirdiṣṭo daivacintikaiḥ /
śāntaḥ śubhaphalaś caiva daivajñaiḥ samudāhṛtaḥ //
230.d:
सर्वः पापफलो दीप्तो निर्दिष्टो दैवचिन्तिकैः /
शान्तः शुभफलश् चैव दैवज्ञैः समुदाहृतः //
230.m: Every inflamed [omen] is proclaimed by interpreters of fate as yielding evil results; / a tranquil [omen] is declared by astrologers as yielding auspicious results.

230.s:
ṣaṭprakārā vinirdiṣṭā śakunānāñca dīptayaḥ /
velādigdeśakaraṇarutajātivibhedataḥ //
230.d:
षट्प्रकारा विनिर्दिष्टा शकुनानाञ्च दीप्तयः /
वेलादिग्देशकरणरुतजातिविभेदतः //
230.m: The inflamed states of omens are stated to be of six kinds, / differentiated by time, direction, place, action, cry, and species.

230.s:
pūrvā pūrvā ca vijñeyā sā teṣāṃ balavattarā /
divācaro rātricaras tathā rātrau divācaraḥ //
230.d:
पूर्वा पूर्वा च विज्ञेया सा तेषां बलवत्तरा /
दिवाचरो रात्रिचरस् तथा रात्रौ दिवाचरः //
230.m: Each preceding one among them is to be known as stronger: / a diurnal creature moving at night, or a nocturnal creature moving by day;

230.s:
krūreṣu dīptā vijñeyā ṛkṣalagnagrahādiṣu /
dhūmitā sā tu vijñeyā yāṅgamiṣyati bhāskaraḥ //
230.d:
क्रूरेषु दीप्ता विज्ञेया ऋक्षलग्नग्रहादिषु /
धूमिता सा तु विज्ञेया याङ्गमिष्यति भास्करः //
230.m: It should be known as inflamed under cruel asterisms, ascendants, planets, and the like. / That direction toward which the sun will proceed is to be known as 'smoky';

230.s:
yasyāṃ sthitaḥ sā jvalitā muktā cāṅgāriṇī matā /
etāstisraḥ smṛtā dīptāḥ pañca śāntās tathāparāḥ //
:p 335
230.d:
यस्यां स्थितः सा ज्वलिता मुक्ता चाङ्गारिणी मता /
एतास्तिस्रः स्मृता दीप्ताः पञ्च शान्तास् तथापराः //
:प् 335
230.m:
The direction in which it stands is 'blazing', and that which it has left is considered 'charcoal-like'. / These three are remembered as inflamed; the other five are tranquil.
[Page 335]

230.s:
dīptāyāndiśi digdīptaṃ śakunaṃ parikīrtitaṃ /
grāmo 'raṇyā vane grāmyās tathā ninditapādapaḥ //
230.d:
दीप्तायान्दिशि दिग्दीप्तं शकुनं परिकीर्तितं /
ग्रामो ऽरण्या वने ग्राम्यास् तथा निन्दितपादपः //
230.m: An omen in an inflamed direction is proclaimed as directionally inflamed. / A wild creature in a village, village creatures in a forest, or an inauspicious tree,

230.s:
deśe caivāśubhe jñeyo deśadīpto dvijottamaḥ /
kriyādīpto vinirdiṣṭaḥ svajātyanucitakriyaḥ //
230.d:
देशे चैवाशुभे ज्ञेयो देशदीप्तो द्विजोत्तमः /
क्रियादीप्तो विनिर्दिष्टः स्वजात्यनुचितक्रियः //
230.m: And in an inauspicious place, O best of the twice-born, it should be known as spatially inflamed; / one performing an action unsuited to its own species is stated to be actionally inflamed;

230.s:
rutadīptaś ca kathito bhinnabhairavanisvanaḥ /
jātidīptas tathā jñeyaḥ kevalaṃ māṃsabhojanaḥ //
230.d:
रुतदीप्तश् च कथितो भिन्नभैरवनिस्वनः /
जातिदीप्तस् तथा ज्ञेयः केवलं मांसभोजनः //
230.m: One having a harsh and frightful sound is called vocally inflamed; / and one feeding exclusively on meat is to be known as specifically inflamed.

230.s:
dīptācchānto vinirdiṣṭaḥ sarvair bhedaiḥ prayatnataḥ /
miśrair miśro vinirdiṣṭastasya vācyaṃ phalāphalaṃ //
230.d:
दीप्ताच्छान्तो विनिर्दिष्टः सर्वैर् भेदैः प्रयत्नतः /
मिश्रैर् मिश्रो विनिर्दिष्टस्तस्य वाच्यं फलाफलं //
230.m: A tranquil [omen] is defined as opposite to an inflamed one by every category, with care; / by mixed categories it is stated to be mixed, and its good or bad fruit should be declared accordingly.

230.s:
gośvoṣṭragardabhaśvānaḥ sārikā gṛhagodhikā /
caṭakā bhāsakūrmādyāḥ kathitā grāmavāsinaḥ //
230.d:
गोश्वोष्ट्रगर्दभश्वानः सारिका गृहगोधिका /
चटका भासकूर्माद्याः कथिता ग्रामवासिनः //
230.m: Cows, horses, camels, donkeys, dogs, mynahs, house lizards, / sparrows, vultures, turtles, and the like are declared village-dwellers.

230.s:
ajāviśukanāgendrāḥ kolo mahiṣavāyasau /
grāmyāraṇyā vinirdiṣṭāḥ sarve 'nye vanagocarāḥ(1) //
230.d:
अजाविशुकनागेन्द्राः कोलो महिषवायसौ /
ग्राम्यारण्या विनिर्दिष्टाः सर्वे ऽन्ये वनगोचराः(1) //
230.m: Goats, sheep, parrots, noble elephants, boars, buffaloes, and crows / are designated as both village and forest dwellers; all others range in the forest.

230.s:
mārjārakukkuṭau grāmyau tau caiva vanagocarau /
tayorbhavati vijñānaṃ nityaṃ vai rūpabhedataḥ //
230.d:
मार्जारकुक्कुटौ ग्राम्यौ तौ चैव वनगोचरौ /
तयोर्भवति विज्ञानं नित्यं वै रूपभेदतः //
230.m: The cat and the rooster are domestic, and they also range in the forest; / the distinction between the two is always made by their difference in appearance.

230.s:
gokarṇaśikhicakrāhvakharahārītavāyasāḥ /
kulāhakukkubhaśyenapherukhañjanavānarāḥ //
230.d:
गोकर्णशिखिचक्राह्वखरहारीतवायसाः /
कुलाहकुक्कुभश्येनफेरुखञ्जनवानराः //
230.m: The gokarṇa antelope, peacock, ruddy shelduck, donkey, green pigeon, crow, / owl, coucal, hawk, jackal, wagtail, monkey,

230.s:
śataghnacaṭakaśyāmacāsaśyenakaliñjalāḥ /
tittiraḥ śatapatrañca kapotaś ca tathā trayaḥ //
230.d:
शतघ्नचटकश्यामचासश्येनकलिञ्जलाः /
तित्तिरः शतपत्रञ्च कपोतश् च तथा त्रयः //
230.m: Woodpecker, sparrow, Indian robin, blue jay, falcon, sparrow, / francolin, hoopoe, and the pigeon—these three—

230.s:
khañjarīṭakadātyūhaśukarājīvakukkuṭāḥ /
bhāradvājaś ca sāraṅga iti jñeyā divācarāḥ //
230.d:
खञ्जरीटकदात्यूहशुकराजीवकुक्कुटाः /
भारद्वाजश् च सारङ्ग इति ज्ञेया दिवाचराः //
230.m: Wagtail, water-hen, parrot, kingfisher, rooster, / skylark, and sāraṅga bird are to be known as diurnal creatures.

230.s:
vāguryulūkaśarabhakrauñcāḥ śaśakakacchapāḥ /
lomāsikāḥ piṅgalikāḥ kathitā rātrigocarāḥ //
:n
1 sarve 'nye ca vanecarā iti jha..
:p 336
230.d:
वागुर्युलूकशरभक्रौञ्चाः शशककच्छपाः /
लोमासिकाः पिङ्गलिकाः कथिता रात्रिगोचराः //
:न्
1 सर्वे ऽन्ये च वनेचरा इति झ..
:प् 336
230.m:
The bat, horned owl, śarabha, crane, hare, turtle, / fox, and spotted owlet are declared nocturnal creatures.
[...]
[Variant reading: 'and all others move in the forest' in manuscript jha. Page 336]

230.s:
haṃṣāś ca mṛgamārjāranakularkṣabhujaṅgamāḥ /
vṛkārisiṃhavyāghroṣṭragrāmaśūkaramānuṣāḥ //
230.d:
हंषाश् च मृगमार्जारनकुलर्क्षभुजङ्गमाः /
वृकारिसिंहव्याघ्रोष्ट्रग्रामशूकरमानुषाः //
230.m: Swans, deer, cats, mongooses, bears, serpents, / wolves, lions, tigers, camels, village boars, men,

230.s:
śvāvidvṛṣabhagomāyuvṛkakokilasārasāḥ /
turaṅgakaupīnanarā godhā hy ubhayacāriṇaḥ //
230.d:
श्वाविद्वृषभगोमायुवृककोकिलसारसाः /
तुरङ्गकौपीननरा गोधा ह्य् उभयचारिणः //
230.m: porcupines, bulls, jackals, wolves, cuckoos, cranes, / horses, men in loincloths, and monitors are land-and-water animals.

230.s:
balaprasthānayoḥ sarve purastātsaṅghacāriṇaḥ /
jayāvahā vinirdiṣṭāḥ paścānnidhanakāriṇaḥ //
230.d:
बलप्रस्थानयोः सर्वे पुरस्तात्सङ्घचारिणः /
जयावहा विनिर्दिष्टाः पश्चान्निधनकारिणः //
230.m: When an army marches, all of them moving together in a flock in front / are declared to bring victory; [if] behind, they cause destruction.

230.s:
gṛhādgamya yadā cāso vyāharet purutaḥ sthitaḥ /
nṛpāvamānaṃ vadati vāmaḥ kalahabhojane //
230.d:
गृहाद्गम्य यदा चासो व्याहरेत् पुरुतः स्थितः /
नृपावमानं वदति वामः कलहभोजने //
230.m: And when having left the house it cries while standing in front, / it indicates insult from the king; on the left, [it indicates] a meal in a quarrel.

230.s:
yāne taddarśanaṃ śastaṃ savyamaṅgasya vāpyatha /
caurair moṣamathākhyāti mayūro bhinnanisvanaḥ //
230.d:
याने तद्दर्शनं शस्तं सव्यमङ्गस्य वाप्यथ /
चौरैर् मोषमथाख्याति मयूरो भिन्ननिस्वनः //
230.m: Upon setting out, the sight of it is praised, or on the left side of the body. / Moreover, a peacock with a broken call announces theft by thieves.

230.s:
prayātasyāgrato rāma mṛgaḥ prāṇaharo bhavet /
ṛkṣākhujambukavyāghrasiṃhamārjāragardabhāḥ //
230.d:
प्रयातस्याग्रतो राम मृगः प्राणहरो भवेत् /
ऋक्षाखुजम्बुकव्याघ्रसिंहमार्जारगर्दभाः //
230.m: A deer in front of one who has set forth, O Rāma, takes away life. / Bears, mice, jackals, tigers, lions, cats, donkeys,

230.s:
pratilomās tathā rāma kharaś ca vikṛtrasvanaḥ /
vāmaḥ kapiñjalaḥ śreṣṭhas tathā dakṣiṇasaṃsthitaḥ //
230.d:
प्रतिलोमास् तथा राम खरश् च विकृत्रस्वनः /
वामः कपिञ्जलः श्रेष्ठस् तथा दक्षिणसंस्थितः //
230.m: going against the wind, O Rāma, and a donkey with an unnatural cry [bring evil]. / A francolin partridge on the left is best, and likewise situated on the right;

230.s:
pṛṣṭhato ninditaphalastittiristu na śasyate /
eṇā varāhāḥ pṛṣatā vāmā bhūtvā tu dakṣiṇāḥ //
230.d:
पृष्ठतो निन्दितफलस्तित्तिरिस्तु न शस्यते /
एणा वराहाः पृषता वामा भूत्वा तु दक्षिणाः //
230.m: behind, its fruit is censured; but a partridge is not commended. / Blackbucks, boars, and spotted deer, being on the left and then on the right,

230.s:
bhavantyarthakarā nityaṃ viparītā vigarhitāḥ /
vṛṣāśvajambukavyāghrāḥ siṃhamārjāragardabhāḥ(1) //
230.d:
भवन्त्यर्थकरा नित्यं विपरीता विगर्हिताः /
वृषाश्वजम्बुकव्याघ्राः सिंहमार्जारगर्दभाः(1) //
230.m: always bring wealth; reversed, they are censured. / Bulls, horses, jackals, tigers, lions, cats, donkeys,

230.s:
vāñchitārthakarā jñeyā dakṣiṇādvāmato gatāḥ /
śivā śyāmānanācchūcchūḥ piṅgalā gṛhagodhikā //
230.d:
वाञ्छितार्थकरा ज्ञेया दक्षिणाद्वामतो गताः /
शिवा श्यामाननाच्छूच्छूः पिङ्गला गृहगोधिका //
230.m: gone from the right to the left, are to be known as fulfilling desired aims. / A female jackal, a dark-faced chūcchū-bird, a screech-owl, a house lizard,

230.s:
śūkarī parapuṣṭā ca punnāmānaś ca vāmataḥ /
:n
1 pratilomāstathetyādiḥ, siṃhamārjāragardabhā ity antaḥ pāṭhaḥ
ja.. bha.. pustakadvaye nāsti
:p 337
strīsañjñā bhāsakārūṣakapiśrīkarṇaśchitkarāḥ //
230.d:
शूकरी परपुष्टा च पुन्नामानश् च वामतः /
:न्
1 प्रतिलोमास्तथेत्यादिः, सिंहमार्जारगर्दभा इत्य् अन्तः पाठः
ज.. भ.. पुस्तकद्वये नास्ति
:प् 337
स्त्रीसञ्ज्ञा भासकारूषकपिश्रीकर्णश्छित्कराः //
230.m:
a sow, a cuckoo, and [creatures] with masculine names, [are auspicious] on the left.
[...]
1. The reading beginning with "pratilomās tathā" and ending with "siṃhamārjāragardabhāḥ" is not found in the two manuscripts ja and bha. / [Page 337]
[Creatures] with feminine names, bhāsas, kārūṣas, monkeys, śrīkarṇas, [and birds that] make a screeching cry,

230.s:
kapiśrīkarṇapipyīkā(1) ruruśyenāś ca dakṣiṇāḥ /
jātīkṣāhiśaśakroḍagodhānāṃ kīrtanaṃ śubhaṃ //
230.d:
कपिश्रीकर्णपिप्यीका(1) रुरुश्येनाश् च दक्षिणाः /
जातीक्षाहिशशक्रोडगोधानां कीर्तनं शुभं //
230.m: monkeys, śrīkarṇas, pipyīkās, ruru deer, and falcons [are auspicious] on the right. / Mentioning a chameleon, a snake, a hare, a boar, or an iguana is auspicious;

230.s:
tataḥ sandarśanaṃ neṣṭaṃ pratīpaṃ vānararkṣayoḥ /
kāryakṛdbalī śakunaḥ prasthitasya hi yo 'nvahaṃ //
230.d:
ततः सन्दर्शनं नेष्टं प्रतीपं वानरर्क्षयोः /
कार्यकृद्बली शकुनः प्रस्थितस्य हि यो ऽन्वहं //
230.m: the sighting of them afterwards is not desired; [likewise] an monkey or a bear coming from the opposite direction. / An omen that is strong and effective for one who has departed every day,

230.s:
bhavettasya phalaṃ vācyaṃ tadeva divasaṃ budhaiḥ /
matā bhakṣyārthino bālā vairasaktāstathaiva ca //
230.d:
भवेत्तस्य फलं वाच्यं तदेव दिवसं बुधैः /
मता भक्ष्यार्थिनो बाला वैरसक्तास्तथैव च //
230.m: its fruit should be pronounced by the wise on that very day. / Those seeking food, young ones, and those engaged in enmity,

230.s:
sīmāntamabhyantaritā vijñeyā niṣphalā dvija /
ekadvitricaturbhistu śivā dhanyā rutair bhavet //
230.d:
सीमान्तमभ्यन्तरिता विज्ञेया निष्फला द्विज /
एकद्वित्रिचतुर्भिस्तु शिवा धन्या रुतैर् भवेत् //
230.m: and those separated by a boundary are to be known as fruitless, O twice-born. / By one, two, three, or four cries, a female jackal is auspicious;

230.s:
pañcabhiś ca tathā ṣaḍbhiradhanyā parikīrtitā /
saptabhiś ca tathā dhanyā niṣphalā parato bhavet //
230.d:
पञ्चभिश् च तथा षड्भिरधन्या परिकीर्तिता /
सप्तभिश् च तथा धन्या निष्फला परतो भवेत् //
230.m: by five and six cries, she is declared inauspicious; / by seven cries, she is likewise auspicious; beyond that, she becomes fruitless.

230.s:
nṛṇāṃ romāñcajananī vāhanānāṃ bhayapradā /
jvālānalā sūryamukhī vijñeyā bhayavardhanī //
230.d:
नृणां रोमाञ्चजननी वाहनानां भयप्रदा /
ज्वालानला सूर्यमुखी विज्ञेया भयवर्धनी //
230.m: Causing goosebumps to men and causing fear to conveyances, / flaming with fire, facing the sun, she is to be known as increasing fear.

230.s:
prathamaṃ sāraṅge dṛṣṭe śubhe deśe śubhaṃ vadet /
saṃvatsaraṃ manuṣyasya aśubhe ca śubhaṃ tathā //
230.d:
प्रथमं सारङ्गे दृष्टे शुभे देशे शुभं वदेत् /
संवत्सरं मनुष्यस्य अशुभे च शुभं तथा //
230.m: When a deer is first seen in an auspicious region, one should declare good fortune / for a man for a year; and [likewise] what is auspicious in an inauspicious [region].

230.s:
tathāvidhannaraḥ paśyetsāraṅgaṃ prathame 'hani /
ātmanaś ca tathātvena jñātavyaṃ vatsaraṃ phalaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe śakunāni nāma triṃśadadhikadviśatatamo
'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 punnāmāstathetyādiḥ, pippīkā ity antaḥ pāṭho 'smallabdheṣu
navapustakeṣu prāyaḥ samāna eva / teṣāmekatamasyāpi sāhāyyena
śodhituṃ na sa śakyate / abhidhānādiṣvapi tatratyaśabdo nopalabhyante /
atastatra viratiḥ
:p 338
:ś athaikatriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
śakunāni
230.d:
तथाविधन्नरः पश्येत्सारङ्गं प्रथमे ऽहनि /
आत्मनश् च तथात्वेन ज्ञातव्यं वत्सरं फलं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे शकुनानि नाम त्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो
ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 पुन्नामास्तथेत्यादिः, पिप्पीका इत्य् अन्तः पाठो ऽस्मल्लब्धेषु
नवपुस्तकेषु प्रायः समान एव / तेषामेकतमस्यापि साहाय्येन
शोधितुं न स शक्यते / अभिधानादिष्वपि तत्रत्यशब्दो नोपलभ्यन्ते /
अतस्तत्र विरतिः
:प् 338
:श् अथैकत्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
शकुनानि
230.m:
When a man sees a deer of such a kind on the first day, / the fruit of the year for himself is to be known accordingly.
Thus ends the two hundred and thirtieth chapter, named [Omens from] Birds, in the great Agni Purāṇa.
[...]
1. The passage beginning with "punnāmās tathā" and ending with "pippīkā" is largely identical across the nine manuscripts available to us. It cannot be emended even with the aid of any one of them; nor are the words found therein attested in dictionaries and the like. Therefore, we desist here. / [Page 338]
Now the two hundred and thirty-first chapter.
Omens from Birds
